questionEn: In which mountain cave overlooking Makkah did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ receive the very first revelation of the Qur'an?
optionsEn: Cave of Thawr
Cave of Al-Kahf
Cave of Hira
Cave of Uhud
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ was in spiritual retreat in Cave Hira on Jabal al-Noor when Angel Jibril came with the opening verses of Surah Al-'Alaq.

questionEn: How many verses of Surah Al-'Alaq were revealed in the very first encounter with Angel Jibril in Cave Hira?
optionsEn: The entire nineteen verses
The first five verses
The first three verses
The first seven verses
explanationEn: Angel Jibril taught the Prophet ﷺ the first five verses of Surah Al-'Alaq (96:1–5), beginning with 'Iqra' and ending with teaching humanity what it knew not.

questionEn: Which Surah was revealed after the temporary pause in revelation (Fatrat al-Wahy), commanding the Prophet ﷺ to rise and warn?
optionsEn: Surah Ash-Sharh
Surah Al-Muzzammil
Surah Al-Muddaththir
Surah Ad-Duha
explanationEn: Following the pause in revelation after Al-'Alaq, Angel Jibril appeared on a throne between heaven and earth, and the opening verses of Surah Al-Muddaththir (74:1–5) were revealed.

questionEn: Over approximately how many years was the Noble Qur'an revealed gradually to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: 10 years
30 years
23 years
13 years
explanationEn: The Qur'an was revealed in stages over roughly 23 years—13 years in Makkah and 10 years in Madinah—to strengthen the Prophet's heart and guide the community step by step.

questionEn: Which companion led the scholarly committee appointed by Caliph Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) to compile the first unified manuscript of the Qur'an?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA)
Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA)
Mu'adh ibn Jabal (RA)
Zayd ibn Thabit (RA)
explanationEn: Abu Bakr (RA), advised by Umar (RA) after many Qurra were martyred at Yamamah, entrusted Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) because he was young, wise, and one of the primary scribes of revelation.

questionEn: Which battle prompted Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) to urge Abu Bakr (RA) to compile the Qur'an into a single bound volume?
optionsEn: Battle of Mu'tah
Battle of al-Yamamah
Battle of Tabuk
Battle of Hunayn
explanationEn: After seventy or more memorizers (Qurra) were martyred in the Battle of al-Yamamah during the Riddah wars, Umar (RA) feared loss of the memorized text if not gathered into one Suhuf.

questionEn: With which Mother of the Believers were the compiled sheets (Suhuf) of the Qur'an safeguarded after the passing of Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)?
optionsEn: Zaynab bint Jahsh (RA)
Hafsah bint Umar (RA)
Umm Salamah (RA)
Aishah bint Abi Bakr (RA)
explanationEn: Abu Bakr's compiled sheets passed to Umar (RA) and then to his daughter Hafsah bint Umar (RA), from whom Uthman (RA) later borrowed them to produce the official copies.

questionEn: What standard condition did Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) require before accepting any written verse during Abu Bakr's compilation?
optionsEn: A seal from the tribe of Quraysh
Approval from every governor
Only one witness from the Ansar
Two witnesses confirming it was written in the Prophet's ﷺ presence
explanationEn: Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) and Umar (RA) verified each verse both by memorization and by two witnesses testifying that it had been written directly before the Prophet ﷺ.

questionEn: Which last verses of Surah At-Tawbah did Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) find in written form only with Abu Khuzaymah al-Ansari (RA), though known by memorization?
optionsEn: At-Tawbah 9:1–2
At-Tawbah 9:128–129
At-Tawbah 9:111–112
At-Tawbah 9:40–41
explanationEn: Zayd (RA) reported finding the final two verses of Surah At-Tawbah (9:128–129, 'Laqad ja'akum rasulun...') in written record only with Khuzaymah/Abu Khuzaymah al-Ansari (RA), whose testimony the Prophet ﷺ had counted equal to two.

questionEn: Which companion alerted Caliph Uthman ibn Affan (RA) to disputes in recitation among soldiers in Armenia and Azerbaijan, prompting standardized Mushaf copies?
optionsEn: Salman al-Farisi (RA)
Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA)
Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (RA)
Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA)
explanationEn: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (RA) saw Syrian and Iraqi troops arguing over dialectal variations and urged Uthman (RA) to unite the Ummah before they differed like earlier nations.

questionEn: During Uthman's (RA) standardization, in which dialect did he instruct the committee to write any word on which they differed?
optionsEn: The dialect of Tayy
The dialect of Quraysh
The dialect of Hawazin
The dialect of Hudhayl
explanationEn: Uthman (RA) instructed the three Qurayshi members—Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, Sa'id ibn al-'As, and Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Harith—to record any disputed spelling in the dialect of Quraysh, since the Qur'an was revealed in their tongue.

questionEn: According to Sahih Hadith, in how many Ahruf (modes/dialects) was the Qur'an revealed to ease recitation for diverse Arab tribes?
optionsEn: Seven Ahruf
Twelve Ahruf
Three Ahruf
Five Ahruf
explanationEn: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ taught that the Qur'an was revealed in seven Ahruf so that different tribes could recite with ease.

questionEn: Which companion memorized over seventy Surahs directly from the mouth of the Prophet ﷺ and was later praised in Hadith as one of four primary Qur'an teachers?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA)
Bilal ibn Rabah (RA)
Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA)
Talhah ibn Ubaydillah (RA)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ advised learning the Qur'an from four companions: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Salim Mawla Abi Hudhayfah, Mu'adh ibn Jabal, and Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA).

questionEn: Which Ansari companion did the Prophet ﷺ inform that Allah had commanded him to recite Surah Al-Bayyinah to him?
optionsEn: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA)
Anas ibn Malik (RA)
Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (RA)
Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA)
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ told Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA) that Allah had ordered him to recite 'Lam yakunilladhina kafaru' to him, Ubayy wept with awe upon hearing Allah had named him.

questionEn: How many times did Angel Jibril review the entire Qur'an with the Prophet ﷺ in the Ramadan immediately preceding the Prophet's ﷺ passing?
optionsEn: Three times
Twice
Seven times
Once
explanationEn: Angel Jibril reviewed the Qur'an with the Prophet ﷺ once every Ramadan, and twice in the final Ramadan of his life, which the Prophet ﷺ understood as a sign of his nearing departure.

questionEn: Which Surah's opening verses address the Prophet ﷺ when he feared forgetting the verses by moving his tongue hastily during revelation?
optionsEn: Surah Al-A'la
Surah Ash-Sharh
Surah Al-Qiyamah
Surah Al-Qalam
explanationEn: In Surah Al-Qiyamah (75:16–19), Allah assured the Prophet ﷺ: 'Move not your tongue therewith to hasten it; upon Us is its collection and its recitation.'

questionEn: Which verse did the Prophet ﷺ command the scribes to place immediately after Verse 2:278 when revealing the final verses of Al-Baqarah, and is widely held as one of the very last verses revealed?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:255
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:183
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:281
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:286
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated that Surah Al-Baqarah 2:281 ('And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah...') was the last verse revealed, shortly before the Prophet's ﷺ passing.

questionEn: Which companion's beautiful recitation of Surah Al-Baqarah caused angels to descend like a luminous cloud over his courtyard?
optionsEn: Suhaib al-Rumi (RA)
Abu Hurayrah (RA)
Usayd ibn Hudayr (RA)
Ammar ibn Yasir (RA)
explanationEn: As Usayd ibn Hudayr (RA) recited Surah Al-Baqarah at night while his horse startled, he saw a canopy of lights; the Prophet ﷺ explained they were angels listening to his recitation.

questionEn: Which companion was told by the Prophet ﷺ that his voice in Qur'an recitation sounded like 'one of the flutes (mazamir) of the family of Dawud'?
optionsEn: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA)
Mu'adh ibn Jabal (RA)
Zayd ibn Harithah (RA)
Abdullah ibn Umar (RA)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ overheard Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA) reciting melodiously at night and praised him with this tribute to his soulful voice.

questionEn: Which scholar introduced vowel markings (diacritical dots like fatha, kasra, damma initially as colored dots) to help non-Arab Muslims recite accurately?
optionsEn: Imam Malik
Hasan al-Basri
Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali
Al-Shafi'i
explanationEn: Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali pioneered early Arabic vowelization dots for the Mushaf during the Umayyad era, which Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad later refined into modern harakat.

questionEn: What is the primary scholarly definition of a 'Makki' Surah versus a 'Madani' Surah in Ulum al-Qur'an?
optionsEn: Based on whether it mentions Makkah or Madinah by name
Based on whether it was revealed before or after the Hijrah to Madinah
Based on whether it begins with disconnected letters
Based on whether it has more or fewer than 50 verses
explanationEn: According to the majority of scholars, Makki revelations occurred before the Hijrah (regardless of location), while Madani revelations occurred after the Hijrah.

questionEn: Which address appears exclusively in Makki Surahs (never in Madani Surahs) as a distinctive stylistic marker?
optionsEn: 'Qul' (Say)
'Kalla' (Nay / Never!)
'Ya Bani Isra'il' (O Children of Israel)
'Ya ayyuhalladhina amanu' (O you who believe)
explanationEn: The emphatic word 'Kalla' appears 33 times across 15 Surahs, all of them Makki, delivering a sharp rebuke to arrogance and heedlessness.

questionEn: Which major theme characterizes Madani Surahs compared to Makki Surahs?
optionsEn: Stories of Prophet Salih and Thamud only
Exclusive focus on the resurrection of bones
Detailed legislation, family law, governance, and relations with the People of the Book
Short poetic oaths by celestial bodies
explanationEn: While Makki Surahs anchor Tawhid, prophethood, and the Hereafter, Madani Surahs establish community laws, worship details, treaties, and civic justice.

questionEn: Which Makki Surah was revealed in Makkah during the Farewell Pilgrimage or Conquest era, yet is classified by the Hijrah standard as Madani because it came after the Hijrah?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Masad
Surah Al-Fil
Surah Quraysh
Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:3 (perfection of religion)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:3 ('Today I have perfected your religion for you...') was revealed on the Day of Arafah during the Farewell Pilgrimage, yet it is Madani because it followed the Hijrah.

questionEn: How are the 114 Surahs of the Mushaf ordered after Al-Fatihah?
optionsEn: Strict chronological order of revelation
Alphabetical order of Surah titles
Alternating Makki and Madani
Generally from longest to shortest by divine and prophetic arrangement
explanationEn: Except for Al-Fatihah at the opening and a few short placements, the Surahs are arranged broadly from longest (Al-Baqarah) to shortest (An-Nas) as taught by the Prophet ﷺ.

questionEn: What is the term for the 29 Surah openings composed of individual Arabic letters such as Alif-Lam-Mim or Ha-Mim?
optionsEn: Al-Huruf al-Muqatta'at
Al-Mathani
Al-Mu'awwidhat
Al-Mufassal
explanationEn: Al-Huruf al-Muqatta'at (disconnected letters) open 29 Surahs, symbolizing the miraculous inimitability of the Qur'an composed from the very letters of Arabic speech.

questionEn: Into how many Hizb sections is the Noble Qur'an divided, with two Hizbs forming each Juz'?
optionsEn: 30 Hizbs
90 Hizbs
60 Hizbs
120 Hizbs
explanationEn: Each of the 30 Juz' is split into 2 Hizbs, making 60 Hizbs in total, and each Hizb is further marked in quarters (rub') for steady daily reading.

questionEn: What is a 'Manzil' in traditional Qur'an recitation schedules?
optionsEn: One of seven roughly equal portions to complete the Qur'an in a week
A single Sajdah verse
One of twelve lunar-month portions
The final page of every Surah
explanationEn: Dividing the Qur'an into 7 Manzils allows a reader to complete a full Khatmah every seven days, a practice documented among early companions.

questionEn: Which Surah is known as the 'Heart of the Qur'an' in classic devotional literature and opens with the letters Ya-Sin?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Mulk
Surah Al-Waqi'ah
Surah Yasin
Surah Ar-Rahman
explanationEn: Surah Yasin (Chapter 36) is famously cherished in Islamic devotion for its vivid message on revelation, resurrection, and Allah's signs in creation.

questionEn: Which group of Surahs from Qaf (50) to An-Nas (114) is referred to in Hadith as 'Al-Mufassal' due to its frequent short Surah breaks?
optionsEn: Al-Mufassal
Al-Tiwal
Al-Mathani
Al-Mi'un
explanationEn: Al-Mufassal comprises the shorter Surahs toward the end of the Qur'an (commonly starting at Surah Qaf 50 or Al-Hujurat 49), distinguished by frequent Basmalah separators.

questionEn: How many prostration verses (Sajdah al-Tilawah) are found across the standard 15-prostration count in the Qur'an (with 14 agreed upon or 15 including Al-Hajj's second)?
optionsEn: 25 verses
14 or 15 verses
7 verses
10 verses
explanationEn: Scholars count 14 or 15 verses of Sajdah al-Tilawah depending on whether the second prostration in Surah Al-Hajj (22:77) is counted alongside 22:18.

questionEn: Which Surah uniquely contains TWO verses of Sajdah al-Tilawah in the Shafi'i and Hanbali count?
optionsEn: Surah Maryam
Surah Al-Baqarah
Surah Al-Hajj
Surah Al-A'raf
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hajj has two prostration verses (22:18 and 22:77), and 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir (RA) narrated a hadith noting its two prostrations.

questionEn: Which verse in Surah Al-A'raf (7:206) is the very first Sajdah al-Tilawah encountered when reading the Qur'an from the beginning?
explanationEn: The closing verse of Surah Al-A'raf (7:206), describing the angels who glorify Allah day and night and prostrate to Him, is the first Sajdah in Mushaf order.

questionEn: What is the last verse of Sajdah al-Tilawah in Mushaf order?
optionsEn: Surah As-Sajdah 32:15
Surah Al-'Alaq 96:19
Surah Al-Inshiqaq 84:21
Surah An-Najm 53:62
explanationEn: Surah Al-'Alaq concludes with 'No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near [to Allah]' (96:19), which is the final Sajdah al-Tilawah in the Mushaf.

questionEn: Which Surah was the FIRST in which the Prophet ﷺ performed Sajdah al-Tilawah publicly in Makkah, causing even the polytheists present to prostrate in awe?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Inshiqaq
Surah Sad
Surah Al-'Alaq
Surah An-Najm
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ recited Surah An-Najm in Makkah and prostrated at its final verse (53:62), every Muslim and polytheist present prostrated except one elder who lifted dirt to his forehead.

questionEn: Before beginning Qur'an recitation, what does Surah An-Nahl (16:98) command the believer to do?
optionsEn: Seek refuge in Allah from Satan the outcast (Isti'adhah)
Recite Surah Al-Ikhlas first
Stand upright
Face the Qiblah
explanationEn: Allah instructs: 'So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the expelled [from His mercy]'—i.e., saying A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim.

questionEn: What does Surah Al-Muzzammil (73:4) mean by commanding: 'Wa rattilil-Qur'ana tartila'?
optionsEn: Write the verses on parchment
Memorize only at midday
Recite the Qur'an swiftly in one breath
Recite the Qur'an with measured, clear, and deliberate rhythmic intonation
explanationEn: Tartil means reciting clearly, calmly, observing Tajweed rules and pausing to reflect upon the meanings of Allah's words.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-A'raf (7:204), what are believers commanded to do when the Qur'an is being recited aloud?
optionsEn: Listen attentively and remain silent so they may receive mercy
Repeat every word louder than the reciter
Engage in quiet conversation
Stand up immediately
explanationEn: Surah Al-A'raf 7:204 instructs: 'When the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and pay attention that you may receive mercy.'

questionEn: In a famous Sahih Hadith, what reward does the believer earn for reciting a SINGLE letter of the Book of Allah?
optionsEn: One good deed
Ten good deeds (one reward multiplied tenfold)
Three good deeds
Seventy good deeds
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever recites a letter of Allah's Book receives one hasanah, and each hasanah is multiplied tenfold—clarifying that Alif, Lam, Mim are three separate letters.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the person who struggles and stammers while trying to read the Qur'an diligently?
optionsEn: They should wait until fluent before reading
They must only listen to others
They receive half the reward
They receive a double reward—one for reciting and one for the effort
explanationEn: While the skilled reciter is with the noble angelic scribes, the one who recites with difficulty and perseverance earns two rewards.

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim, how did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ describe the Qur'an's role on the Day of Resurrection for those who recite it?
optionsEn: As a silent record
As an intercessor for its companions
As a replacement for Salah
As a witness only against scholars
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ urged: 'Recite the Qur'an, for it will come as an intercessor for its companions on the Day of Resurrection.'

questionEn: To what two fragrant things did the Prophet ﷺ compare a believer who recites the Qur'an?
optionsEn: A date palm—tall and shaded
A citron (Utrujjah)—sweet in scent and sweet in taste
Olive oil and honey
Musk and saffron
explanationEn: The believer who recites the Qur'an is like a citron (Utrujjah): pleasant in fragrance and delicious in flavor.

questionEn: What warning did the Prophet ﷺ give to someone whose heart holds nothing of the Qur'an at all?
optionsEn: It is like a ship without a sail
It is like a ruined, desolate house
It is like an unlit lantern
It is like a dry well
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ compared a heart empty of the Qur'an to a dilapidated, uninhabited house.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ advise Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-'As (RA) not to finish reciting the entire Qur'an in less than three days?
optionsEn: Because Makkah laws forbade it
Because one who finishes it in less than three days cannot grasp its deeper meaning
To leave time for fasting
To preserve vocal cords
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ emphasized comprehension over speed: 'He who recites the Qur'an in less than three days does not understand it.'

questionEn: Which two people did the Prophet ﷺ say are exclusively worthy of positive envy (Ghibtah—wishing to be blessed similarly)?
optionsEn: A king and a merchant
One given the Qur'an who recites it night and day, and one given wealth who spends it righteously night and day
A traveler and a builder
A poet and an archer
explanationEn: Healthy emulation (ghibtah) is praised only for the person dedicated to reciting and living the Qur'an day and night, and the generous donor spending sincerely in Allah's path.

questionEn: In Hadith, what is commanded to the companion of the Qur'an when entering Paradise?
optionsEn: 'Recite and ascend, and recite slowly as you did in the world, for your station is at the last verse you recite'
'Wait for the scholars'
'Count your pages'
'Sit at the threshold and rest'
explanationEn: Every verse memorized and lived elevates the believer's rank in Jannah until they reach the final verse they recite.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ urge memorizers to constantly review (ta'ahhadu) the Qur'an, comparing it to a hobbled camel?
optionsEn: Because camels carried the earliest manuscripts
Because recitation is best done while traveling
Because review replaces charity
Because it can escape from memory faster than a camel freed from its tether
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ warned that without steady revision, memorized verses slip away faster than a camel released from its rope.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Waqi'ah (56:79), what purity condition do the vast majority of jurists cite regarding touching the Arabic Mushaf?
optionsEn: Sitting on a prayer mat
Wearing white garments
Being in a state of ritual purity (Wudu / Taharah)
Fasting that day
explanationEn: Based on 56:79 ('None touch it except the purified') and the Prophet's ﷺ letter to Amr ibn Hazm ('No one should touch the Qur'an except one who is pure'), scholars require Wudu to touch the Mushaf.

questionEn: Which two 'bright ones' (Al-Zahrawan) did the Prophet ﷺ say will come on the Day of Judgment like two clouds or flocks of birds defending their reciter?
optionsEn: Surah Yasin and Surah Ar-Rahman
Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas
Surah Al-Baqarah and Surah Al Imran
Surah Al-Kahf and Surah Maryam
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ called Al-Baqarah and Al Imran 'Al-Zahrawan' (the Two Radiant Ones) and urged believers to recite them so they shade and plead for their reciter.

questionEn: How many verses constitute Surah Al-Fatihah, known in the Qur'an itself as 'Al-Sab' al-Mathani' (The Seven Oft-Repeated)?
optionsEn: 6 verses
7 verses
8 verses
5 verses
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hijr 15:87 refers to Surah Al-Fatihah as the Seven Oft-Repeated verses and the Great Qur'an.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Fatihah, which divine names appear together in the verse immediately following 'Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbil-'alamin'?
optionsEn: Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim
Al-Ghafur Al-Wadud
Al-Aziz Al-Hakim
Al-Malik Al-Quddus
explanationEn: Verses 2–3 praise Allah as Lord of all worlds, then immediately affirm His all-encompassing and special mercy: 'Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim.'

questionEn: Which attribute of Allah is highlighted in the fourth verse of Surah Al-Fatihah, 'Maliki Yawmid-Din'?
optionsEn: Knower of the unseen stars
Sovereign Master of the Day of Judgment
Creator of the heavens
Provider of rain
explanationEn: 'Maliki Yawmid-Din' reminds the believer every prayer that Allah alone holds absolute authority on the Day of Recompense.

questionEn: In the Hadith Qudsi about Surah Al-Fatihah, what happens when the worshipper recites 'Iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'in'?
optionsEn: The verse ends the prayer
Allah says: 'This is solely for Me'
Allah says: 'This is between Me and My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks'
The angels say Ameen first
explanationEn: Allah divided Al-Fatihah into halves: the first half is pure praise of Allah, the middle verse ('You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help') is shared between Allah and the servant, and the closing verses are the servant's supplication.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Fatihah (1:7), whose path do believers ask to be guided away from besides those who earned anger?
optionsEn: Those who traveled afar
Those who fell silent
Those who went astray (Ad-Dallin)
Those who built cities
explanationEn: The closing supplication seeks the Straight Path of the blessed, distinct from those who earned wrath (knowing truth yet rejecting it) and those astray (acting without sound guidance).

questionEn: Why did Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA) call Surah Al-Fatihah 'Al-Ruqyah' after reciting it over a stung tribal chief?
optionsEn: Because it mentions medicine
Because it was revealed in Madinah
Because Allah healed the chief through its recitation as a lawful spiritual cure
Because it is recited only in funerals
explanationEn: When Abu Sa'id (RA) recited Al-Fatihah as Ruqyah and the chief recovered, the Prophet ﷺ smiled and affirmed: 'How did you know it is a Ruqyah?'

questionEn: In the opening verses of Surah Al-Baqarah (2:2), for whom is 'this Book, in which there is no doubt' specifically described as guidance?
optionsEn: Al-Muttaqin (the God-conscious / mindful)
Only scholars of law
Only kings
Only travelers
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:2 declares the Qur'an to be 'Hudan lil-muttaqin'—a guidance for those conscious of Allah, who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend from what He provided.

questionEn: From which event in the story of the Children of Israel does Surah Al-Baqarah ('The Cow') take its name?
optionsEn: Livestock brought to Makkah
Allah's command to slaughter a specific cow to expose a hidden murder
The cows in Yusuf's dream
The golden calf of Samiri
explanationEn: Verses 2:67–73 recount how Allah ordered Banu Isra'il to sacrifice a cow and strike the slain man with part of it so he revived briefly and named his killer.

questionEn: Which two angels in Babylon are mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:102) as a test warning people not to fall into disbelief through sorcery?
optionsEn: Harut and Marut
Munkar and Nakir
Raqib and Atid
Jibril and Mikail
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:102 states that Harut and Marut explicitly warned anyone approaching them: 'We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:125), what exact spot beside the Kaaba did Allah command believers to take as a place of prayer?
optionsEn: Mount Hira
Maqam Ibrahim (Station of Ibrahim)
Bab al-Fath
The Well of Zamzam
explanationEn: Allah commanded: 'And take, [O believers], from the standing place of Ibrahim a place of prayer,' which pilgrims follow after Tawaf.

questionEn: For how many months after the Hijrah did Muslims pray toward Jerusalem before Allah revealed the verses changing the Qiblah to the Kaaba in Surah Al-Baqarah?
optionsEn: 36 months
16 to 17 months
6 to 7 months
3 months
explanationEn: Al-Bara ibn 'Azib (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis for 16 or 17 months until 2:144 turned the Qiblah toward Al-Masjid al-Haram.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:143), by turning the Qiblah, what title does Allah bestow upon the Muslim Ummah?
optionsEn: Ummatan Wasatan (a justly balanced community)
Ummatan Qadimah
Ummatan Ghaniyyah
Ummatan Sabirah
explanationEn: 'And thus We have made you a justly balanced community (Ummatan Wasatan) that you will be witnesses over the people.'

questionEn: What concise verse in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:152) promises reciprocal closeness when the believer remembers Allah?
optionsEn: 'Travel and reflect'
'Give charity and I will double it'
'Remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me'
'Fast and be purified'
explanationEn: Verse 2:152 ('Fadhkuruni adhkurkum...') is one of the most uplifting reminders for Dhikr during daily life and pilgrimage.

questionEn: Which timeless phrase of comfort during loss and calamity is taught in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:156)?
optionsEn: Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal-wakil
La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
Subhanallahi wa bihamdihi
Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un
explanationEn: 'Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we shall return' (2:156) brings Allah's blessings, mercy, and guidance to the patient.

questionEn: Why did Allah reassure the companions in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:158) that there is no blame in walking between Safa and Marwah?
optionsEn: Because Sa'i was optional in winter
Because some Ansari companions hesitated due to pre-Islamic idols once placed near those hills
Because the hills were far from Madinah
Because rain flooded the valley
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) explained to Urwah that some Ansar feared sin because of idols associated with Safa and Marwah before Islam, so 2:158 affirmed them as symbols of Allah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:183), what primary spiritual objective is stated for prescribing fasting during Ramadan?
optionsEn: Physical endurance
Attaining Taqwa (God-consciousness)
Saving provisions
Counting lunar phases
explanationEn: 'O you who believe, fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, that you may attain Taqwa.'

questionEn: Where in the Qur'an does Allah place the famous verse of closeness and answered prayer: 'When My servants ask you about Me—indeed I am near'?
optionsEn: In Surah Al-Kawthar
At the end of Surah Yusuf
In the middle of the verses on Ramadan and fasting (Al-Baqarah 2:186)
In Surah Al-Kafirun
explanationEn: Placed directly amid the Ramadan verses (2:183–187), verse 2:186 assures every fasting and supplicating believer that Allah answers directly without an intermediary.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Baqarah (2:189), what purpose do the crescent moons (Al-Ahillah) serve for humanity?
optionsEn: Marking fixed times for people and for the Hajj pilgrimage
Predicting rainfall
Decorating desert camps
Measuring mountain heights
explanationEn: When companions asked about the waxing and waning moon, 2:189 answered that crescents serve as clear timekeepers for worship, daily affairs, and the Hajj season.

questionEn: Which three practices does Surah Al-Baqarah (2:197) specifically forbid once a pilgrim has entered the state of Hajj (and Ihram)?
optionsEn: Walking, speaking, and trading
Praying outdoors, fasting, and giving charity
Sexual relations (rafath), sinful conduct (fusuq), and quarreling (jidal)
Sleeping, eating dates, and drinking Zamzam
explanationEn: 'Whoever intends Hajj therein, there is to be no sexual relations, no wickedness, and no quarreling during Hajj.'

questionEn: From which plain does Surah Al-Baqarah (2:198) instruct pilgrims to depart while remembering Allah at Al-Mash'ar al-Haram (Muzdalifah)?
optionsEn: Hunayn
Mount Uhud
Arafat
Badr
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:198 states: 'When you depart from Arafat, remember Allah at Al-Mash'ar al-Haram,' anchoring the sequence of Hajj stations.

questionEn: Which comprehensive dua immediately follows the Hajj verses in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:201) and was the Prophet's ﷺ most frequent supplication?
optionsEn: Rabbi zidni 'ilma
Rabbana la tu'akhidhna
Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhaban-nar
Rabbana zalamna anfusana
explanationEn: Anas (RA) reported that the Prophet ﷺ most frequently prayed: 'Our Lord, grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'

questionEn: How many days of staying in Mina to remember Allah are mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:203), allowing either two days or three without sin?
optionsEn: Seven days
Ten days
The numbered days (Ayyam Ma'dudat—Days of Tashriq)
Forty days
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:203 refers to the Days of Tashriq (11–13 Dhul-Hijjah): whoever hastens in two days commits no sin, and whoever stays the third commits no sin, if mindful of Allah.

questionEn: In Ayat al-Kursi (Al-Baqarah 2:255), which two eternal names open the verse declaring Allah's self-subsisting life?
optionsEn: Al-Sami' Al-Basir
Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum
Al-Awwal Al-Akhir
Al-Khaliq Al-Bari'
explanationEn: 'Allah—there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living (Al-Hayy), the Sustainer of all existence (Al-Qayyum).'

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ promise to whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi right after every obligatory prayer?
optionsEn: Exemption from fasting
Travel to Makkah that year
Wealth within a week
Nothing stands between them and entering Paradise except death
explanationEn: Abu Umamah (RA) narrated that whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi after every obligatory prayer will have nothing preventing them from Jannah except death.

questionEn: Which is the longest SINGLE verse in the entire Noble Qur'an, occupying a full page in standard Mushafs?
optionsEn: Ayat al-Nur (24:35)
Ayat al-Kursi (2:255)
Ayat al-Wudu (5:6)
Ayat al-Dayn / Verse of Debt (2:282)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:282 (Ayat al-Dayn) details the writing and witnessing of financial contracts and debts to uphold justice and prevent disputes.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ promise regarding reciting the LAST TWO verses of Surah Al-Baqarah (2:285–286) at night?
optionsEn: They double the length of Fajr
They replace Tahajjud
They suffice the believer as protection and spiritual blessing
They must be written on parchment
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever recites the last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him.'

questionEn: Which Surah is Chapter 3 of the Qur'an, named after the pious family of Maryam's father?
optionsEn: Surah Al-An'am
Surah Al Imran
Surah Maryam
Surah An-Nisa
explanationEn: Surah Al Imran (Chapter 3) opens with Tawhid, explains clear vs allegorical verses, recounts the birth of Maryam and Isa (AS), and draws lessons from the Battle of Uhud.

questionEn: Which Surah states in 3:96 that the very FIRST House of worship established for humanity is the one at Bakkah (Makkah)?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Hajj
Surah Al Imran
Surah Quraysh
Surah Al-Baqarah
explanationEn: Surah Al Imran 3:96–97 affirms that the House at Bakkah was the first sanctuary established for mankind, containing clear signs including Maqam Ibrahim, and obligates Hajj upon those able.

questionEn: According to Surah Al Imran (3:92), when will a believer never truly attain righteousness (Al-Birr)?
optionsEn: Until they spend from what they love
Until they memorize ten Surahs
Until they fast half the year
Until they climb Mount Safa
explanationEn: 'Never will you attain righteousness until you spend [in the way of Allah] from that which you love.' Upon hearing this, Abu Talhah (RA) donated his prized garden Bayruha'.

questionEn: In Surah Al Imran (3:103), what are believers commanded to hold fast to altogether while avoiding division?
optionsEn: The walls of Madinah
The Rope of Allah (Hablullah)
Gold reserves
Tribal alliances
explanationEn: 'And hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided'—referring to the Qur'an and Allah's covenant.

questionEn: What triumphant phrase did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) say in the fire and the companions say after Uhud, recorded in Surah Al Imran (3:173)?
optionsEn: Subhanallahi al-'Azim
Allahu Akbar Kabira
Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal-wakil
Alhamdulillahi Rabbil-'alamin
explanationEn: When warned of enemy armies gathering against them, the believers' faith increased and they declared: 'Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.'

questionEn: Which closing verses of Surah Al Imran (3:190–200) did the Prophet ﷺ weep over and recite upon waking for Tahajjud?
optionsEn: 3:190–200 (the creation of heavens and earth and the alternation of night and day)
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) observed the Prophet ﷺ wake at night, look to the sky, and recite 3:190 onward, describing 'Woe to whoever recites these and does not reflect upon them.'

questionEn: Which verse in Surah An-Nisa caused Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to weep when Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) recited it up to 'How will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and bring you as a witness over these?'
optionsEn: An-Nisa 4:58
An-Nisa 4:41
An-Nisa 4:103
An-Nisa 4:1
explanationEn: When Ibn Mas'ud (RA) reached An-Nisa 4:41, the Prophet ﷺ said 'Enough for now!' and Ibn Mas'ud saw tears streaming down his face.

questionEn: In Surah An-Nisa (4:58), what two core civic duties does Allah command rulers and citizens alike to uphold?
optionsEn: Collecting taxes at night
Building bridges and digging wells
Returning trusts (amanat) to their rightful owners and judging with justice
Traveling every spring
explanationEn: 'Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due and when you judge between people to judge with justice.'

questionEn: Which verse in Surah An-Nisa (4:86) teaches the etiquette of returning greetings?
optionsEn: Greet only elders
Greet back with a greeting even better than it, or at least return the like of it
Respond with silence
Greet only inside mosques
explanationEn: Surah An-Nisa 4:86 encourages generosity in peace: 'When you are greeted with a greeting, greet [in return] with one better than it or [at least] return it.'

questionEn: Which Surah An-Nisa verse (4:103) reminds believers that prayer has been prescribed upon them at fixed appointed times?
explanationEn: 'Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times (Kitaban mawquta).'

questionEn: In Surah An-Nisa (4:135), even against whom must a believer stand firmly for justice as a witness for Allah?
optionsEn: Only enemies in battle
Only strangers
Only merchants
Even against oneself, parents, and close relatives
explanationEn: Surah An-Nisa 4:135 sets the gold standard of impartiality: stand firmly in justice even if testimony goes against yourself, your parents, or your kin.

questionEn: Which Surah opens with 'O you who believe, fulfill all contracts ('Uqud)' and contains the verse perfecting the religion of Islam?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Anfal
Surah At-Tawbah
Surah Al-A'raf
Surah Al-Ma'idah
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ma'idah (Chapter 5, 'The Table Spread') opens with honoring covenants and contains 5:3, revealed at Arafah during the Farewell Pilgrimage.

questionEn: Which verse of Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:2) sets the Islamic ethic for teamwork and community service?
optionsEn: Cooperate in righteousness and Taqwa, and do not cooperate in sin and aggression
Compete only in trade
Avoid neighbors
Keep silent in public assemblies
explanationEn: 'Wa ta'awanu 'alal-birri wat-taqwa wa la ta'awanu 'alal-ithmi wal-'udwan' is a foundational Qur'anic rule for collective good.

questionEn: Which ritual obligation's four core steps (washing face, arms to elbows, wiping head, washing feet to ankles) are detailed explicitly in Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:6)?
optionsEn: Tawaf
Wudu (ablution) and Tayammum
Aqiqah
Zakat al-Fitr
explanationEn: Verse 5:6 (Ayat al-Wudu) outlines the obligatory limbs of Wudu as well as Ghusl and dry ablution (Tayammum) when water is unavailable or harmful.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:32), saving a single innocent human life is equated in moral magnitude to what?
optionsEn: Saving all of humanity
Praying for a hundred nights
Giving a mountain of silver
Building a city
explanationEn: Immediately following the story of Adam's two sons, 5:32 declares that whoever saves one life, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely.

questionEn: What hunting restriction while in the state of Ihram is explicitly stated in Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:95–96)?
optionsEn: Fishing in the sea is forbidden
Eating dates is forbidden
Cooking bread is forbidden
Hunting land game is forbidden in Ihram, whereas seafood is lawful
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:95–96 forbids killing land game while in Ihram (with sacrificial compensation if violated), while expressly permitting catch from the sea.

questionEn: Why is Surah Al-Ma'idah named 'The Table Spread'?
optionsEn: After a feast in Madinah
After Ibrahim's hospitality to the angels
After Yusuf's royal banquet
After the disciples of Isa (AS) requested a table spread with food sent down from heaven
explanationEn: Verses 5:112–115 recount the Hawariyyun (disciples) asking Isa (AS) to supplicate Allah for a Ma'idah from heaven to satisfy their hearts and serve as a recurring sign.

questionEn: Which major Makki Surah (Chapter 6) was revealed largely at one time escorted by seventy thousand angels according to narrations?
optionsEn: Surah Al-An'am
Surah Al-Ma'idah
Surah At-Tawbah
Surah Al-Anfal
explanationEn: Surah Al-An'am ('The Cattle', Chapter 6) was revealed in Makkah mostly in a single revelation, hammering home pure Tawhid and refuting pre-Islamic livestock superstitions.

questionEn: In Surah Al-An'am (6:59), what does Allah say about a single leaf that falls from a tree?
optionsEn: Only wind knows its path
It vanishes unseen
Not a leaf falls except that He knows it
Angels record it monthly
explanationEn: 'With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. He knows what is on land and in the sea; not a leaf falls except that He knows it.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-An'am (6:160), how does Allah contrast the reward of a good deed versus the recompense of an evil deed?
optionsEn: Both are multiplied sevenfold
Equal one-for-one in both cases
A good deed is multiplied tenfold, while an evil deed is repaid only with its like
Good deeds double; evil deeds triple
explanationEn: 'Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times the like thereof, and whoever comes with an evil deed will not be recompensed except the like thereof.'

questionEn: Which closing declaration of total devotion in Surah Al-An'am (6:162) is often recited in the opening prayer (Du'a al-Istiftah)?
optionsEn: Qul huwa Allahu ahad
Subhana Rabbika
Qul inna salati wa nusuki wa mahyaya wa mamati lillahi Rabbil-'alamin
Rabbana taqabbal minna
explanationEn: 'Say: Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-A'raf (Chapter 7), what does 'Al-A'raf' refer to?
optionsEn: A valley near Ta'if
The highest heavens
The elevated barrier/heights between Paradise and Hellfire where people of equal good and bad deeds await Allah's mercy
The gate of Makkah
explanationEn: Surah Al-A'raf (7:46–49) describes the companions of the Heights looking upon the dwellers of Paradise and Hellfire while hoping for Allah's mercy.

questionEn: What primordial covenant (Alastu bi-Rabbikum) did Allah take from all descendants of Adam in Surah Al-A'raf (7:172)?
optionsEn: To speak one language
To build temples
To fast on Mondays
To testify 'Am I not your Lord?' and they replied 'Yes, we testify'
explanationEn: Surah Al-A'raf 7:172 reminds humanity of our innate spiritual testimony (Fitrah) acknowledging Allah as our sole Lord.

questionEn: In Surah Al-A'raf (7:180), how are believers told to call upon Allah in their Duas?
optionsEn: Only in silent whispers
Only through poetry
Only at midnight
By His Most Beautiful Names (Al-Asma al-Husna)
explanationEn: 'And to Allah belong the best names, so invoke Him by them'—guiding every believer to align their Dua with Allah's names like Al-Ghafur, Ar-Razzaq, and Ash-Shafi.

questionEn: Which three gentle commands of prophetic wisdom appear together in Surah Al-A'raf (7:199)?
optionsEn: Hold to forgiveness, enjoin what is good ('Urf), and turn away from the ignorant
Wait, listen, and write
Travel, trade, and teach
Fast, pray, and build
explanationEn: 'Khudhil-'afwa wa'mur bil-'urfi wa a'rid 'anil-jahilin'—Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA) called this verse the core of noble character in the Qur'an.

questionEn: After which decisive 2 AH battle was Surah Al-Anfal (Chapter 8) revealed, teaching etiquette around spoils and reliance on Allah?
optionsEn: Battle of Badr
Battle of Khaybar
Battle of the Trench
Battle of Uhud
explanationEn: Surah Al-Anfal addresses the aftermath of Badr, reminding believers that victory came from Allah's angelic support and obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Anfal (8:2), what happens to true believers' hearts when Allah is mentioned?
optionsEn: They feel fear-awe (wajilat qulubuhum), and when His verses are recited, their faith increases
They argue immediately
They fall asleep
They remain unaffected
explanationEn: Verse 8:2 defines true believers by three inner traits: awe at Allah's mention, growth in Iman upon hearing the Qur'an, and complete reliance (Tawakkul) on their Lord.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anfal (8:33), what two shields prevented immediate collective punishment from descending upon Makkah?
optionsEn: The presence of the Prophet ﷺ among them and their seeking forgiveness (Istighfar)
Desert storms
High walls and deep wells
Trade caravans and treaties
explanationEn: 'Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.'

questionEn: Why do scholars say Surah At-Tawbah (Chapter 9) begins without 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim'?
optionsEn: Because it is the shortest Surah
Because it is Makki
Because Bismillah is a declaration of peace and mercy, while At-Tawbah opens with an ultimatum dissolving violated treaties (and it was treated as a unit with Al-Anfal or left as revealed)
A scribe forgot it
explanationEn: Uthman (RA) and classical commentators noted it was revealed without Basmalah due to its severe opening declaration of disavowal from treaty-breakers.

questionEn: In Surah At-Tawbah (9:60), how many eligible categories of recipients are specified for obligatory Zakat?
optionsEn: Six categories
Ten categories
Eight categories
Four categories
explanationEn: Verse 9:60 lists eight exact categories: the poor, the needy, Zakat administrators, reconciling hearts, freeing captives, those in debt, in Allah's cause, and the stranded traveler.

questionEn: Which event during the Hijrah is immortalized in Surah At-Tawbah (9:40) with the words 'Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us'?
optionsEn: Entering Quba
The Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr (RA) sheltering inside the Cave of Thawr
Crossing the Red Sea
The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
explanationEn: When pursuers stood near Cave Thawr, the Prophet ﷺ comforted Abu Bakr (RA) with 'La tahzan innallaha ma'ana,' and Allah sent down tranquility upon him.

questionEn: In Surah At-Tawbah (9:18), who are the rightful maintainers of the mosques of Allah?
optionsEn: Only tribal leaders
Wealthy builders regardless of faith
Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish prayer, give Zakat, and fear none except Allah
Only residents of Makkah
explanationEn: Verse 9:18 emphasizes that maintaining Allah's houses is both spiritual and practical, belonging to faithful worshippers who fear Allah alone.

questionEn: Which three companions remained behind from the Tabuk expedition and had their sincere fifty-day repentance accepted in Surah At-Tawbah (9:118)?
optionsEn: Ka'b ibn Malik, Murarah ibn al-Rabi', and Hilal ibn Umayyah (RA)
Talhah, Zubayr, and Sa'd (RA)
Abu Dharr, Miqdad, and Suhaib (RA)
Bilal, Ammar, and Salman (RA)
explanationEn: Their truthful confession—without fabricating excuses—led to intense soul-searching until Allah revealed 9:117–119 accepting their Tawbah and urging believers to be with the truthful.

questionEn: In Surah Yunus (10:57), what four uplifting qualities describe the Qur'an itself?
optionsEn: Victory, tribute, trade, and travel
History, astronomy, poetry, and law
Wealth, power, speed, and song
An admonition, a healing for what is in the breasts, guidance, and mercy for the believers
explanationEn: 'O mankind, there has come to you instruction from your Lord and healing for what is in the breasts and guidance and mercy for the believers.'

questionEn: Which Surah's opening verses (11:1) describe the Qur'an's verses as 'uhkimat' (perfected) and 'fussilat' (explained in detail) from One Wise and All-Aware, and was among the Surahs that turned the Prophet's ﷺ hair gray from its weighty warnings?
optionsEn: Surah Hud
Surah Yusuf
Surah Ar-Ra'd
Surah Ibrahim
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told Abu Bakr (RA): 'Hud and its sisters have turned my hair gray' due to its vivid accounts of past nations and the command 'Stand firm as you have been commanded' (11:112).

questionEn: Which Surah (Chapter 12) is uniquely dedicated almost from beginning to end to a single continuous story called 'Ahsan al-Qasas' (the best of stories)?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Kahf
Surah Ibrahim
Surah Yunus
Surah Yusuf
explanationEn: Surah Yusuf (12:3) introduces itself as 'the best of stories,' narrating Prophet Yusuf's (AS) journey from the well and slavery to forgiveness and leadership in Egypt.

questionEn: In Surah Yusuf (12:2), why did Allah emphasize that He sent down the Qur'an as an 'Arabic Qur'an'?
optionsEn: So only poets could memorize it
So only merchants could trade with it
So it would never be translated
So that people may understand and reflect with reason
explanationEn: 'Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you might understand' highlights clarity, precision, and comprehension.

questionEn: What does Surah Yusuf (12:53) teach about the human soul (al-nafs al-ammarah bis-su') unless guarded by Allah's mercy?
optionsEn: It is naturally inclined to command evil unless my Lord bestows mercy
It controls the weather
It remembers everything instantly
It never desires anything
explanationEn: Verse 12:53 teaches humility and vigilance over the inner self: 'Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those upon which my Lord has mercy.'

questionEn: Which famous verse of hope in Surah Yusuf (12:87) forbids believers from despairing of Allah's comforting mercy?
optionsEn: 'Never despair of the relief/mercy of Allah; indeed none despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people'
'Travel the earth and see'
'Give from your harvest'
'Keep your promises'
explanationEn: Prophet Ya'qub (AS) urged his sons to search for Yusuf and his brother without losing hope, reminding them never to despair of Allah's relief (Rawh Allah).

questionEn: In Surah Ar-Ra'd (Chapter 13, 'The Thunder'), what phenomenon glorifies Allah with His praise out of awe?
optionsEn: Only desert winds
Only mountain peaks
The thunder (Al-Ra'd) and the angels alike
Only ocean waves
explanationEn: Surah Ar-Ra'd 13:13 declares: 'And the thunder exalts [Allah] with praise of Him—and the angels [as well] from fear of Him.'

questionEn: According to Surah Ar-Ra'd (13:11), when does Allah change the condition of a people?
optionsEn: Only when rivers dry up
Every hundred years automatically
Not until they change what is within themselves
Only during solar eclipses
explanationEn: 'Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves'—a foundational principle of personal and collective renewal.

questionEn: In Surah Ar-Ra'd (13:28), what alone brings true tranquility and peace to human hearts?
optionsEn: High stone fortresses
The remembrance of Allah (Dhikr Allah)
Long journeys
Abundant silver
explanationEn: 'Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured (tatma'innul-qulub).'

questionEn: In Surah Ibrahim (14:7), what promise did Allah make to those who show gratitude (Shukr) for His blessings?
optionsEn: He will test them with drought
He will reduce their days
He will surely increase them ('La-azidannakum')
He will hide their deeds
explanationEn: 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed My punishment is severe.'

questionEn: How does Surah Ibrahim (14:24–25) describe a good word (Kalimah Tayyibah, such as the testimony of faith)?
optionsEn: Like a fleeting cloud
Like sand in the wind
Like a dry reed
Like a good tree whose root is firmly fixed and whose branches reach the sky, yielding fruit in every season
explanationEn: The parable in 14:24–25 contrasts a good word—deeply rooted and eternally fruitful—with an evil word uprooted from the earth with no stability.

questionEn: In Surah Ibrahim (14:37), why did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) settle part of his family in the barren valley beside the Sacred House?
optionsEn: To build ships
To escape winter floods
So that they may establish prayer ('li-yuqimus-salah') and hearts of people incline toward them
For mining gold
explanationEn: Ibrahim (AS) prayed in 14:37: 'Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer...'

questionEn: Which direct divine guarantee regarding the preservation of the Qur'an appears in Surah Al-Hijr (15:9)?
optionsEn: 'It will last for three centuries'
'Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder (Dhikr), and indeed We will be its Guardian'
'Only scholars in Madinah will keep it'
'Write it on gold plates'
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hijr 15:9 guarantees that Allah Himself preserves the Qur'an from alteration, addition, or loss across all generations.

questionEn: What historical region gives Surah Al-Hijr (Chapter 15) its name?
optionsEn: A fortress near Jerusalem
A mountain in Yemen
The rocky valley in northwestern Arabia inhabited by the people of Thamud
An island in the Red Sea
explanationEn: Al-Hijr (Mada'in Salih) was the stone-carved habitat of the Companions of Al-Hijr (Thamud), mentioned in 15:80–84.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hijr (15:99), until what moment is the believer commanded to worship their Lord?
optionsEn: Until reaching forty years
Until the end of Ramadan
Until certainty (Al-Yaqin, meaning death) comes to you
Until completing one Hajj
explanationEn: 'Wa'bud Rabbaka hatta ya'tiyakal-yaqin'—Scholars agree 'al-yaqin' here refers to death, meaning devotion never retires in this life.

questionEn: Why is Surah An-Nahl (Chapter 16) also affectionately called 'Surah al-Ni'am' (The Surah of Blessings) by scholars?
optionsEn: Because it lists only laws of war
Because it extensively enumerates Allah's blessings in rain, livestock, honey, oceans, shade, and family
Because it mentions no prophets
Because it is the shortest Makki Surah
explanationEn: Surah An-Nahl ('The Bee') catalogs countless earthly and spiritual mercies, reminding us: 'If you tried to count Allah's favors, you could never enumerate them' (16:18).

questionEn: In Surah An-Nahl (16:68–69), what remarkable substance produced by the bee is explicitly described as containing 'healing for people'?
optionsEn: Tree resin
Morning dew
Wax alone
A drink of varying colors (honey)
explanationEn: Allah inspired the bee to build hives in mountains, trees, and trellises, producing honey of varying hues 'in which there is healing for mankind.'

questionEn: According to Surah An-Nahl (16:90), which three moral pillars is Allah always commanding (often recited at the end of Friday Khutbahs)?
optionsEn: Justice ('Adl), excellence/benevolence (Ihsan), and giving to relatives
Silence, fasting, and solitude
Poetry, debate, and architecture
Trade, travel, and diplomacy
explanationEn: Verse 16:90 commands justice, excellence (Ihsan), and generosity to kin, while forbidding immorality, wrongdoing, and oppression—Ibn Mas'ud called it the most comprehensive ethical verse.

questionEn: In Surah An-Nahl (16:125), with what three qualities must callers invite others to the path of their Lord?
optionsEn: Strictness alone
Force, haste, and debate
Wisdom (Hikmah), goodly instruction (Maw'izah Hasanah), and arguing in the best manner
Wealth, rank, and silence
explanationEn: 'Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best.'

questionEn: Which two sacred mosques are linked in the opening verse of Surah Al-Isra (17:1) describing the Night Journey?
optionsEn: Al-Masjid al-Nabawi and Masjid Quba
Masjid Qiblatayn and Masjid al-Ghamamah
Masjid al-Khaif and Masjid Namirah
Al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah and Al-Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem
explanationEn: Surah Al-Isra 17:1 opens with 'Subhanalladhi asra bi-'abdihi laylan minal-Masjidil-Haram ilal-Masjidil-Aqsa...'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:9), to what does Allah say 'Indeed, this Qur'an guides'?
optionsEn: To earthly kingdoms
To seasonal calendars
To that which is most upright / straightest (Aqrab/Aqwam)
Only to ancient customs
explanationEn: 'Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable/upright (allati hiya aqwam) and gives glad tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:23), what exact expression of annoyance are children forbidden to utter even in mild frustration toward aging parents?
optionsEn: 'No thank you'
'Uff' (even a slight sigh of exasperation)
'Tomorrow'
'Wait'
explanationEn: Alongside worshipping Allah alone, 17:23 commands utmost kindness to parents: 'Do not say to them [so much as] "Uff," and do not repel them, but speak to them a noble word.'

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Isra (17:44), what do the seven heavens, the earth, and everything within them continuously do?
optionsEn: Sleep at midnight
Exalt Allah's glory (Yusabbihu), though humans do not understand their glorification
Orbit silently without praise
Wait for winter
explanationEn: 'The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them exalt Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts Him by His praise, but you do not understand their [way of] exalting.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:78), which prayer is famously highlighted by the phrase 'Inna Qur'anal-Fajri kana mashhuda' (witnessed by the angels of night and day)?
optionsEn: Fajr prayer (recitation at dawn)
Isha prayer
Asr prayer
Zuhr prayer
explanationEn: At the dawn recitation of Fajr, the angels of the night and the angels of the day gather together to witness the believer's prayer.

questionEn: What spiritual property of the Qur'an does Surah Al-Isra (17:82) affirm for the believers?
optionsEn: It is a hidden riddle
It is a healing and a mercy (Shifa'un wa Rahmah)
It is only a legal code
It is a seasonal song
explanationEn: 'And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers, and it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:88), what challenge (Tahaddi) does Allah issue to all mankind and jinn combined?
optionsEn: To build a tower to the clouds
To cross the ocean on foot
To count every star
Even if mankind and jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they could not produce the like thereof
explanationEn: Verse 17:88 issues the ultimate literary and spiritual challenge proving the Qur'an's divine origin.

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Isra (17:110) instruct believers regarding tone of voice during Salah recitation?
optionsEn: Neither recite too loudly nor in total silence, but seek a moderate way between them
Recite only in whispers during Fajr
Always shout as loud as possible
Sing melodically in crowds
explanationEn: Revealed when Makkan polytheists mocked loud recitation, 17:110 teaches balance: neither overly loud nor barely audible, taking a middle path.

questionEn: How many verses of Surah Al-Kahf did the Prophet ﷺ say will protect whoever memorizes them from the trial (Fitnah) of the Dajjal?
optionsEn: The first three verses
Only verse 100
Only verse 50
The first ten verses (and in another narration, the last ten verses)
explanationEn: Sahih Muslim narrates that memorizing the opening ten verses (and in one narration, the closing ten verses) of Surah Al-Kahf shields a believer from the Dajjal.

questionEn: Which four great stories/tests anchor Surah Al-Kahf (Chapter 18), representing trials of faith, wealth, knowledge, and power?
optionsEn: Badr, Uhud, Khandaq, Tabuk
Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Lut
Yusuf, Dawud, Sulayman, Yunus
Sleepers of the Cave, Owner of Two Gardens, Musa & Al-Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn
explanationEn: Scholars note Surah Al-Kahf illustrates four trials: test of religion (Youth of the Cave), test of wealth (Owner of Two Gardens), test of knowledge (Musa & Khidr), and test of power (Dhul-Qarnayn).

questionEn: In Surah Al-Kahf (18:23–24), what phrase are believers instructed never to omit when speaking of any future plan?
optionsEn: Astaghfirullah
SubhanAllah
In sha'Allah (If Allah wills)
Alhamdulillah
explanationEn: 'And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," except [when adding], "If Allah wills."'

questionEn: How long did the People of the Cave remain asleep according to Surah Al-Kahf (18:25)?
optionsEn: 500 years
300 years, and add nine (309 lunar years)
100 years
70 years
explanationEn: Allah states they stayed in their cave three hundred years and exceeded by nine—reflecting the exact conversion between 300 solar years and 309 lunar years.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Kahf (18:46), what are called 'the adornment of worldly life' compared to lasting righteous deeds (Al-Baqiyat al-Salihat)?
optionsEn: Palaces and gardens
Gold and ships
Horses and crowns
Wealth and children
explanationEn: 'Wealth and children are [but] adornment of the worldly life. But the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord for reward and better for [one's] hope.'

questionEn: What special word lies in the middle of Surah Al-Kahf (18:19)—'walyatalattaf' (and let him be cautious/courteous)—often highlighted in Mushaf prints?
optionsEn: It is the longest Surah name
It is the only word in Syriac
It is the exact midpoint of the Qur'an by letter/word count in classical Mushaf counts
It is a Sajdah verse
explanationEn: Classical scribes often wrote 'walyatalattaf' in bold or red ink because according to traditional counts it marks the central word/letter midpoint of the entire Qur'an.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Kahf (18:109), if the sea were ink for the words of Allah, what would happen?
optionsEn: It would turn into gold
It would overflow the mountains
It would record half of them
The sea would be exhausted before the words of Allah were exhausted, even if another like it were brought
explanationEn: Verse 18:109 illustrates the infinite majesty and knowledge of Allah beyond human measurement.

questionEn: In the closing verse of Surah Al-Kahf (18:110), what two conditions are required for someone hoping to meet their Lord?
optionsEn: Fast every day and speak little
Do righteous deeds and associate none in the worship of their Lord
Build a dome and plant trees
Travel far and give silver
explanationEn: Scholars note 18:110 summarizes the two pillars of accepted deeds: sincerity (no shirk) and righteous action aligned with prophetic guidance.

questionEn: Which five Surahs of the Qur'an open directly with the praise 'Al-hamdu lillah' (All praise is due to Allah)?
optionsEn: Al-Fatihah, Al-An'am, Al-Kahf, Saba, and Fatir
Al-Falaq, An-Nas, Al-Kawthar, Al-Asr, Al-Fil
Yasin, Ar-Rahman, Al-Mulk, Nuh, Al-Ikhlas
Al-Baqarah, Al Imran, An-Nisa, Al-Ma'idah, Al-Anfal
explanationEn: Five Surahs begin with 'Al-hamdu lillah': Al-Fatihah (1), Al-An'am (6), Al-Kahf (18), Saba (34), and Fatir (35).

questionEn: Which Surah is known as 'Fustat al-Qur'an' (the Tent/Canopy of the Qur'an) due to its breadth of rulings and majesty?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Fatihah
Surah Al-Baqarah
Surah Al-Kahf
Surah Yusuf
explanationEn: Early scholars and companions such as Khalid ibn Ma'dan termed Surah Al-Baqarah 'Fustat al-Qur'an' because it encompasses faith, stories, worship, Hajj, family law, and economics.

questionEn: According to Sahih Muslim, what happens to a house in which Surah Al-Baqarah is recited?
optionsEn: Angels depart from it
Rain falls upon it
Satan flees from that house
It becomes a mosque automatically
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Do not make your houses into graveyards; indeed Satan flees from the house in which Surah Al-Baqarah is recited.'

questionEn: Which Surah's name literally means 'The Heights' and contains the dialogue between the inhabitants of Paradise, Hellfire, and those upon the elevated barrier?
optionsEn: Surah Al-A'raf
Surah Al-Hijr
Surah Al-Anfal
Surah Ar-Ra'd
explanationEn: Surah Al-A'raf (Chapter 7) takes its name from verses 7:46–48 depicting Al-A'raf.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:256), what clear principle is declared regarding entry into faith?
optionsEn: 'There shall be no compulsion in [acceptance of] the religion'
'Force tribes to convert'
'Test newcomers by fire'
'Charge tribute for entry'
explanationEn: 'La ikraha fid-din' affirms that sincere faith cannot be coerced, as truth stands manifestly distinct from error.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:286), what comforting rule about human capacity follows 'Allah does not burden a soul beyond that it can bear'?
optionsEn: It gets what it has earned, and against it is what it has deserved
Only prophets are tested
Angels carry all debts
Every burden doubles yearly
explanationEn: Verse 2:286 establishes both divine fairness—no soul is tasked beyond capacity—and personal accountability, followed by heartfelt prayers for pardon and mercy.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the light of Surah Al-Fatihah and the closing verses of Surah Al-Baqarah when an angel descended from a gate in heaven never opened before?
optionsEn: They must be inscribed on silver
They are recited only in Ramadan
They were never given to any prophet before him, and no letter from them is recited without being granted
They belong solely to Makkah
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated that an angel told the Prophet ﷺ: 'Rejoice in two lights given to you that were never given to any prophet before you: Al-Fatihah and the concluding verses of Al-Baqarah.'

questionEn: Which Surah opens with the pledge 'O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul' (Nafs Wahidah), highlighting human unity and family rights?
optionsEn: Surah Al-A'raf
Surah An-Nisa
Surah Al-Ma'idah
Surah At-Tawbah
explanationEn: Surah An-Nisa (4:1) anchors all family, orphan, and women's rights in our shared origin from a single soul (Adam) and his mate.

questionEn: In Surah Al Imran (3:159), what gentle quality of the Prophet ﷺ is credited for keeping the companions united around him?
optionsEn: Royal lineage
Severe discipline
Great wealth
His gentleness by mercy from Allah—for had he been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have dispersed
explanationEn: 'So by mercy from Allah, you were lenient with them. And if you had been rude and harsh in heart, they would have disbanded from about you.'

questionEn: Which two terms describe the decisive verses versus the allegorical/ambiguous verses in Surah Al Imran (3:7)?
optionsEn: Muhkamat (clear/decisive) and Mutashabihat (unspecific/allegorical)
Zahir and Batin
Makki and Madani
Nasikh and Mansukh
explanationEn: Surah Al Imran 3:7 explains that Muhkamat are the foundation (Umm al-Kitab) of the Book, while those firm in knowledge affirm all of it comes from Allah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:196), what two major acts of worship is the pilgrim commanded to complete for Allah?
optionsEn: Eid and Friday prayer
Hajj and Umrah
Fasting and I'tikaf
Zakat and Jihad
explanationEn: 'Wa atimmul-Hajja wal-'Umrata lillah'—complete Hajj and Umrah sincerely for Allah once entered into Ihram.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:196), if a pilgrim performing Tamattu' (combining Umrah then Hajj in Hajj months) cannot afford a sacrificial animal (Hady), what alternative is prescribed?
optionsEn: Staying in Arafat twice
Repeating Tawaf seven times
Fasting three days during Hajj and seven days upon returning home (ten total)
Paying 100 silver coins
explanationEn: Verse 2:196 specifies fasting 3 days during Hajj and 7 days when back home—making ten complete days—for one who cannot find or afford the Hady.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the superiority of Surah Al-Fatihah when speaking to Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla (RA)?
optionsEn: It was revealed in Madinah only
It has no equal in length
It is the shortest Surah
It is the greatest Surah in the Qur'an
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla (RA): 'I will surely teach you the greatest Surah in the Qur'an... It is Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbil-'alamin—the Seven Oft-Repeated verses.'

questionEn: In the science of Tajweed, what does the rule 'Idgham' mean when reciting the Qur'an?
optionsEn: Stretching a vowel for six counts
Merging/assimilating a silent consonant (like Nun Sakinah) smoothly into the following letter
Pronouncing a letter with heavy echo
Stopping completely at the end of a page
explanationEn: Idgham merges Nun Sakinah or Tanwin into the six letters of 'Yarmalun' (y, r, m, l, w, n) for fluid, harmonious recitation.

questionEn: In Tajweed, what are the five 'Qalqalah' letters that carry a crisp echoing bounce when voweled with Sukun?
optionsEn: Alif, Waw, Ya, Nun, Mim
Sin, Shin, Sad, Dad, Za
Kha, Ha, Ghayn, 'Ayn, Hamza
Qaf, Ta, Ba, Jim, Dal (Qutbu Jadin)
explanationEn: Grouped in the mnemonic 'Qutbu Jadin' (ق ط ب ج د), these five letters produce a slight vibration/echo when paused upon or carrying sukun.

questionEn: In Tajweed, what is 'Ghunnah'?
optionsEn: A sudden stop
A resonant nasal sound held for two counts, characteristic of Mim and Nun
A silent letter
A throat vibration on Ha
explanationEn: Ghunnah is the nasalized sound emanating from the nasal passage (khayshum), especially clear on Mushaddad Nun and Mim.

questionEn: In Tajweed, what does 'Madd' refer to?
optionsEn: Lengthening/prolonging a vowel sound beyond its natural two counts
Shortening a syllable
Whispering a verse
Skipping a Hamzah
explanationEn: Madd elongates vowel sounds (Alif, Waw, Ya) for 2, 4, 5, or 6 counts depending on rules like Madd Muttasil, Munfasil, or Lazim.

questionEn: How many standard canonical Qira'at (authentic modes of Qur'anic recitation) are universally recognized in the Ten Qira'at tradition?
optionsEn: Fourteen Qira'at
Seven foundational and three completing, totaling Ten Qira'at
Five Qira'at
Three Qira'at
explanationEn: Ibn Mujahid compiled the famous Seven Qira'at, and Ibn al-Jazari verified the Three completing them (likewise Mutawatir), forming the Ten Authentic Qira'at.

questionEn: Which narration (Riwayah) of the Qira'ah of Imam 'Asim is the most widely printed and recited across the Muslim world today?
optionsEn: Hafs 'an 'Asim
Qalun 'an Nafi'
Warsh 'an Nafi'
Al-Duri 'an Abi 'Amr
explanationEn: The transmission of Hafs from Imam 'Asim of Kufa is the most widespread globally, while Warsh and Qalun from Nafi' are widely recited in North and West Africa.

questionEn: What is the Uthmani script ('Rasm al-Uthmani') of the Mushaf?
optionsEn: Kufic stone engraving only
Modern Arabic calligraphy invented in Cairo
Persian cursive script
The standardized consonantal orthography approved by Caliph Uthman (RA) and his committee
explanationEn: Rasm al-Uthmani preserves the exact spelling conventions of the master Mushafs distributed by Uthman (RA) to major Islamic centers.

questionEn: Where did Caliph Uthman (RA) keep one master copy (often called Al-Mushaf al-Imam) while sending copies to Makkah, Syria, Kufa, and Basra?
optionsEn: Madinah
Damascus
Alexandria
Ta'if
explanationEn: Uthman (RA) retained a master copy in Madinah and dispatched official copies to the main provinces, ordering variant personal fragments burned to prevent discord.

questionEn: Which two companions did the Prophet ﷺ praise specifically in Hadith as among the earliest masters—one even offering to learn from him though a freed servant?
optionsEn: Abu Sufyan and Ikrimah
Salim Mawla Abi Hudhayfah and Mu'adh ibn Jabal (RA)
Abbas and Hamzah
Khalid and Amr
explanationEn: In Bukhari 4999, the Prophet ﷺ specifically named Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Salim Mawla Abi Hudhayfah, Mu'adh ibn Jabal, and Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA) as primary Qur'an teachers.

questionEn: What does the Qur'anic word 'Tadabbur' mean in verses like 'Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an?' (4:82 and 47:24)?
optionsEn: Copying the text
Counting pages rapidly
Memorizing without translation
Deep, contemplative reflection on its meanings, wisdom, and call to action
explanationEn: Surah Sad 38:29 explains the very purpose of revealing the Book: 'that they might reflect upon its verses (li-yaddabbaru ayatihi) and those of understanding would be reminded.'

questionEn: According to Surah An-Nisa (4:82), what proves the Qur'an comes from Allah rather than any human author?
optionsEn: Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found within it much contradiction
Its short length
Its gold binding
Its rhyme alone
explanationEn: Despite being revealed over 23 years across varied crises and triumphs, the Qur'an exhibits complete internal harmony without contradiction.

questionEn: What does Surah Al-Baqarah (2:121) say characterizes 'those who recite it with its true recitation' (Haqqa tilawatihi)?
optionsEn: Reading silently only
Following its guidance faithfully, affirming its truth, and acting by it
Reciting only on holidays
Debating its grammar
explanationEn: Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas (RA) explained 'haqqa tilawatihi' means reciting it properly, believing in it, declaring lawful what it permits, and refraining from what it forbids.

questionEn: Which Surah mentions in 4:29 the ethical rule against devouring one another's wealth unjustly except through trade by mutual consent?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Baqarah
Surah Yunus
Surah Al-Anfal
Surah An-Nisa
explanationEn: Surah An-Nisa 4:29 establishes consent-based commerce and prohibits fraud, usurpation, and self-harm.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:261), spending wealth in Allah's cause is compared to a single grain that sprouts into how many grains?
optionsEn: 70 grains
100 grains
1,000 grains
700 grains (seven spikes, each bearing a hundred grains)
explanationEn: Allah illustrates the exponential blessing of sincere charity: one grain produces seven ears, each ear containing a hundred grains, and Allah multiplies even further for whom He wills.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:264), what two harmful attitudes nullify the reward of charity like rain washing thin soil off a smooth rock?
optionsEn: Giving quietly and smiling
Reminders of generosity (Al-Mann) and hurtful words/injury (Al-Adha)
Giving dates and water
Giving at dawn
explanationEn: 'Do not invalidate your charities with reminders [of it] or injury'—preserving the dignity of recipients is essential in Islam.

questionEn: Which Surah's name literally means 'The Spoils of War' (Chapter 8)?
optionsEn: Surah At-Tawbah
Surah Al-Anfal
Surah Al-Ma'idah
Surah Al-A'raf
explanationEn: Surah Al-Anfal opens with a question about Al-Anfal (spoils after Badr), teaching that all provisions and victory belong to Allah and His Messenger.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anfal (8:46), what four traits ensure believers remain strong and do not lose heart?
optionsEn: Travel only by night
Build high towers
Gather swift horses only
Obey Allah and His Messenger, do not dispute lest you falter and lose strength, and be patient
explanationEn: Verse 8:46 warns that internal quarreling drains collective strength (tadh-hab rihukum), whereas obedience and patience bring Allah's support.

questionEn: Which Surah (Chapter 10) is named after a Prophet whose people were the only entire city in history to believe before punishment struck, so their doom was lifted?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Hijr
Surah Ibrahim
Surah Hud
Surah Yunus
explanationEn: Surah Yunus 10:98 notes that when the people of Yunus (Nineveh) sincerely repented and believed, Allah removed the punishment of disgrace from them.

questionEn: In Surah Yunus (10:62–63), who are defined as 'Awliya Allah' (the close friends/allies of Allah) who have no fear nor grief?
optionsEn: Kings and governors
Those who believe and are constantly mindful of Allah (Taqwa)
Only hermits in caves
Only scholars of poetry
explanationEn: 'Unquestionably, [for] the allies of Allah there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve—those who believed and were fearing Allah.'

questionEn: In Surah Hud (11:6), what does Allah guarantee for every single living creature on earth?
optionsEn: Its sustenance (Rizq) is upon Allah, and He knows its dwelling and resting place
Wings to fly
A hundred years of life
A shelter of stone
explanationEn: 'And there is no creature on earth but that upon Allah is its provision'—reassuring believers to strive lawfully without anxiety.

questionEn: What uplifting rule about good deeds erasing minor sins is stated in Surah Hud (11:114)?
optionsEn: 'Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds' (Innal-hasanati yudhhibnas-sayyi'at)
Only charity counts
Only yearly fasting counts
Good deeds erase nothing
explanationEn: Revealed when a remorseful companion confessed a minor sin, 11:114 teaches that establishing prayer and righteous deeds wipes away misdeeds.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:177), how does the Qur'an define true righteousness (Al-Birr) beyond merely turning faces east or west?
optionsEn: Sound faith, spending wealth out of love for Allah on kin, orphans, the needy, travelers, establishing prayer, Zakat, fulfilling pledges, and patience
Counting beads in silence
Facing one wall only
Wearing ceremonial robes
explanationEn: Ayat al-Birr (2:177) unites creed, social compassion, worship, integrity in promises, and resilience in hardship.

questionEn: In Surah Al Imran (3:134), what three noble traits describe the people of Paradise (Muttaqin) regarding anger and people's faults?
optionsEn: Speaking only in courts
Keeping strict grudges
Isolating from society
Spending in ease and hardship, restraining anger (Kazimin al-ghayz), and pardoning people
explanationEn: Allah loves the Muhsinin who give generously in both plenty and scarcity, swallow their anger, and pardon others.

questionEn: Which verse in Surah Al Imran (3:185) reminds every soul of mortality and true success?
optionsEn: 'Time never ends'
'Kings live forever'
'Wealth saves the noble'
'Every soul will taste death... Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained success'
explanationEn: Verse 3:185 clarifies that worldly life is only fleeting enjoyment of delusion compared to salvation in the Hereafter.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say is the best gathering among people who assemble in one of the houses of Allah?
optionsEn: Reciting the Book of Allah and studying it together, upon which tranquility descends and mercy covers them
Counting donations
Trading goods
Debating poetry
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim 2699, angels surround circles of Qur'an recitation and study, Sakinah descends, mercy envelops them, and Allah mentions them to those with Him.

questionEn: According to Sahih al-Bukhari, who are the very best people in the Ummah as declared by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: Those who learn the Qur'an and teach it
The fastest horsemen
The wealthiest merchants
The builders of towers
explanationEn: 'Khayrukum man ta'allamal-Qur'ana wa 'allamahu'—the best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it.

questionEn: With whom does the Prophet ﷺ say the skilled, fluent reciter of the Qur'an is ranked?
optionsEn: With ancient kings
With the merchants of Makkah
With the noble, obedient angelic scribes (Al-Safarat al-Kiram al-Bararah)
With desert guides
explanationEn: Fluency paired with devotion places the reciter in the spiritual company of the noble recording angels.

questionEn: Which Surah was revealed when some people ridiculed the Muslims after the change of Qiblah, asking 'What turned them away from their previous Qiblah?'
optionsEn: Surah Al-Baqarah (verses 2:142–150)
Surah At-Tawbah
Surah Al-Fatihah
Surah Al-Anfal
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:142 directly answers 'The foolish among the people will say, "What has turned them away from their qiblah..." Say: "To Allah belongs the east and the west."'

questionEn: How many Surahs in the Noble Qur'an begin with the disconnected letters 'Alif-Lam-Mim'?
optionsEn: 6 Surahs
9 Surahs
12 Surahs
3 Surahs
explanationEn: Six Surahs open with Alif-Lam-Mim: Al-Baqarah (2), Al Imran (3), Al-'Ankabut (29), Ar-Rum (30), Luqman (31), and As-Sajdah (32).

questionEn: Which single Surah in the Qur'an opens with five disconnected letters: 'Kaf-Ha-Ya-'Ayn-Sad'?
optionsEn: Surah Sad
Surah Maryam
Surah Ta-Ha
Surah Ash-Shura
explanationEn: Surah Maryam (Chapter 19) uniquely opens with the five-letter sequence Kaf-Ha-Ya-'Ayn-Sad.

questionEn: How many consecutive Surahs in the Mushaf (Chapters 40 through 46) open with the letters 'Ha-Mim', known collectively as 'Al-Hawamim'?
optionsEn: Five Surahs
Seven Surahs
Four Surahs
Ten Surahs
explanationEn: Seven consecutive Surahs—Ghafir (40), Fussilat (41), Ash-Shura (42), Az-Zukhruf (43), Ad-Dukhan (44), Al-Jathiyah (45), and Al-Ahqaf (46)—open with Ha-Mim.

questionEn: In Surah Al-An'am (6:125), how does Allah describe the chest of one whom He wills to guide?
optionsEn: He seals his tongue
He blinds his sight
He expands his breast to [accept] Islam (Yashrah sadrahu lil-Islam)
He increases his wealth
explanationEn: Spiritual openness and serenity in welcoming faith is described as Allah expanding the believer's chest to Islam.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:238), which prayer do many scholars identify with 'Al-Salat al-Wusta' (the Middle Prayer) that believers are urged to guard strictly?
optionsEn: Tahajjud prayer
Tarawih prayer
Asr prayer
Duha prayer
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim 627, the Prophet ﷺ explicitly identified Al-Salat al-Wusta during the Battle of the Trench as the Asr prayer.

questionEn: Which Surah contains the instruction in 17:79 encouraging Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to pray extra night vigil (Tahajjud) so his Lord may raise him to 'Maqam Mahmud'?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Muzzammil
Surah Al-Baqarah
Surah Al-Isra
Surah Al-Kahf
explanationEn: Surah Al-Isra 17:79 instructs the Prophet ﷺ to rise in the night for Tahajjud so Allah grants him the Praiseworthy Station (the Great Intercession on Judgment Day).
