questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:48), what is the Qur'an called in relation to earlier revealed scriptures like the Torah and Gospel?
optionsEn: An unrelated history
A hidden scroll
Confirming what came before it and a criterion/guardian (Muhaymin) over it
A replacement poem
explanationEn: 'Muhayminan 'alayhi' means the Qur'an serves as the trustworthy guardian and ultimate benchmark affirming true prior revelation and correcting distortions.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when someone listens to or recites a verse of Sajdah al-Tilawah and prostrates?
optionsEn: Only Imams may prostrate
Satan withdraws weeping, lamenting that the son of Adam was commanded to prostrate and obeyed, while Satan refused
The prayer becomes invalid
It must be repeated seven times
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrated that Satan weeps whenever a believer prostrates in obedience to a Sajdah verse, recalling his own fatal arrogance.

questionEn: According to Abu Umamah (RA) in Sahih Muslim, why did the Prophet ﷺ say 'Beautify the Qur'an with your voices'?
optionsEn: To imitate bells
To replace Adhan
To compete in markets
Because a beautiful, heartfelt voice enhances the impact and beauty of the Qur'an
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah (RA) also narrated that Allah listens more attentively to a prophet or believer reciting the Qur'an melodiously aloud than anything else.

questionEn: What is 'Hafiz' (or Hafizah) in Islamic tradition?
optionsEn: A calligrapher of seals
Someone who has committed the entire Noble Qur'an to memory
A pilgrim guide
A mosque architect
explanationEn: Since the time of the Prophet ﷺ, millions of Muslims have memorized every verse of the Qur'an word-for-word, preserving it both in hearts and in print.

questionEn: Which phrase in Surah Al-Qamar is repeated four times as a reassuring promise for memorizers and learners?
optionsEn: 'Write it in gold'
'Read it only in winter'
'Travel to learn it'
'We have made the Qur'an easy for remembrance—so is there any who will remember?'
explanationEn: 'Wa laqad yassarnal-Qur'ana lidh-dhikri fahal min muddakir' (54:17, 22, 32, 40) invites every seeker to memorize and reflect on the Qur'an.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anfal (8:24), what are believers urged to respond to immediately when Allah and His Messenger call them?
optionsEn: To silent retreat
To that which gives them true life (lima yuhyikum)
To tribal honor
To worldly trade
explanationEn: Responding to the Qur'an and Sunnah revives the spiritual heart just as rain revives dead earth.

questionEn: In Surah At-Tawbah (9:71), how are believing men and believing women described in relation to one another?
optionsEn: Unconcerned neighbors
Allies/protectors (Awliya) of one another, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong
Strangers to one another
Competitors in wealth
explanationEn: Verse 9:71 affirms mutual spiritual partnership and shared responsibility between believing men and women in prayer, charity, and moral uplift.

questionEn: In Surah At-Tawbah (9:103), what spiritual effect does taking Zakat/charity have upon the giver according to Allah's command to the Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: It purifies them and sanctifies/grows them (tutahhiruhum wa tuzakkihim)
It diminishes their blessings
It delays their prayers
It replaces pilgrimage
explanationEn: 'Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them increase, and invoke [Allah's blessings] upon them.'

questionEn: Which closing verse of Surah At-Tawbah (9:128) describes Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as deeply grieved by the believers' hardship and full of compassion and mercy for them?
optionsEn: At-Tawbah 9:5
At-Tawbah 9:40
At-Tawbah 9:100
At-Tawbah 9:128
explanationEn: 'There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; [he is] concerned over you and to the believers is kind and merciful.'

questionEn: Which supplication closes Surah At-Tawbah (9:129) for complete reliance when people turn away?
optionsEn: Hasbiyallahu la ilaha illa Huwa, 'alayhi tawakkaltu wa Huwa Rabbul-'Arshil-'Azim
Subhana Rabbil-'Azim
Alhamdulillahi wahdah
Rabbana atina fid-dunya
explanationEn: 'Sufficient for me is Allah; there is no deity except Him. On Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne.'

questionEn: With which set of disjointed Arabic letters (Huruf Muqatta'at) does Surah Maryam (19) open?
optionsEn: Ta-Sin-Mim
Kaf-Ha-Ya-'Ayn-Sad
Ha-Mim-'Ayn-Sin-Qaf
Alif-Lam-Mim-Sad
explanationEn: Surah Maryam opens uniquely with the five letters Kaf-Ha-Ya-'Ayn-Sad in its very first verse.

questionEn: What unique distinction does Surah Maryam mention about the name of Prophet Zakariyya's son, Yahya?
optionsEn: No one before him had ever been given that name
It meant 'the one who speaks in the cradle'
It was chosen by Zakariyya after a dream
It was shared by three earlier prophets
explanationEn: Allah gave Zakariyya glad tidings of a boy named Yahya and stated that He had not assigned that name to anyone before him.

questionEn: When Prophet Zakariyya asked for a sign after receiving news of a son in Surah Maryam, what sign was granted to him?
optionsEn: Hearing angels recite inside the sanctuary
A cloud shading his home for three days
Being unable to speak to people for three nights despite being healthy
A staff blossoming with leaves
explanationEn: Allah told Zakariyya that his sign was that he would not speak to people for three consecutive nights while being completely sound.

questionEn: Under which type of tree did Maryam experience the pains of childbirth according to Surah Maryam?
optionsEn: A date-palm tree
A lote tree
A fig tree
An olive tree
explanationEn: The pains of childbirth drove Maryam to the trunk of a date-palm tree, where she was told to shake the trunk so fresh ripe dates would fall.

questionEn: What vow was Maryam instructed to announce if she saw any human being after giving birth to Isa?
optionsEn: That she was travelling to Egypt immediately
That she would remain in the sanctuary for forty days
That she would distribute all her dates to the poor
That she had vowed a fast of silence to the Most Merciful
explanationEn: Maryam was commanded to say that she had vowed a fast (abstaining from speech) to Ar-Rahman and would not speak to any human that day.

questionEn: Which prophet is described in Surah Maryam as a man of truth and a prophet whom Allah raised to a high station (makanan 'aliyya)?
optionsEn: Prophet Salih
Prophet Idris
Prophet Hud
Prophet Shu'ayb
explanationEn: Surah Maryam mentions Prophet Idris, describing him as a truthful prophet whom Allah raised to a high station.

questionEn: Which verse of Surah Maryam contains a prostration of recitation (Sajdah al-Tilawah)?
optionsEn: Verse 85
Verse 15
Verse 58
Verse 34
explanationEn: Surah Maryam 19:58 describes the blessed prophets falling down in prostration and weeping when the verses of Ar-Rahman were recited to them, and marks a Sajdah al-Tilawah.

questionEn: In Surah Ta-Ha, what was Prophet Musa instructed to do upon reaching the sacred valley of Tuwa?
optionsEn: Remove his sandals
Fast until sunset
Cast his cloak upon the stone
Perform two units of prayer
explanationEn: Allah addressed Musa at the sacred valley of Tuwa, saying: 'Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals.'

questionEn: In Surah Ta-Ha, what did Prophet Musa pray for immediately after being commanded to go to Pharaoh?
optionsEn: For wealth to support the Children of Israel
For Pharaoh's palace to be shaken by an earthquake
For his chest to be expanded, his task eased, and the knot untied from his tongue
For an army of angels to precede him into Egypt
explanationEn: Musa prayed: 'My Lord, expand for me my breast, ease for me my task, and untie the knot from my tongue that they may understand my speech.'

questionEn: How did Allah instruct Musa and Harun to speak when delivering the message to Pharaoh in Surah Ta-Ha?
optionsEn: Only through written scrolls
With gentle speech so he might remember or fear
With stern warnings of immediate destruction
In complete silence while showing miracles
explanationEn: Allah commanded Musa and Harun to speak to Pharaoh gently (qawlan layyinan) so that perhaps he might be reminded or fear Allah.

questionEn: According to Surah Ta-Ha, who fashioned a calf out of melted ornaments that produced a lowing sound while Musa was away on the mount?
optionsEn: Bal'am
Haman
Qarun
As-Samiri
explanationEn: As-Samiri misled the Children of Israel during Musa's absence by casting ornaments into fire and crafting a calf that made a lowing sound.

questionEn: What short supplication is Prophet Muhammad commanded to recite in Surah Ta-Ha 20:114?
optionsEn: My Lord, increase me in knowledge
My Lord, grant me a sound heart
My Lord, make me steadfast in prayer
My Lord, forgive me and have mercy
explanationEn: Allah instructed the Prophet not to hasten with the Quran before its revelation was completed and to say: 'Rabbi zidni ilma' (My Lord, increase me in knowledge).

questionEn: How did Shaytan tempt Prophet Adam to eat from the forbidden tree according to Surah Ta-Ha?
optionsEn: He claimed eating from it would grant control over the winds
He said it was required to remain in the Garden for forty years
He called it the Tree of Immortality and a kingdom that never decays
He promised it would make Adam equal to the angels in wings
explanationEn: Shaytan whispered to Adam saying: 'Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity (shajarat al-khuld) and possession that will not deteriorate?'

questionEn: What consequence does Surah Ta-Ha 20:124 warn awaits whoever turns away from Allah's remembrance?
optionsEn: Exile from one's homeland for seven years
Constant nightmares during sleep
A depressed, straitened life and being raised blind on Resurrection Day
Total loss of speech in old age
explanationEn: Allah states that whoever turns away from His remembrance will have a straitened life (ma'ishatan danka) and will be gathered blind on the Day of Resurrection.

questionEn: What cosmic fact does Surah Al-Anbiya 21:30 invite disbelievers to reflect upon?
optionsEn: That the sun orbits around the earth every twelve months
That mountains float above oceans of fire
That the moon borrows its light from the stars
That the heavens and earth were joined together before Allah separated them, and every living thing was made from water
explanationEn: Surah Al-Anbiya states that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity (ratqan), Allah separated them, and He made every living thing from water.

questionEn: What command did Allah give to the fire when Prophet Ibrahim was cast into it in Surah Al-Anbiya?
optionsEn: Turn into flowing river water
Become extinguished before he touches the embers
Lift him up into the clouds
Be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim
explanationEn: Allah commanded the fire: 'O fire, be coolness and safety (bardan wa salaman) upon Ibrahim,' protecting him completely.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anbiya, what dispute were Prophets Dawud and Sulayman both given wisdom to judge?
optionsEn: An inheritance disagreement between two brothers
A case involving a people's sheep that strayed into another's crop field at night
A theft of silver vessels from the sanctuary
A boundary dispute over two wells in Jerusalem
explanationEn: Dawud and Sulayman judged regarding a tilled field in which another people's sheep had pastured at night, and Allah gave Sulayman deeper understanding of the ruling.

questionEn: Which prophet is referred to as 'Dhun-Nun' (Man of the Fish) in Surah Al-Anbiya, who called upon Allah from within the darknesses?
optionsEn: Prophet Al-Yasa'
Prophet Dhul-Kifl
Prophet Ilyas
Prophet Yunus
explanationEn: Dhun-Nun refers to Prophet Yunus, who called out inside the darknesses: 'La ilaha illa Anta Subhanaka inni kuntu minaz-zalimin.'

questionEn: In which previously revealed scripture does Surah Al-Anbiya 21:105 state Allah wrote that the earth will be inherited by His righteous servants?
optionsEn: The Suhuf of Ibrahim
The Injil
The Suhuf of Musa
The Zabur
explanationEn: Allah states: 'And We have already written in the Zabur after the [previous] mention that the land is inherited by My righteous servants.'

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Anbiya 21:107 describe the universal purpose of Prophet Muhammad's mission?
optionsEn: A conqueror of ancient empires
A light solely for the tribes of Quraysh
A mercy to the worlds (rahmatan lil-'alamin)
A judge over past scriptures
explanationEn: Allah declares: 'And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.'

questionEn: What unique distinction does Surah Al-Hajj (22) hold regarding Sajdah al-Tilawah in the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools?
optionsEn: Its prostration must be performed twice consecutively
It has no prostration verses despite mentioning prayer
It is the only Surah containing two verses of prostration
Its prostration verse appears in the opening Ayah
explanationEn: According to the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools, Surah Al-Hajj is the only Surah in the Quran with two Sajdah al-Tilawah verses: 22:18 and 22:77.

questionEn: What terrifying event does the opening of Surah Al-Hajj warn humanity about?
optionsEn: The violent convulsion (zalzalah) of the Hour
The darkening of the sun for forty days
The splitting of the seven seas
The drowning of Pharaoh's army
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hajj opens with an urgent command to fear Allah because the convulsion (zalzalah) of the Hour is a tremendous thing.

questionEn: Whom did Allah command in Surah Al-Hajj 22:27 to proclaim the Pilgrimage to mankind?
optionsEn: Prophet Muhammad
Prophet Ya'qub
Prophet Isma'il
Prophet Ibrahim
explanationEn: After showing Ibrahim the site of the House, Allah commanded him: 'And proclaim to the people the Hajj; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel.'

questionEn: What title is given to the Kaaba in Surah Al-Hajj 22:29 and 22:33 where pilgrims perform Tawaf?
optionsEn: Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur
Al-Masjid al-Aqsa
Al-Bayt al-'Atiq (The Ancient House)
Dar as-Salam
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hajj commands pilgrims to fulfill their vows and circumambulate Al-Bayt al-'Atiq (the Ancient House), referring to the Kaaba.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Hajj 22:32, what does honoring the sacred symbols and rites of Allah (Sha'a'ir Allah) stem from?
optionsEn: Memorization of pilgrimage poetry
The piety (taqwa) of the hearts
Abundance of sacrificial livestock
Fear of tribal elders
explanationEn: Allah says: 'And whoever honors the symbols of Allah - indeed, it is from the piety of hearts.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hajj 22:37, what does Allah clarify actually reaches Him from sacrificial animals?
optionsEn: The number of animals slaughtered
The blood sprinkled near the sanctuary
The finest portions of meat
The piety (taqwa) of the believers
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hajj states: 'Their meat will not reach Allah, nor will their blood, but what reaches Him is piety from you.'

questionEn: Why is Surah Al-Hajj 22:39 especially significant in Islamic history and jurisprudence?
optionsEn: It abolished the pre-Islamic sacred months
It granted the first Quranic permission for the wronged believers to fight in self-defense
It established the five daily prayers
It mandated the direction of Qiblah toward Makkah
explanationEn: Verse 22:39—'Permission [to fight] has been given to those who are being fought, because they were wronged'—is widely recognized as the earliest verse permitting defensive armed struggle.

questionEn: What tiny creature does Surah Al-Hajj 22:73 use in a parable to prove the helplessness of false deities?
optionsEn: A mosquito
A spider
A fly
An ant
explanationEn: Allah states that those invoked besides Him could never create even a fly—even if they all gathered together—and if the fly snatches anything from them, they cannot recover it.

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Mu'minun begin when describing the believers who attain true success?
optionsEn: Those who are humbly submissive (khashi'un) in their prayer
Those who recite the Quran at dawn
Those who fast every Monday and Thursday
Those who migrate across the sea
explanationEn: After declaring 'Certainly will the believers have succeeded,' the very first quality listed is 'They who are during their prayer humbly submissive.'

questionEn: Which level of Paradise are the successful believers described in Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:1-9 promised to inherit?
optionsEn: Jannat al-Khuld
Al-Firdaws
Jannat 'Adn
Dar al-Muqamah
explanationEn: Surah Al-Mu'minun concludes its list of seven qualities of successful believers by stating: 'Those are the inheritors who will inherit Al-Firdaws; they will abide therein eternally.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:12-14, after tracing human creation from clay through nutfah, 'alaqah, mudghah, and bones clothed with flesh, what praise concludes verse 14?
optionsEn: Allahu Akbar
So blessed is Allah, the Best of Creators
To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens
Subhana Rabbil-'Azim
explanationEn: Verse 23:14 details the developmental stages of the human embryo and concludes with 'Fatabarakallahu ahsanul-khaliqin' (So blessed is Allah, the best of creators).

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:27, what signaled that the Flood of Prophet Nuh had begun so he should board the Ark?
optionsEn: A trumpet blast from the mountains
The falling of three stars
A sudden solar eclipse
The oven (at-tannur) gushing forth water
explanationEn: Allah told Nuh: 'When Our command comes and the oven overflows, put into it from each [kind] two mates and your family.'

questionEn: What spiritual counsel does Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:96 give on how to respond to evil conduct?
optionsEn: Withdraw permanently from human society
Expose the wrongdoer publicly before the tribe
Repel evil by that which is best
Respond with an equal harshness
explanationEn: Allah instructs: 'Repel, by [means of] what is best, [their] evil. We are most knowing of what they describe.'

questionEn: What rhetorical question does Allah ask humanity near the end of Surah Al-Mu'minun (23:115)?
optionsEn: Did you think wealth could ransom a soul from death?
Did you think angels were invisible out of weakness?
Did you think the sun and moon move by chance?
Did you think that We created you in vain and that to Us you would not be returned?
explanationEn: Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:115 asks: 'Then did you think that We created you uselessly and that to Us you would not be returned?'

questionEn: In Surah An-Nur 24:4, what punishment is prescribed for qadhf (slandering a chaste woman without producing four witnesses)?
optionsEn: Forty lashes
Eighty lashes and permanent rejection of their testimony
A fine of one hundred camels
Exile for one year
explanationEn: Surah An-Nur mandates that those who accuse chaste women and do not bring four witnesses are to be flogged eighty lashes and their testimony never accepted thereafter (unless they repent and reform).

questionEn: Which legal procedure in Surah An-Nur 24:6-9 resolves a husband's accusation of infidelity against his wife when he has no other witnesses?
optionsEn: Divorce by triple pronouncement
Li'an (mutual sworn testimonies and invoking Allah's curse if lying)
A forty-day waiting period
Arbitration by two elders
explanationEn: Surah An-Nur prescribes Li'an, where the husband swears four times by Allah and invokes Allah's curse on the fifth if lying, and the wife averts punishment by swearing four times and invoking Allah's wrath on the fifth if he is truthful.

questionEn: Which historical event involving the Prophet's household was addressed and cleared in Surah An-Nur 24:11-20?
optionsEn: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
The Battle of the Trench
The Incident of Al-Ifk (the false slander against A'ishah)
The Boycott of Banu Hashim
explanationEn: Verses 24:11-20 were revealed during the Incident of Al-Ifk, exonerating A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) and censuring those who spread the rumor.

questionEn: What social etiquette does Surah An-Nur 24:27 require before entering a home other than one's own?
optionsEn: Knocking three times loudly
Bringing a small gift for the host
Asking permission and greeting the inhabitants with peace (salam)
Waiting outside until sunset
explanationEn: Allah commands believers: 'Do not enter houses other than your own houses until you ascertain welcome and greet their inhabitants.'

questionEn: What fundamental moral command does Surah An-Nur 24:30-31 give to both believing men and believing women?
optionsEn: To lower their gaze and guard their private parts
To wear only white garments in public
To fast three days every month
To avoid traveling alone at night
explanationEn: In consecutive verses (24:30 and 24:31), Allah commands believing men and believing women to lower their gaze and guard their modesty.

questionEn: In Ayat an-Nur (24:35), from which blessed tree is the oil of the radiant lamp described as coming?
optionsEn: A date-palm of Madinah
A pomegranate tree of Syria
A blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west
A cedar tree of Lebanon
explanationEn: The famous Verse of Light likens Allah's light to a niche holding a lamp inside glass, lit from 'a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire.'

questionEn: Which three times of privacy does Surah An-Nur 24:58 require household servants and young children to ask permission before entering private rooms?
optionsEn: During Friday sermon, at Maghrib, and at dawn
Before the dawn prayer (Fajr), at midday rest, and after the night prayer (Isha)
Before sunrise, at Asr, and at midnight
Before Dhuhr, before Asr, and before Maghrib
explanationEn: Surah An-Nur 24:58 specifies three times of privacy ('awrat): before Fajr prayer, when laying aside garments at noon, and after Isha prayer.

questionEn: How does Surah An-Nur 24:22 respond when a believer vows to stop helping a needy relative who wronged them (revealed regarding Abu Bakr as-Siddiq)?
optionsEn: It instructs cutting ties for one full year
It requires paying ten dinars in expiation only
It encourages pardoning and overlooking, asking: 'Would you not like that Allah should forgive you?'
It confirms the oath is binding forever
explanationEn: When Abu Bakr vowed to stop supporting Mistah after the slander, 24:22 urged him to pardon and overlook, asking: 'Would you not like that Allah should forgive you?'

questionEn: What does the name of Surah Al-Furqan (25) mean?
optionsEn: The Noble Gathering
The Final Warning
The Criterion (between truth and falsehood)
The Clear Light
explanationEn: Al-Furqan means The Criterion, referring to the Quran as the standard that distinguishes truth from falsehood.

questionEn: What complaint will Prophet Muhammad raise on the Day of Judgment according to Surah Al-Furqan 25:30?
optionsEn: My people fought one another over trade routes
My people neglected the pilgrimage to Makkah
My people have taken this Quran as a thing abandoned (mahjura)
My people forgot the direction of prayer
explanationEn: Verse 25:30 records the Messenger saying: 'O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Quran as [a thing] abandoned.'

questionEn: What geographical/natural phenomenon does Surah Al-Furqan 25:53 highlight as a sign of Allah's power?
optionsEn: Four rivers flowing beneath Mount Sinai
Two bodies of water—one fresh and sweet, the other salty and bitter—separated by a barrier (barzakh)
Volcanoes erupting beneath frozen seas
Clouds carrying snow across the equator
explanationEn: Surah Al-Furqan 25:53 states that Allah released the two seas—one fresh and sweet, the other salty and bitter—and placed between them a barrier and prohibiting partition.

questionEn: How do 'Ibad ar-Rahman (the Servants of the Most Merciful) respond when addressed harshly by ignorant people in Surah Al-Furqan 25:63?
optionsEn: They debate them until midnight
They report them to the judges
They say words of peace ('Salam')
They turn away without answering at all
explanationEn: Surah Al-Furqan describes the servants of Ar-Rahman as those who walk upon the earth in humility and, when the ignorant address them, say 'Peace' (Salam).

questionEn: Which verse of Surah Al-Furqan marks a Sajdah al-Tilawah when the disbelievers object to prostrating to Ar-Rahman?
optionsEn: Verse 25
Verse 74
Verse 44
Verse 60
explanationEn: Surah Al-Furqan 25:60 states that when it is said to them, 'Prostrate to Ar-Rahman,' they scornfully refuse, and the verse is a Sajdah al-Tilawah.

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shu'ara (26), what did Prophet Musa reply when his followers panicked at the sea saying, 'Indeed, we are to be overtaken!'?
optionsEn: No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me
Prepare to surrender to Pharaoh
Wait until the wind turns back the chariots
Let us swim across before nightfall
explanationEn: Musa replied with unwavering trust: 'Kalla! Inna ma'iya Rabbi sayahdin' (No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me), after which the sea parted.

questionEn: According to Prophet Ibrahim's prayer in Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:88-89, what alone will benefit a person on the Day when neither wealth nor children avail?
optionsEn: Coming to Allah with a sound heart (qalbin salim)
Having traveled to distant lands
Having built grand stone monuments
Speaking eloquent Arabic poetry
explanationEn: Ibrahim prayed not to be disgraced on the Day of Resurrection—'The Day when there will not benefit [anyone] wealth or children, except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart.'

questionEn: What sign did Prophet Salih present to the people of Thamud in Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:155?
optionsEn: A cloud that rained only on believers' crops
A staff that turned into a serpent
A she-camel with an alternating day's share of water
A spring of honey in the desert
explanationEn: Salih told Thamud: 'This is a she-camel. For her is a [time of] drink, and for you is a [time of] drink, [each] on a known day.'

questionEn: Whom was Prophet Muhammad specifically instructed to warn in Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:214?
optionsEn: His closest kindred ('ashirataka al-aqrabin)
The scribes of Madinah
The rulers of Persia
The merchants of Syria
explanationEn: Allah commanded the Prophet: 'Wa andhir 'ashirataka al-aqrabin' (And warn your closest kindred), marking the start of his public call to his family.

questionEn: Which group of poets does Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:227 exempt from its censure of aimless poets?
optionsEn: Those who compose epics of ancient kings
Those who recite only at royal courts
Those who avoid rhyming prose
Those who believe, do righteous deeds, remember Allah much, and defend themselves after being wronged
explanationEn: After stating that the deviators follow the poets, verse 227 exempts those who believe, do righteous deeds, remember Allah often, and only retaliate after being wronged.

questionEn: What unique structural feature distinguishes Surah An-Naml (27) regarding the phrase 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim'?
optionsEn: It contains Bismillah twice: once at the opening and once inside Prophet Sulayman's letter
Every tenth verse begins with Bismillah
It omits Bismillah completely
It places Bismillah at the very end of the Surah
explanationEn: Surah An-Naml opens with Bismillah and also quotes it inside Sulayman's letter to the Queen of Sheba in verse 27:30.

questionEn: What extraordinary gift given to Prophet Sulayman is highlighted in Surah An-Naml 27:16?
optionsEn: Living for a thousand years
Creating diamonds from sand
Being taught the speech/language of birds (mantiq at-tayr)
Walking on water without a ship
explanationEn: Sulayman declared to his people: 'O mankind, we have been taught the language of birds, and we have been given from all things.'

questionEn: Why did an ant warn its fellow ants in the Valley of the Ants in Surah An-Naml 27:18?
optionsEn: Because birds were hunting near their colony
Because a flash flood was approaching the valley
Lest Sulayman and his soldiers crush them while they did not perceive
Because winter had arrived early
explanationEn: The ant cried out: 'O ants, enter your dwellings that you not be crushed by Sulayman and his soldiers while they perceive not,' causing Sulayman to smile in gratitude.

questionEn: Which bird brought Prophet Sulayman intelligence about the Queen of Sheba (Saba) and her people's worship of the sun?
optionsEn: The raven
The dove
The eagle
The hoopoe (al-hudhud)
explanationEn: The hoopoe (hudhud) arrived after being briefly absent and reported finding a woman ruling Saba with a great throne, whose people prostrated to the sun instead of Allah.

questionEn: Which verse of Surah An-Naml contains a Sajdah al-Tilawah?
optionsEn: Verse 40
Verse 82
Verse 26
Verse 62
explanationEn: Following the mention of Satan beautifying sun-worship for the people of Saba, Surah An-Naml 27:25-26 calls to prostrate to Allah alone, with Sajdah marked at 27:26.

questionEn: How quickly did the person who had knowledge from the Scripture bring the Queen of Sheba's throne to Prophet Sulayman in Surah An-Naml 27:40?
optionsEn: Before Sulayman's glance returned to him (in the blink of an eye)
By the end of the night
Before the sun reached midday
Within three days
explanationEn: After an 'ifrit of the jinn offered to bring it before Sulayman rose from his seat, one who had knowledge from the Scripture said: 'I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Qasas 28:7, what instruction did Allah inspire to the mother of Prophet Musa to save him from Pharaoh?
optionsEn: Send him with a caravan to Madyan
Nurse him, and when she feared for him, cast him into the river
Hide him in a cave outside Egypt
Dress him as a girl for seven years
explanationEn: Allah inspired Musa's mother: 'Nurse him; but when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you.'

questionEn: What two qualities did one of the daughters of the elder in Madyan praise when urging her father to hire Prophet Musa in Surah Al-Qasas 28:26?
optionsEn: Eloquent and wealthy
Learned and patient
Strong and trustworthy (al-qawiyyul-amin)
Tall and soft-spoken
explanationEn: She said: 'O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy.'

questionEn: What humble supplication did Prophet Musa make under the shade after watering the flocks in Madyan in Surah Al-Qasas 28:24?
optionsEn: My Lord, grant me kingship over Madyan
My Lord, return me swiftly to my mother in Egypt
My Lord, give me a staff of iron
My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need
explanationEn: Musa prayed: 'Rabbi inni lima anzalta ilayya min khayrin faqir' (My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need).

questionEn: In Surah Al-Qasas 28:56, what reality did Allah clarify to Prophet Muhammad when he grieved over his uncle Abu Talib not accepting Islam?
optionsEn: Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills
Guidance comes only after migration
No one over sixty years old accepts new scripture
Wealth always blinds tribal leaders
explanationEn: Allah revealed: 'Indeed, [O Muhammad], you do not guide whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills. And He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.'

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Qasas 28:76 illustrate the immense wealth of Qarun?
optionsEn: His camels stretched across three valleys
He owned half the ships on the Nile
The keys to his treasuries alone were a heavy burden for a band of strong men
His palace had gates of solid emerald
explanationEn: Surah Al-Qasas notes that Allah gave Qarun such treasures that their very keys were a heavy burden for a strong group of men.

questionEn: What balanced advice did the righteous scholars give to Qarun in Surah Al-Qasas 28:77?
optionsEn: Spend only on your own tribe and ignore outsiders
Seek the Hereafter through what Allah has given you, and do not forget your share of the world
Keep your wealth secret from Pharaoh's tax collectors
Throw all your gold into the sea to purify your soul
explanationEn: They advised him: 'Seek, through that which Allah has given you, the home of the Hereafter; and [yet], do not forget your share of the world. And do good as Allah has done good to you.'

questionEn: How long did Prophet Nuh remain among his people calling them to Allah according to Surah Al-Ankabut 29:14?
optionsEn: 770 years
500 years
120 years
950 years (a thousand years less fifty)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ankabut 29:14 states that Nuh remained among his people 'a thousand years less fifty years' (950 years) before the Flood.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ankabut 29:41, what does the frailty of a spider's web symbolize?
optionsEn: The fragility of merchant treaties
The fleeting nature of desert rain
The helplessness of taking protectors/deities besides Allah
The shortness of human youth
explanationEn: Allah compares those who take protectors besides Him to the spider that builds a house, declaring: 'And indeed, the weakest of houses is the house of the spider, if they only knew.'

questionEn: What protective effect of regular prayer (Salah) is highlighted in Surah Al-Ankabut 29:45?
optionsEn: It prevents all physical illness
It guarantees immense wealth in trade
It removes the need for seeking knowledge
It prohibits immorality and wrongdoing (al-fahsha'i wal-munkar)
explanationEn: Allah says: 'Establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater.'

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Ankabut 29:46 instruct Muslims to dialogue with the People of the Scripture?
optionsEn: By mocking their scholars in public
By avoiding all conversation with them
In a way that is best, affirming belief in what was revealed to us and to them
By demanding tribute before speaking
explanationEn: Verse 29:46 instructs: 'And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best, except for those who commit injustice among them.'

questionEn: What promise does Allah make in the concluding verse of Surah Al-Ankabut (29:69) to those who strive in His cause?
optionsEn: We will give them rule over the oceans
We will surely guide them to Our ways
We will spare them from every worldly trial
We will send angels visible to all eyes
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ankabut closes with the reassuring promise: 'And those who strive for Us - We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good.'

questionEn: What geopolitical prophecy made in the opening verses of Surah Ar-Rum (30:2-4) came true within a decade?
optionsEn: The building of a bridge across the Red Sea
The conquest of Andalusia
The victory of the Romans (Byzantines) over the Persians within three to nine years after their defeat
The collapse of the Abyssinian kingdom
explanationEn: After the Byzantines were defeated by the Persians, Allah foretold they would triumph within 'bid'i sinin' (3 to 9 years), which was fulfilled when Heraclius defeated Persia.

questionEn: What three spiritual gifts in marriage does Surah Ar-Rum 30:21 describe as signs of Allah?
optionsEn: Silence, obedience, and seclusion
Wealth, lineage, and status
Strength, speed, and courage
Tranquility (sakan), affection (mawaddah), and mercy (rahmah)
explanationEn: Surah Ar-Rum 30:21 mentions that Allah created spouses from among yourselves so you may find tranquility (sakan) in them, and placed affection (mawaddah) and mercy (rahmah) between you.

questionEn: What does the term 'Fitrat Allah' in Surah Ar-Rum 30:30 refer to?
optionsEn: The pure, natural disposition upon which Allah created all mankind
The architectural design of the Kaaba
The lunar calendar established for fasting
The annual charity due on livestock
explanationEn: Fitrat Allah denotes the innate human inclination toward recognizing and worshipping Allah alone, upon which He created all people.

questionEn: According to Surah Ar-Rum 30:41, what is the root cause of corruption appearing on land and sea?
optionsEn: What the hands of people have earned
The shifting orbits of distant planets
The natural aging of mountains
Excessive rainfall in winter
explanationEn: Allah states: 'Corruption has appeared throughout the land and sea by [reason of] what the hands of people have earned so He may let them taste part of [the consequence of] what they have done that perhaps they will return.'

questionEn: What three stages of human physical existence does Surah Ar-Rum 30:54 outline?
optionsEn: Weakness, then strength after weakness, then weakness and gray hair
Hunger, fullness, and fasting
Sleep, wakefulness, and dreaming
Youth, leadership, and travel
explanationEn: Allah describes creating humans from weakness (infancy), then making strength after weakness (adulthood), then making weakness and gray hair after strength (old age).

questionEn: What was the very first piece of advice Luqman gave to his son in Surah Luqman 31:13?
optionsEn: Do not associate partners with Allah; indeed, shirk is a great injustice
Memorize the stories of ancient kings
Speak softly when entering a marketplace
Give charity daily before sunrise
explanationEn: Luqman began his counsel to his son by saying: 'O my son, do not associate [anything] with Allah. Indeed, association [with Him] is great injustice (zulmun 'azim).'

questionEn: How does Surah Luqman 31:15 instruct a child to treat parents who actively pressure them to commit shirk?
optionsEn: Do not obey them in shirk, yet accompany them in this world with kindness
Cut off all contact and refuse to speak to them
Obey them out of filial duty even in shirk
Publicly denounce them before the community
explanationEn: Allah commands: 'If they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them, but accompany them in [this] world with appropriate kindness (ma'rufa).'

questionEn: What tiny object did Luqman cite in Surah Luqman 31:16 to teach his son about Allah's all-encompassing knowledge?
optionsEn: A spark of flint
A drop of morning dew
The weight of a mustard seed (mithqala habbatin min khardal)
A single eyelash
explanationEn: Luqman taught his son that even if a deed were the weight of a mustard seed inside a rock, in the heavens, or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth.

questionEn: Which four duties did Luqman pair together in Surah Luqman 31:17?
optionsEn: Reciting, memorizing, teaching, and judging
Establishing prayer, enjoining right, forbidding wrong, and being patient over what befalls you
Silence, fasting, seclusion, and charity
Fasting, Hajj, trade, and writing
explanationEn: Luqman told his son: 'O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you.'

questionEn: In Surah Luqman 31:19, which animal's voice is given as a warning against loud, harsh shouting?
optionsEn: The camel
The hyena
The donkey
The crow
explanationEn: Luqman advised his son to be moderate in his pace and lower his voice, noting: 'Indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys.'

questionEn: What imagery does Surah Luqman 31:27 use to express the inexhaustibility of Allah's words?
optionsEn: All trees on earth as pens and the sea as ink, replenished by seven more seas
All stars stacked from horizon to horizon
All grains of sand counted by angels
All rain falling since the dawn of creation
explanationEn: Allah states that if every tree on earth were pens and the sea were ink, followed by seven more seas, the words of Allah would still not be exhausted.

questionEn: Which set accurately lists the five matters of the Unseen (Mafatih al-Ghayb) reserved exclusively for Allah in Surah Luqman 31:34?
optionsEn: Knowledge of the Hour, sending rain, what is in the wombs, what a soul earns tomorrow, and in what land a soul will die
The number of prophets, weight of clouds, speed of light, age of the earth, and language of jinn
Future rulers, prices of grain, length of winter, dreams of kings, and hidden treasures
The number of stars, depth of oceans, lifespan of mountains, names of angels, and dates of eclipses
explanationEn: Surah Luqman 31:34 closes by declaring that Allah alone possesses knowledge of the Hour, sends down rain, knows what is in the wombs, what a soul will earn tomorrow, and in what land it will die.

questionEn: Which two Surahs did Prophet Muhammad habitually recite in the two rak'ahs of Fajr prayer on Fridays?
optionsEn: Surah Ya-Sin and Surah Ar-Rahman
Surah Al-Hajj and Surah Al-Mu'minun
Surah As-Sajdah (32) and Surah Al-Insan (76)
Surah Maryam and Surah Ta-Ha
explanationEn: Authentic narrations in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim report that the Prophet regularly recited Surah As-Sajdah in the first rak'ah and Surah Al-Insan in the second rak'ah of Friday Fajr.

questionEn: Which verse of Surah As-Sajdah (32) contains the obligatory/recommended prostration of recitation (Sajdah al-Tilawah)?
optionsEn: Verse 10
Verse 5
Verse 15
Verse 25
explanationEn: Surah As-Sajdah 32:15 describes true believers who, when reminded of Allah's verses, fall down in prostration and glorify their Lord without arrogance.

questionEn: What practice of devoted night worshippers is praised in Surah As-Sajdah 32:16?
optionsEn: Reciting poetry until dawn
Writing down verses by candlelight
Staying awake only on the nights of full moons
Their sides forsake their beds as they invoke their Lord in fear and hope and spend in charity
explanationEn: Verse 32:16 praises those whose sides rise from their beds to supplicate to their Lord in fear and hope and who spend out of what Allah has provided them.

questionEn: What does Surah As-Sajdah 32:17 say is hidden in store for those devout night worshippers?
optionsEn: Knowledge of every past civilization
Castles made of white pearl beside the Nile
No soul knows what comfort for the eyes (qurrati a'yun) has been hidden for them
Immediate relief from all worldly hardship
explanationEn: Allah says: 'And no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do.'

questionEn: To which confederacy of forces does the title of Surah Al-Ahzab (33) refer?
optionsEn: The armies of Persia and Rome
The tribes of Thamud and 'Ad
The allied tribes and groups who besieged Madinah in the Battle of the Trench (Khandaq)
The defenders of Jerusalem
explanationEn: Al-Ahzab ('The Confederates') refers to the coalition of Quraysh and allied tribes who marched against Madinah in 5 AH during the Battle of the Trench.

questionEn: What ruling regarding adoption did Surah Al-Ahzab 33:4-5 establish?
optionsEn: Adopted children must be attributed to their biological fathers, or treated as brothers in faith and freedmen if unknown
Adoption of orphans is forbidden altogether
Adopted children must take the adoptive father's tribal name
Adopted children inherit double shares automatically
explanationEn: Allah commanded: 'Call them by [the names of] their fathers; it is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers - then they are [still] your brothers in religion and those entrusted to you.'

questionEn: What honorary status does Surah Al-Ahzab 33:6 confer upon the wives of Prophet Muhammad?
optionsEn: Judges over Madinah
Mothers of the Believers (Ummahat al-Mu'minin)
Scribes of the Revelation
Custodians of the Treasury
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ahzab 33:6 declares that the Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers (Ummahat al-Mu'minin).

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Ahzab 33:21 describe Prophet Muhammad for anyone who hopes in Allah and the Last Day?
optionsEn: An angel disguised in human form
A ruler over all kings of the earth
A miracle-worker free from all sorrow
An excellent pattern/example (uswatun hasanah)
explanationEn: Allah states: 'There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent pattern for anyone whose hope is in Allah and the Last Day and [who] remembers Allah often.'

questionEn: Which distinctive feature characterizes Surah Al-Ahzab 33:35?
optionsEn: It forbids all forms of commerce on Fridays
It lists ten paired spiritual qualities explicitly for both men and women, promising equal forgiveness and immense reward
It specifies the exact dates of the Battle of Badr and Uhud
It records the exact names of the twelve tribes of Israel
explanationEn: Verse 33:35 explicitly pairs Muslim men and women, believing men and women, obedient, truthful, patient, humble, charitable, fasting, chaste, and Allah-remembering men and women, affirming equal spiritual reward.

questionEn: Which final title of prophethood is explicitly conferred upon Prophet Muhammad in Surah Al-Ahzab 33:40?
optionsEn: Khatam an-Nabiyyin (Seal of the Prophets)
Ruhullah (Spirit from Allah)
Kalimullah (One who spoke to Allah)
Khalilullah (Friend of Allah)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ahzab 33:40 states: 'Muhammad is not the father of [any] one of your men, but [he is] the Messenger of Allah and Seal of the Prophets (Khatam an-Nabiyyin).'

questionEn: What direct obligation upon believers does Surah Al-Ahzab 33:56 command after stating that Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet?
optionsEn: To build a dome over his house
To invoke blessings and ask peace (Salawat and Salam) upon him
To travel to Makkah every spring
To fast on the Prophet's birthday
explanationEn: Allah says: 'Indeed, Allah confers blessing upon the Prophet, and His angels [ask Him to do so]. O you who have believed, ask [Allah to confer] blessing upon him and ask [Allah to grant him] peace.'

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Ahzab 33:72, how did the heavens, earth, and mountains react when Allah offered them the Trust (Al-Amanah)?
optionsEn: They immediately accepted it with joy
They declined to bear it and feared it, while mankind undertook it
They asked for forty days to deliberate
Only the mountains accepted half of it
explanationEn: Verse 33:72 explains that the heavens, earth, and mountains refused to bear the Trust out of fear of failing it, whereas man bore it.

questionEn: What metal did Allah make pliable for Prophet Dawud according to Surah Saba 34:10-11?
optionsEn: Silver
Tin
Gold
Iron
explanationEn: Allah softened iron for Dawud and instructed him to craft full coats of mail and measure the links well.

questionEn: How did the jinn working under Prophet Sulayman discover that he had passed away according to Surah Saba 34:14?
optionsEn: His crown turned to dust at midnight
A flash of lightning struck his throne
A creature of the earth (termite) gnawed away his staff until he fell
A bird announced his death from the palace roof
explanationEn: Sulayman remained leaning on his staff after death until a creature of the earth ate away the staff and he collapsed—proving the jinn had no knowledge of the Unseen.

questionEn: What disaster destroyed the two prosperous gardens of the people of Saba after they turned ungrateful in Surah Saba 34:16?
optionsEn: The flood of the dam (Sayl al-'Arim)
Seven years of frost
A swarm of locusts
A volcanic eruption
explanationEn: Because the people of Saba turned away from gratitude, Allah sent upon them Sayl al-'Arim (the devastating flood of the Ma'rib dam) and replaced their orchards with bitter fruit and tamarisk.

questionEn: To whom was Prophet Muhammad sent according to Surah Saba 34:28?
optionsEn: Solely to those living during the seventh century
Exclusively to the dwellers of Makkah and Ta'if
Only to the tribes descended from Isma'il
Universally to all mankind (kaffatan lin-nas) as a bringer of glad tidings and warner
explanationEn: Allah tells His Messenger: 'And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.'

questionEn: In the opening verse of Surah Fatir (35:1), how are angels described as messengers?
optionsEn: Living beneath the seven oceans
Possessing crowns of emerald
Possessing wings—two, three, or four
Created from pure rainwater
explanationEn: Surah Fatir praises Allah, Originator of the heavens and earth, who made the angels messengers having wings—two or three or four—and increases in creation whatever He wills.

questionEn: According to Surah Fatir 35:28, which group among Allah's servants truly fears Him in reverence?
optionsEn: Wealthy merchants
Hermits living on mountaintops
Kings and governors
Those who have knowledge (al-'ulama')
explanationEn: After mentioning the marvelous diversity in rain, fruits, mountains, and creatures, Allah states: 'Only those fear Allah, from among His servants, who have knowledge.'

questionEn: Into which three categories does Surah Fatir 35:32 divide those who inherit the Book (the Quran)?
optionsEn: Scholars, warriors, and travelers
Elders, youth, and children
Rich, middle-class, and poor
One who wrongs himself, one who is moderate, and one who is foremost in good deeds
explanationEn: Surah Fatir 35:32 states that among the inheritors of the Book are the zalimun linafsihi (wrongdoer to himself), the muqtasid (moderate), and the sabiqun bil-khayrat (foremost in good deeds by Allah's permission).

questionEn: Which core principle of individual moral accountability is affirmed in Surah Fatir 35:18?
optionsEn: Tribal chiefs answer for their entire clan's debts
Wealth can ransom a relative from punishment
Parents automatically carry half their children's sins
No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another
explanationEn: Surah Fatir 35:18 affirms: 'And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to [carry some of] its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he should be a close relative.'

questionEn: By what attribute of the Quran does Allah swear immediately after the opening letters in Surah Ya-Sin 36:1-2?
optionsEn: The Ancient Quran
The Hidden Quran
The Wise Quran (Al-Quran al-Hakim)
The Shortest Quran
explanationEn: Surah Ya-Sin opens with 'Ya-Sin. Wal-Quranil-Hakim' (By the Wise Quran), affirming that Muhammad is indeed among the messengers on a straight path.

questionEn: In the parable of the People of the Town (Ashab al-Qaryah) in Surah Ya-Sin 36:13-14, how many messengers did Allah send to them?
optionsEn: Seven messengers over seven decades
Two messengers, then reinforced them with a third
Twelve messengers at once
One messenger alone
explanationEn: Allah sent two messengers to the town, and when the townspeople denied them, Allah reinforced them with a third messenger.

questionEn: In Surah Ya-Sin 36:20-27, what did the believing man who came running from the farthest end of the city wish after he was told 'Enter Paradise'?
optionsEn: That his people could know how his Lord forgave him and placed him among the honored
That his wealth be buried with him
That his city be flooded immediately
That a monument be built in his honor
explanationEn: Even after martyrdom and entering Paradise, the sincere believer wished his people knew how Allah had forgiven him and honored him, hoping they too would be guided.

questionEn: What celestial sign does Surah Ya-Sin 36:40 mention to illustrate Allah's cosmic order?
optionsEn: The stars vanish completely during the month of Ramadan
Comets pause every seventh century above Makkah
The moon emits its own internal fire
The sun cannot overtake the moon nor the night outstrip the day, each floating in an orbit
explanationEn: Surah Ya-Sin 36:40 declares: 'It is not allowable for the sun to reach the moon, nor does the night overtake the day, but each, in an orbit, is swimming.'

questionEn: What special greeting from Allah awaits the inhabitants of Paradise according to Surah Ya-Sin 36:58?
optionsEn: 'Peace' (Salam)—a word from a Merciful Lord
'Command the angels as you wish'
'You are free from all remembrance'
'Take your thrones among the clouds'
explanationEn: Surah Ya-Sin 36:58 describes the ultimate bliss of the people of Paradise: '[And] "Peace," a word from a Merciful Lord.'

questionEn: In Surah Ya-Sin 36:65, what happens when Allah seals the mouths of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection?
optionsEn: Their scrolls burn before being read
Their shadows vanish beneath them
Their hands speak and their feet testify to what they used to earn
Their garments turn into chains of copper
explanationEn: Allah states: 'That Day, We will seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify about what they used to earn.'

questionEn: How does Surah Ya-Sin 36:78-79 answer the skeptic who crumbled an old bone and asked who could bring decayed bones back to life?
optionsEn: Through the prayers of living descendants
By transferring the soul into a newborn infant
Only after the oceans evaporate completely
He who produced them the first time will give them life, for He knows every creation
explanationEn: Allah instructed the Prophet to reply: 'He will give them life who produced them the first time; and He is, of all creation, Knowing.'

questionEn: What concise phrase in Surah Ya-Sin 36:82 expresses Allah's absolute creative command?
optionsEn: 'Rise,' and it obeys
'Be,' and it is (Kun fayakun)
'Wait,' until the appointed hour
'Flow,' as water from stone
explanationEn: Surah Ya-Sin 36:82 states: 'His command is only when He intends a thing that He says to it, "Be," and it is.'

questionEn: To whom does the title of Surah As-Saffat (37, 'Those Ranged in Ranks') primarily refer in its opening verses?
optionsEn: The angels standing in ordered ranks of worship and obedience
Roman cavalry formations
Prophets gathered in Jerusalem
Mountains lined along the Arabian coast
explanationEn: As-Saffat opens with an oath by the angels ranged in ranks (37:1), who later declare: 'And indeed, we are those who line up [for prayer/service]' (37:165).

questionEn: According to Surah As-Saffat 37:10, what pursues rebellious devils who try to eavesdrop on the highest assembly?
optionsEn: Blinding flashes of ocean lightning
Whirlwinds of desert sand
Flocks of iron-winged birds
A piercing burning flame/meteor (shihab thaqib)
explanationEn: Surah As-Saffat explains that devils cannot listen to the exalted assembly and are pelted from every side, chased by a piercing flame (shihab thaqib).

questionEn: In Surah As-Saffat 37:101-107, how did Allah reward Prophet Ibrahim and his forbearing son after both submitted to the dream of sacrifice?
optionsEn: He granted them a palace of white marble
He ransomed the son with a great sacrifice (dhibhin 'azim)
He sent rain over Makkah for forty days
He turned the knife into olive wood
explanationEn: After Ibrahim and his son submitted completely, Allah called out that Ibrahim had fulfilled the vision and ransomed the boy with a great sacrifice.

questionEn: According to Surah As-Saffat 37:143-144, why was Prophet Yunus rescued rather than remaining in the belly of the great fish until the Day of Resurrection?
optionsEn: Because fishermen caught the fish the next morning
Because an angel split the sea in half
Because he fasted for ninety days inside it
Because he was among those who glorify Allah (al-musabbihin)
explanationEn: Allah states regarding Yunus: 'And had he not been of those who exalt Allah, he would have remained inside its belly until the Day they are resurrected.'

questionEn: What plant did Allah cause to grow over Prophet Yunus to shade and shelter him after he was cast onto the barren shore in Surah As-Saffat 37:146?
optionsEn: A cedar sapling
A cluster of reeds
A gourd vine (yaqtin)
A pomegranate bush
explanationEn: When Yunus was cast out onto the open shore while ill, Allah caused a broad-leaved gourd plant (yaqtin) to grow over him.

questionEn: In Surah Sad 38:21-24, what parable did two disputants present to Prophet Dawud that moved him to seek forgiveness and fall in prostration (marked as a Sajdah in Hanafi/Maliki schools)?
optionsEn: Two brothers dividing an olive orchard
One man owning ninety-nine ewes demanding the single ewe of his brother
Two merchants arguing over a lost camel
Two builders disputing the height of a wall
explanationEn: Two litigants entered Dawud's chamber presenting the case of one with 99 ewes who demanded his brother's lone ewe; Dawud realized Allah was testing him, sought forgiveness, and fell down bowing/prostrating.

questionEn: What primary purpose for revealing the Quran is stated in Surah Sad 38:29?
optionsEn: To serve solely as an amulet for travelers
To replace all spoken poetry
That people may reflect deeply upon its verses (liyaddabbaru ayatihi) and the wise be reminded
To preserve ancient Arabian genealogies
explanationEn: Allah says: '[This is] a blessed Book which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that they might reflect upon its verses and that those of understanding would be reminded.'

questionEn: What extraordinary request did Prophet Sulayman make after repenting to Allah in Surah Sad 38:35?
optionsEn: Turn all the rivers of Syria into milk
Make me immortal until the Day of Judgment
Forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me
Give every inhabitant of Jerusalem a mountain of gold
explanationEn: Sulayman prayed: 'My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower.'

questionEn: How was Prophet Ayyub cured and enabled to fulfill his earlier oath gently according to Surah Sad 38:42-44?
optionsEn: By drinking honey brought by eagles and freeing ten captives
By striking the ground with his foot for a cool spring to bathe and drink, and striking gently with a bundle of grass/twigs
By fasting seven Mondays and donating his flock
By traveling to Mount Sinai for forty nights
explanationEn: Allah told Ayyub to strike the earth with his foot to produce a cool spring for bathing and drinking, and to take a bundle of thin stalks (dighthan) and strike with it so he would not break his oath.

questionEn: What arrogant excuse did Iblis give in Surah Sad 38:76 for refusing Allah's command to prostrate to Adam?
optionsEn: He boasted: 'I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay'
He said he had already prostrated earlier
He argued that angels should never bow to anything
He claimed he was too busy glorifying the Throne
explanationEn: Iblis replied arrogantly: 'I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay.'

questionEn: To what scene on the Day of Judgment does the title of Surah Az-Zumar (39, 'The Troops/Throngs') refer?
optionsEn: Angels descending with rainclouds
Groups of the disbelievers driven to Hell and groups of the righteous led honorably to Paradise
Roman legions marching into Arabia
Tribes competing in horse races
explanationEn: Az-Zumar ('The Crowds/Groups') takes its name from verses 71 and 73, which describe people being led in groups (zumaran) either toward Hell or toward Paradise.

questionEn: How does Surah Az-Zumar 39:6 describe the environment in which Allah fashions human beings inside their mothers' wombs?
optionsEn: Seven chambers of bone
A single layer of water
Four streams of light
Creation after creation within three darknesses (zulumatin thalath)
explanationEn: Surah Az-Zumar 39:6 states: 'He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, within three darknesses.'

questionEn: Which rhetorical question in Surah Az-Zumar 39:9 highlights the elevated status of people of knowledge?
optionsEn: Are the wealthy equal to the destitute?
Say, 'Are those who know equal to those who do not know?'
Are the swift runners equal to the stationary?
Are the kings of the earth equal to the shepherds?
explanationEn: After praising the devout night worshipper who fears the Hereafter and hopes in his Lord's mercy, Allah asks: 'Are those who know equal to those who do not know?'

questionEn: What spiritual parallel between sleep and death does Surah Az-Zumar 39:42 explain?
optionsEn: Only righteous souls leave the body during sleep
Dreaming is caused by stars passing overhead
Souls sleep for forty years before resurrection
Allah takes the souls at death, and takes the souls of those who do not die during their sleep, keeping the former and returning the latter until an appointed term
explanationEn: Surah Az-Zumar 39:42 explains that Allah takes souls at death and also takes souls during sleep—retaining those decreed to die and sending back the others until their appointed time.

questionEn: Which widely cited verse of hope in Surah Az-Zumar calls sinners back to repentance without despair?
optionsEn: Verse 29
Verse 53 ('Do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins')
Verse 18
Verse 45
explanationEn: Surah Az-Zumar 39:53 proclaims: 'Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins."'

questionEn: According to Surah Az-Zumar 39:68, what happens on the Day of Resurrection between the first and second blasts of the Trumpet?
optionsEn: Seven years of darkness pass between them
At the first blast everyone in the heavens and earth swoons except whom Allah wills; at the second they stand looking on
Mountains turn into rivers of silver
All oceans freeze solid immediately
explanationEn: Surah Az-Zumar 39:68 describes two blasts of the Trumpet: at the first, all in the heavens and earth fall dead except whom Allah wills; at the second, they stand up looking around.

questionEn: By what alternative title is Surah Ghafir (40) also famously known?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Mu'min (The Believer)
Surah An-Naba
Surah Al-Qasas
Surah Al-Mursalat
explanationEn: Surah 40 is known both as Ghafir ('The Forgiver', from 40:3) and Al-Mu'min ('The Believer', referring to the believing man of Pharaoh's household in 40:28).

questionEn: Which group of seven consecutive Surahs in the Quran begins with Surah Ghafir (40)?
optionsEn: Al-Musabbihat
Al-Hawamim (the seven Surahs opening with 'Ha-Mim')
As-Sab' at-Tiwal
Al-Mufassal
explanationEn: Surahs 40 through 46 (Ghafir, Fussilat, Ash-Shura, Az-Zukhruf, Ad-Dukhan, Al-Jathiyah, and Al-Ahqaf) all open with 'Ha-Mim' and are collectively called Al-Hawamim.

questionEn: According to Surah Ghafir 40:7, what do the angels who carry the Throne ('Arsh) and those around it supplicate for?
optionsEn: For Allah to forgive the believers and admit them and their righteous family into Gardens of Eternity
For earthly kings to conquer cities
For extra wings
For clouds to descend every hour
explanationEn: Surah Ghafir 40:7-9 reveals that the Throne-bearing angels glorify Allah, believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for the believers, praying they be admitted into Paradise along with their righteous parents, spouses, and offspring.

questionEn: With what words of complete reliance did the believing man from Pharaoh's family conclude his speech defending Prophet Musa in Surah Ghafir 40:44?
optionsEn: Wait for seventy years until help comes
Flee Egypt before morning arrives
Raise your swords against Pharaoh tonight
I entrust my affair to Allah (Ufawwidu amri ilallah); indeed, Allah is Seeing of His servants
explanationEn: After warning Pharaoh's court, the believer declared: 'And I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of [His] servants,' and Allah protected him from their evil plots.

questionEn: What direct invitation and promise does Allah give in Surah Ghafir 40:60?
optionsEn: Call upon Me; I will respond to you (Ud'uni astajib lakum)
Fast half of every year
Build mosques in every valley
Travel to Madinah on foot
explanationEn: Allah commands: 'And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you." Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell [rendered] contemptible.'

questionEn: What does the name of Surah Fussilat (41) mean, and by what alternate name is it also known?
optionsEn: 'The Smoke'; also called Ash-Shura
'The Stars'; also called Al-Fajr
'The Iron'; also called Al-Qital
'Explained in Detail'; also called Ha-Mim As-Sajdah
explanationEn: Fussilat means 'Explained in Detail' (from 41:3), and the Surah is also widely called Ha-Mim As-Sajdah because it opens with Ha-Mim and contains a Sajdah verse.

questionEn: In Surah Fussilat 41:20-21, what surprises the enemies of Allah when they are gathered at the Fire?
optionsEn: Their shadows run away from them
Their own hearing, sight, and skins testify against them
Their wealth turns into scorpions
Their horses speak against them
explanationEn: Surah Fussilat 41:20-21 describes how their hearing, eyes, and skins testify against what they did; when asked why, their skins reply: 'Allah gave us speech, Who gives speech to all things.'

questionEn: What transformative outcome does Surah Fussilat 41:34 say follows when a believer repels evil with what is better?
optionsEn: Someone between whom and you there was enmity becomes like a devoted close friend
Angels write your name on the Kaaba
The wrongdoer immediately leaves the city
All past debts are legally cancelled
explanationEn: Allah teaches: 'Good and evil are not equal. Repel [evil] by that [deed] which is better; and thereupon the one whom between you and him is enmity [will become] as though he was a devoted friend.'

questionEn: What command in Surah Fussilat 41:37-38 accompanies the verse of Sajdah al-Tilawah?
optionsEn: Bow toward Jerusalem during eclipses
Prostrate only once a year in Ramadan
Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah who created them
Prostrate toward the rising sun at dawn
explanationEn: Surah Fussilat 41:37-38 states that night, day, the sun, and the moon are among Allah's signs, commanding: 'Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them.'

questionEn: Where does Allah promise to show humanity His signs in Surah Fussilat 41:53 until the truth becomes clear?
optionsEn: Exclusively during total solar eclipses
In the horizons (al-afaq) and within themselves
Solely on ancient tablets of stone
Only inside the Cave of Hira
explanationEn: Allah declares: 'We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth.'

questionEn: How are the opening Huruf Muqatta'at structured uniquely in Surah Ash-Shura (42)?
optionsEn: As a single one-letter verse
Repeated at the end of every ten verses
Hidden inside the last verse
Split across the first two verses: 'Ha-Mim' (42:1) and ''Ayn-Sin-Qaf' (42:2)
explanationEn: Surah Ash-Shura is unique in having five Muqatta'at letters split into two separate verses: 'Ha-Mim' in 42:1 and ''Ayn-Sin-Qaf' in 42:2.

questionEn: Which foundational creed statement on Allah's absolute transcendence appears in Surah Ash-Shura 42:11?
optionsEn: He dwells inside every mountain peak
He shares authority with the stars
He rests on the seventh day
There is nothing like unto Him (Laysa kamithlihi shay'un), and He is the Hearing, the Seeing
explanationEn: Surah Ash-Shura 42:11 affirms Allah's utter transcendence alongside His attributes: 'There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.'

questionEn: Which principle of communal decision-making gives Surah Ash-Shura (42) its name in verse 38?
optionsEn: Silent obedience without discussion
Matters of the believers are conducted by mutual consultation among themselves (wa amruhum shura baynahum)
Unilateral decree by tribal elders
Drawing lots before every journey
explanationEn: Surah Ash-Shura 42:38 praises those who respond to their Lord, establish prayer, and 'whose affair is [determined by] consultation among themselves.'

questionEn: According to Surah Ash-Shura 42:51, what are the only three ways Allah speaks to any human being?
optionsEn: By revelation (wahy), from behind a veil (hijab), or by sending an angelic messenger
Through fire, thunder, or ocean tides
Through priests, kings, or poets
Through dreams, omens, or astrology
explanationEn: Surah Ash-Shura 42:51 specifies: 'And it is not for any human being that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a partition or that He sends a messenger to reveal, by His permission, what He wills.'

questionEn: According to Surah Ash-Shura 42:30, what is the source of hardships that strike people, and how does Allah temper them?
optionsEn: Random misfortune with no moral meaning
Punishment only for prophets
Purely the movement of constellations
What people's own hands have earned, while Allah pardons much
explanationEn: Allah states: 'And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned; but He pardons much.'

questionEn: What does the name of Surah Az-Zukhruf (43) mean?
optionsEn: The Ornaments of Gold
The Rising Smoke
The Clear Victory
The Winding Sandhills
explanationEn: Az-Zukhruf means 'The Ornaments of Gold', referring to verse 43:35 which notes that gold adornments are merely transient enjoyment of worldly life.

questionEn: Which well-known Sunnah supplication for mounting a riding animal or vehicle is taken directly from Surah Az-Zukhruf 43:13-14?
optionsEn: 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim, tawakkaltu 'alallah'
'Subhanal-ladhi sakhkhara lana hadha wa ma kunna lahu muqrinin, wa inna ila Rabbina lamunqalibun'
'Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal-wakil'
'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah'
explanationEn: Surah Az-Zukhruf 43:13-14 teaches believers to say when settled upon mounts/ships: 'Exalted is He who has subjected this to us, and we could not have [otherwise] subdued it. And indeed we, to our Lord, will surely return.'

questionEn: What will happen to close worldly friendships on the Day of Resurrection according to Surah Az-Zukhruf 43:67?
optionsEn: They will share equal shares of wealth
Close friends will become enemies to one another, except for the righteous (al-muttaqin)
They will all enter Paradise together regardless of faith
They will forget one another's names completely
explanationEn: Surah Az-Zukhruf 43:67 warns: 'Close friends, that Day, will be enemies to each other, except for the righteous.'

questionEn: What is the name of the angel in charge of Hell whom the inhabitants of the Fire cry out to in Surah Az-Zukhruf 43:77?
optionsEn: Malik
Ridwan
Israfil
Mika'il
explanationEn: Surah Az-Zukhruf 43:77 records the doomed calling out: 'O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!'—to which Malik replies, 'Indeed, you will remain.'

questionEn: Why did Allah explain in Surah Az-Zukhruf 43:35 that He did not give disbelievers houses with silver roofs and golden ornaments only lest all mankind become disbelievers?
optionsEn: Because gold cannot be mined in Arabia
Because all such gold and silver are merely fleeting enjoyment of worldly life, while the Hereafter with Allah belongs to the righteous
Because angels forbade silver roofs on earth
Because silver dissolves in rainwater
explanationEn: Verses 43:33-35 emphasize how worthless worldly luxury is in Allah's sight: had it not risked tempting all mankind into disbelief, He would have given disbelievers silver roofs and golden ornaments, for the Hereafter belongs to the righteous.

questionEn: What does Surah Ad-Dukhan 44:3-4 say occurred on a 'blessed night' (Laylatun Mubarakah)?
optionsEn: The Kaaba was first constructed
Allah sent down the Quran, and on that night every wise matter is made distinct
Pharaoh freed the Children of Israel
Prophet Nuh completed building the Ark
explanationEn: Surah Ad-Dukhan opens by swearing by the clear Book: 'Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night (Laylat al-Qadr)... On that night is made distinct every precise matter.'

questionEn: What terrifying sign does Surah Ad-Dukhan 44:10-11 warn the disbelievers to watch out for?
optionsEn: A sudden freezing of all oceans
The Day when the sky brings forth a visible smoke (dukhan mubin) covering the people
A rain of burning meteorites
The collapse of all mountains into sand
explanationEn: Surah Ad-Dukhan takes its name from 44:10: 'Then watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke covering the people; this is a painful torment.'

questionEn: In Surah Ad-Dukhan 44:43-46, what is described as the food of the sinful in Hell, boiling in their bellies like scalding water?
optionsEn: Salted sand
Bitter locusts
Crushed charcoal
The Tree of Zaqqum, like murky molten oil
explanationEn: Surah Ad-Dukhan 44:43-46 describes the Tree of Zaqqum as the food of the sinful, resembling murky oil boiling inside bellies like scalding water.

questionEn: With what two types of fine silk garments does Surah Ad-Dukhan 44:53 describe the righteous dressed in Paradise?
optionsEn: Wool and linen
Silver mesh and leather
Red velvet and woven palm fiber
Fine silk (sundus) and thick brocade (istabraq)
explanationEn: Surah Ad-Dukhan 44:53 describes the righteous in gardens and springs 'wearing [garments of] fine silk and brocade, facing each other.'

questionEn: What image on the Day of Judgment gives Surah Al-Jathiyah (45, 'The Kneeling') its name in verse 28?
optionsEn: Kings bowing before prophets
Mountains kneeling toward Makkah
Every nation seen kneeling on its knees as each is called to its record
Angels kneeling at the gates of Paradise
explanationEn: Verse 45:28 depicts the awe of Judgment Day: 'And you will see every nation kneeling [from fear]. Every nation will be called to its record.'

questionEn: What spiritual danger does Surah Al-Jathiyah 45:23 warn about regarding a person who worships their own whims?
optionsEn: Worshipping fire inside temples
Consulting fortune-tellers before travel
Taking one's own desire (hawahu) as a god, causing Allah to leave him astray despite knowledge
Taking wealth as an idol
explanationEn: Allah asks: 'Have you seen he who has taken as his god his [own] desire, and Allah has sent him astray due to knowledge and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart...?'

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Jathiyah 45:24 quote the deniers of Resurrection who attribute death solely to nature?
optionsEn: 'Only kings live forever'
'Our souls dissolve into wind'
'There is not but our worldly life; we die and live, and nothing destroys us except time (ad-dahr)'
'The stars control our fates'
explanationEn: Surah Al-Jathiyah 45:24 quotes the materialists saying: 'There is not but our worldly life; we die and live, and nothing destroys us except time.'

questionEn: What does Surah Al-Jathiyah 45:21 reject regarding the assumption that evildoers and righteous believers will receive the same outcome?
optionsEn: Whether those who commit evils think Allah will make them equal in life and death to those who believe and do righteous deeds
Whether gold and silver have equal value in charity
Whether angels and jinn share the same reward
Whether prayer at home equals prayer in Makkah
explanationEn: Verse 45:21 asks: 'Or do those who commit evils think We will make them like those who have believed and done righteous deeds - [make them] equal in their life and their death? Evil is that which they judge.'

questionEn: What does the name 'Al-Ahqaf' (Surah 46) refer to?
optionsEn: The curved sandhills / winding sand-tracts where Prophet Hud warned the people of 'Ad
The basalt plains of Ethiopia
The coral reefs of the Red Sea
The high mountains of northern Syria
explanationEn: Al-Ahqaf ('The Curved Sandhills') was the sandy region in southern Arabia inhabited by the people of 'Ad, to whom Prophet Hud was sent (46:21).

questionEn: Which position does Surah Al-Ahqaf (46) hold within the 'Hawamim' group of Surahs?
optionsEn: It is not part of the Hawamim
The first Surah of the Hawamim
The seventh and final Surah of the Hawamim
The middle Surah of the Hawamim
explanationEn: Surahs 40 through 46 all begin with 'Ha-Mim', making Surah Al-Ahqaf (46) the seventh and concluding Surah of the Hawamim.

questionEn: What total duration does Surah Al-Ahqaf 46:15 state for carrying a child in the womb and weaning them?
optionsEn: Thirty months
Twelve months
Twenty-four months
Eighteen months
explanationEn: Verse 46:15 states that the mother carries him with hardship and gives birth with hardship, and 'his gestation and weaning [period] is thirty months.'

questionEn: At what age of full maturity does Surah Al-Ahqaf 46:15 mention a righteous person making a special prayer of gratitude for himself, his parents, and his descendants?
optionsEn: Sixty years
Forty years
Twenty-five years
Fifty years
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ahqaf 46:15 describes one who reaches full strength and reaches forty years saying: 'My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents...'

questionEn: What remarkable event involving unseen listeners is recounted in Surah Al-Ahqaf 46:29-31?
optionsEn: Angels spoke aloud in the marketplace of Ukaz
Desert stones echoed the Adhan across Makkah
Birds memorized the entire Surah in one night
A group of jinn listened quietly to the Prophet reciting the Quran and returned to their people as warners
explanationEn: Allah directed a group of jinn to listen to the Prophet's recitation; when it ended, they returned to their people calling them to answer Allah's caller.

questionEn: What alternate name is also given to Surah Muhammad (47)?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Qital (The Fighting)
Surah Al-Hijrah
Surah As-Salam
Surah Al-Bayan
explanationEn: Surah Muhammad (47) is a Madani Surah also known as Surah Al-Qital because it addresses regulations and steadfastness in defensive combat.

questionEn: What conditional promise does Allah make to the believers in Surah Muhammad 47:7?
optionsEn: If you migrate westward, you will find hidden gold
If you support Allah (His cause), He will support you and plant firmly your feet
If you build seven mosques, your cities will never flood
If you fast forty days, you will never feel thirst
explanationEn: Allah promises: 'O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet.'

questionEn: Which four rivers of Paradise are contrasted in Surah Muhammad 47:15?
optionsEn: Date syrup, honey, river water, and musk
Olive oil, rosewater, grape juice, and spring water
Unaltered water, milk whose taste never changes, wine delicious to drinkers, and purified honey
Snowmelt, pomegranate nectar, milk, and ginger water
explanationEn: Verse 47:15 describes Paradise as containing rivers of water unaltered, rivers of milk of which the taste never changes, rivers of wine delicious to those who drink, and rivers of purified honey.

questionEn: What piercing question does Surah Muhammad 47:24 ask those who fail to ponder the Quran?
optionsEn: Did the messengers speak in a foreign tongue?
Have they forgotten how to write Arabic?
Have their eyes been blinded by desert dust?
Then do they not reflect upon the Quran, or are there locks upon [their] hearts?
explanationEn: Allah challenges: 'Then do they not reflect upon the Quran, or are there locks upon [their] hearts?'

questionEn: After which major event in 6 AH was Surah Al-Fath (48, 'The Victory') revealed, calling it a 'clear victory'?
optionsEn: The Battle of Badr
The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
The Farewell Pilgrimage
The Battle of Hunayn
explanationEn: Surah Al-Fath was revealed as Prophet Muhammad and the Companions were returning from the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, declaring that truce to be 'a clear victory.'

questionEn: What gift did Allah send down into the hearts of the believers according to Surah Al-Fath 48:4 so they might grow in faith?
optionsEn: Knowledge of hidden springs
Visions of future empires
Tranquility (as-sakinah)
Immunity from hunger
explanationEn: Allah says: 'It is He who sent down tranquility (as-sakinah) into the hearts of the believers that they would increase in faith along with their [present] faith.'

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Fath 48:10 describe the pledge of allegiance given to Prophet Muhammad by the Companions?
optionsEn: It binds only the elders of Madinah
It is a temporary commercial contract
Those who pledge allegiance to him are pledging allegiance to Allah, and the hand of Allah is over their hands
It expires after twelve lunar months
