explanationEn: Verse 48:10 affirms: 'Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, [O Muhammad] - they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands.'

questionEn: Which famous pledge at Hudaybiyyah is honored in Surah Al-Fath 48:18, where Allah declared He was pleased with the believers?
optionsEn: Bay'at ar-Ridwan (the Pledge under the Tree)
The Truce of Khaybar
The Pact of the Confederates
The First Pledge of Aqabah
explanationEn: Surah Al-Fath 48:18 states: 'Certainly was Allah pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you, [O Muhammad], under the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts.'

questionEn: Where did Surah Al-Fath 48:24 note that Allah restrained the hands of enemies from the believers and the believers' hands from them?
optionsEn: Outside the gates of Ta'if
In the valley/interior of Makkah (batni Makkah)
At the pass of Uhud
On the shore of Badr
explanationEn: Verse 48:24 reminds the believers that it was Allah who withheld their hands from each other in the interior of Makkah (at Hudaybiyyah) after giving them victory.

questionEn: What vision of Prophet Muhammad did Allah confirm would be fulfilled in truth in Surah Al-Fath 48:27?
optionsEn: Finding the lost ring of Sulayman
Entering Al-Masjid al-Haram safely with heads shaved and hair shortened, without fear
Seeing Jerusalem rebuilt in gold
Crossing the Red Sea with ships
explanationEn: Surah Al-Fath 48:27 assured the believers that the Prophet's dream of entering Al-Masjid al-Haram in safety—shaving and shortening hair after Umrah—would certainly come true.

questionEn: In the concluding verse of Surah Al-Fath (48:29), what agricultural simile from the Gospel is used for the Companions of the Prophet?
optionsEn: A plant shoot that puts forth its sprout, strengthens itself, becomes thick, and stands firmly on its stem, delighting the sowers
Wheat harvested before the summer sun
A dry vine revived by winter hail
A palm tree bent by coastal gales
explanationEn: Verse 48:29 describes the Companions' likeness in the Gospel as 'a plant which produces its offshoots and strengthens them so they grow firm and stand upon their stalks, delighting the sowers.'

questionEn: To what do the opening verses of Surah Al-Hujurat (49, 'The Private Chambers') relate?
optionsEn: Reverent etiquette toward the Prophet—not speaking ahead of him, not raising voices above his, and not calling him from behind the private chambers
Dividing inheritance shares among cousins
Building walls around the mosque courtyard
Designating land boundaries in Khaybar
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hujurat opens (49:1-5) by teaching Muslims proper respect toward the Messenger: not putting themselves forward before Allah and His Messenger, lowering their voices in his presence, and waiting patiently outside his private chambers.

questionEn: What rule of information ethics does Surah Al-Hujurat 49:6 establish when a wicked or unreliable person (fasiq) brings news?
optionsEn: Accept it immediately if three people repeat it
Spread it quietly to warn neighbors
Punish the messenger before checking the facts
Verify and investigate it carefully (fatabayyanu) lest you harm a people out of ignorance
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hujurat 49:6 commands: 'O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful.'

questionEn: When two groups of believers fight each other, what obligation does Surah Al-Hujurat 49:9-10 place on the wider Muslim community?
optionsEn: Wait until one side surrenders unconditionally
Make peace between them; if one persists in aggression, restrain it until it returns to Allah's command, then reconcile with justice
Stay completely neutral without intervening
Side automatically with the larger tribe
explanationEn: Verses 49:9-10 instruct believers to reconcile fighting Muslim factions, resist the aggressor if it refuses peace until it submits to Allah's decree, and then settle justly because 'the believers are but brothers.'

questionEn: Which three interpersonal harms are explicitly prohibited in Surah Al-Hujurat 49:11?
optionsEn: Debating poetry, singing at weddings, and wearing dyed cloth
Borrowing tools, trading at night, and traveling alone
Raising cattle, planting palms, and building two-story homes
Mocking one another, defaming one another, and calling one another by offensive nicknames
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hujurat 49:11 forbids men and women from ridiculing others, defaming one another, and insulting one another with offensive nicknames (al-alqab).

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hujurat 49:12, to what repulsive act does Allah compare backbiting (ghibah) against a fellow believer?
optionsEn: Eating the flesh of one's dead brother
Drinking stagnant swamp water
Spitting toward the heavens
Stealing bread from an orphan
explanationEn: After forbidding excessive suspicion and spying, 49:12 warns: 'And do not backbite each other. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it.'

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Hujurat 49:13, why did Allah create humanity into nations and tribes, and what alone determines nobility in His sight?
optionsEn: So languages remain isolated; nobility is wealth
So cities can collect tribute; nobility is military strength
So stronger tribes may rule weaker ones; nobility is lineage
So people may come to know one another; the most noble in Allah's sight is the most righteous (atqakum)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hujurat 49:13 declares that Allah created mankind from male and female and made them peoples and tribes 'that you may know one another,' affirming that 'the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you.'

questionEn: How did Surah Al-Hujurat 49:14 correct the Bedouins who claimed, 'We have believed (amanna)'?
optionsEn: It ordered them to memorize thirty chapters first
It told them belief requires migrating to Syria
It instructed the Prophet to tell them: 'You have not [yet] believed; rather say, "We have submitted (aslamna)," for faith has not yet entered your hearts'
It praised them as the highest ranking companions
explanationEn: Verse 49:14 draws a clear distinction between outward submission (Islam) and deep inward conviction (Iman), telling the Bedouins to say 'Aslamna' until true faith enters their hearts.

questionEn: Why did Surah Al-Hujurat 49:17 remind those same Bedouins not to consider their acceptance of Islam a favor done to Prophet Muhammad?
optionsEn: Because they had paid too little zakah
Rather, Allah has conferred a favor upon them by guiding them to faith, if they are truthful
Because only scholars may speak of favors
Because they arrived after the conquest of Makkah
explanationEn: Allah clarified in 49:17: 'They consider it a favor to you that they have accepted Islam. Say, "Do not consider your Islam a favor to me. Rather, Allah has conferred favor upon you that He has guided you to the faith, if you should be truthful."'

questionEn: How did the Companion Umm Hisham bint Harithah report that she memorized Surah Qaf (50)?
optionsEn: From a parchment sent to Abyssinia
During the night journey to Ta'if
Directly from hearing Prophet Muhammad recite it repeatedly from the pulpit during Friday sermons
From angels reciting at the Battle of Badr
explanationEn: Sahih Muslim records Umm Hisham bint Harithah saying she memorized Surah Qaf only from the tongue of the Messenger of Allah, who used to recite it every Friday on the pulpit when addressing the people.

questionEn: What vivid metaphor does Surah Qaf 50:16 use to express Allah's intimate awareness of every human soul's whispers?
optionsEn: Closer to him than his jugular vein (hablil-warid)
Closer than the roof above his head
Closer than the horizon at dawn
Closer than the shadow at noon
explanationEn: Surah Qaf 50:16 declares: 'And We have already created man and know what his soul whispers to him, and We are closer to him than [his] jugular vein.'

questionEn: According to Surah Qaf 50:17-18, what accompanies every spoken word a person utters?
optionsEn: An echo recorded in stone
A flash of light invisible to mortals
A wind that carries it across seven skies
Two receivers seated on the right and left, with an observer ready to record (Raqib 'Atid)
explanationEn: Verses 50:17-18 explain that two recording angels sit on the right and the left, and 'man does not utter any word except that with him is an observer prepared [to record].'

questionEn: In Surah Qaf 50:30, how does Hell respond on the Day of Judgment when Allah asks it, 'Have you been filled?'
optionsEn: 'Yes, close the gates forever'
'Are there any more?' (Hal min mazid)
'I am too full to hold another soul'
'Only the kings remain outside'
explanationEn: Surah Qaf 50:30 depicts the terrifying vastness of Hell: 'On the Day We will say to Hell, "Have you been filled?" and it will say, "Are there some more?"'

questionEn: Which two times of the day does Surah Qaf 50:39 highlight for glorifying Allah with praise?
optionsEn: Only after the Friday congregation
Before the rising of the sun and before its setting
Midday and midnight
At first starlight and third watch of the night
explanationEn: Allah counsels the Prophet in 50:39: 'So be patient over what they say and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting.'

questionEn: What do the opening oaths of Surah Adh-Dhariyat (51:1-4) swear by?
optionsEn: Swords, shields, horses, and banners
Winnowing winds, rain-laden clouds, smoothly sailing ships, and angels distributing commands
Rivers, forests, mountains, and valleys
Gold, silver, pearls, and coral
explanationEn: Surah Adh-Dhariyat opens by swearing by the winds that scatter dust, the clouds carrying heavy rain, the ships gliding swiftly with ease, and the angels who apportion affairs by command.

questionEn: What meal did Prophet Ibrahim quickly prepare for his honored angelic guests in Surah Adh-Dhariyat 51:26?
optionsEn: Barley bread and goat milk
Fresh dates and spring water
Grilled fish and olives
A roasted fattened calf ('ijl samin)
explanationEn: Showing exemplary hospitality, Ibrahim slipped away quietly to his family and brought out a roasted fattened calf for his guests.

questionEn: How does Surah Adh-Dhariyat 51:47 describe Allah's construction and ongoing attribute regarding the heaven/cosmos?
optionsEn: 'And the heaven We painted with falling stars'
'And the heaven We sealed until the end of winter'
'And the heaven We built of seven iron pillars'
'And the heaven We constructed with strength, and indeed, We are [its] expander (lamusi'un)'
explanationEn: Surah Adh-Dhariyat 51:47 states: 'And the heaven We constructed with strength, and indeed, We are [its] expander.'

questionEn: What ultimate purpose for the creation of jinn and mankind is declared in Surah Adh-Dhariyat 51:56?
optionsEn: Except to worship Me (liya'budun)
To build enduring stone cities
To count the stars of the night sky
To conquer the seven seas
explanationEn: Verse 51:56 states concisely: 'And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.'

questionEn: What is 'Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur' (the Frequented House), sworn by in Surah At-Tur 52:4?
optionsEn: The celestial sanctuary in the seventh heaven directly above the Kaaba, entered daily by 70,000 angels
The cave where the Prophet first received revelation
The ancient mosque of Quba
The palace of Sulayman in Jerusalem
explanationEn: In Surah At-Tur 52:4 Allah swears by Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur, which the Prophet explained in Hadith al-Mi'raj (Bukhari & Muslim) is in the seventh heaven entered daily by 70,000 angels who never return to it.

questionEn: What heartwarming blessing of family reunion in Paradise does Surah At-Tur 52:21 promise?
optionsEn: Tribes gather once a year in valleys of musk
Merchants reunite with their business partners
Neighbors from the same street share one palace
Believing descendants who followed their parents in faith will be joined with them in rank without reducing the parents' reward
explanationEn: Surah At-Tur 52:21 promises: 'And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith - We will join with them their descendants, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds.'

questionEn: Which logical challenge in Surah At-Tur 52:35 profoundly shook Jubayr ibn Mut'im when he heard Prophet Muhammad recite it in Maghrib prayer?
optionsEn: 'Why do the stars shine only at night?'
'Who taught the birds to build nests?'
'Or were they created by nothing, or were they the creators [of themselves]?'
'How can iron sink in water while wood floats?'
explanationEn: Sahih al-Bukhari narrates that Jubayr ibn Mut'im said his heart almost took flight when he heard the Prophet recite 52:35-37, questioning whether humans were created out of nothing or created themselves.

questionEn: What reassuring words does Allah speak to Prophet Muhammad in Surah At-Tur 52:48 while commanding patience?
optionsEn: 'Silence them with a single thunderbolt'
'Leave Makkah tonight without informing anyone'
'Indeed, you are in Our eyes (bi-a'yunina), and exalt [Allah] with praise when you arise'
'Your enemies will depart before sunrise'
explanationEn: Allah comforts His Messenger: 'And be patient, [O Muhammad], for the decision of your Lord, for indeed, you are in Our eyes. And exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord when you arise.'

questionEn: What historic reaction occurred in Makkah when Prophet Muhammad recited Surah An-Najm (53) up to its concluding Sajdah verse (53:62)?
optionsEn: A sandstorm stopped the recitation midway
Only the women prostrated while the men stood
Everyone walked out in silence before verse 30
Both the Muslims and the polytheists present fell down in prostration together, overcome by its majesty
explanationEn: Sahih al-Bukhari reports that Surah An-Najm was the first Surah revealed containing a Sajdah verse (53:62); when the Prophet prostrated at its end, everyone present—Muslims and polytheists alike—prostrated except one arrogant elder who lifted dust to his forehead.

questionEn: How does Surah An-Najm 53:3-4 testify to the absolute truthfulness of Prophet Muhammad's prophetic speech?
optionsEn: He wrote down his dreams in poetry
He consulted elders before speaking
Nor does he speak from his own inclination; it is not but a revelation revealed
He studied the stars every evening
explanationEn: After swearing by the star when it descends, Allah affirms of His Messenger: 'Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination. It is not but a revelation revealed.'

questionEn: What landmark at the boundary of the highest heavens did Prophet Muhammad witness during his Night Ascent, as mentioned in Surah An-Najm 53:14-15?
optionsEn: A golden gate inscribed with tribal names
Sidrat al-Muntaha (the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary), near which is the Garden of Refuge
The sunken palace of Pharaoh
A crystal bridge spanning seven oceans
explanationEn: Surah An-Najm 53:13-16 recounts that the Prophet saw Jibril another time 'at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha); near it is the Garden of Refuge.'

questionEn: What principle of personal moral effort and accountability is stated in Surah An-Najm 53:39?
optionsEn: Wealth earned by ancestors automatically saves descendants
Only scholars receive credit for good intentions
And that there is not for man except that [good] for which he strives
Charity counts only when given in silver
explanationEn: Following the reminder that no bearer of burdens bears another's burden, verse 53:39 declares: 'And that there is not for man except that [good] for which he strives.'

questionEn: Which bright star worshipped by some pagan Arabs is explicitly named in Surah An-Najm 53:49 to affirm Allah's sole Lordship over it?
optionsEn: Aldebaran
Polaris
Sirius (Ash-Shi'ra)
Canopus
explanationEn: Surah An-Najm 53:49 declares: 'And that it is He who is the Lord of Sirius (Rabbush-Shi'ra),' refuting those who venerated the star.

questionEn: Which physical miracle witnessed by the Makkans is announced in the opening verse of Surah Al-Qamar (54:1)?
optionsEn: The Hour has come near, and the moon has split in two
All idols falling face-down inside the Kaaba
Water gushing from Mount Safa
The sun standing still at midday
explanationEn: Surah Al-Qamar opens with: 'The Hour has come near, and the moon has split [in two],' referring to the miracle of Inshiqaq al-Qamar shown to Quraysh.

questionEn: Which encouraging verse is repeated four times across Surah Al-Qamar (54:17, 22, 32, 40) after accounts of past nations?
optionsEn: 'To Allah belongs the east and the west'
'Every soul shall taste death'
'Indeed, Allah is with the patient'
'And We have certainly made the Quran easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?'
explanationEn: Four times in Surah Al-Qamar, Allah reminds humanity: 'Wa laqad yassarnal-Qurana lidh-dhikri fahal min muddakir' (And We have certainly made the Quran easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?).

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Qamar 54:50 illustrate the instantaneous execution of Allah's decree?
optionsEn: Written on parchment before sunrise
Slow as the growth of an oak tree
But one command, like a glance of the eye (kalamhin bil-basar)
Measured across seven lunar months
explanationEn: Surah Al-Qamar 54:50 affirms: 'And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye.'

questionEn: In what honored setting does the concluding verse of Surah Al-Qamar (54:54-55) place the righteous?
optionsEn: Sailing across calm blue seas
Standing at the edge of the desert
Among gardens and rivers, in a seat of honor near a Sovereign, Perfect in Ability
Guarding ancient stone gates
explanationEn: Surah Al-Qamar ends with the serene promise: 'Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and rivers, in a seat of honor near a Sovereign, Perfect in Ability.'

questionEn: What unique opening distinction belongs to Surah Ar-Rahman (55) among all 114 Surahs of the Quran?
optionsEn: It contains three Sajdah verses
It is the only Surah that begins directly with one of Allah's Beautiful Names ('Ar-Rahman')
It opens with five Muqatta'at letters
It is the longest Surah in Madani revelation
explanationEn: Surah Ar-Rahman is the only Surah in the entire Quran whose very first word/verse is solely one of the Beautiful Names of Allah: 'Ar-Rahman' (The Most Merciful).

questionEn: Which Companion's plea to the Prophet ﷺ regarding her husband's declaration of dhihar prompted the revelation of the opening verses of Surah Al-Mujadila?
optionsEn: Khawlah bint Tha'labah
Umm Salamah
Nusaybah bint Ka'b
Asma' bint Abi Bakr
explanationEn: Khawlah bint Tha'labah complained to the Prophet ﷺ after her husband Aws ibn as-Samit pronounced dhihar, and Allah heard her plea from above the seven heavens.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Mujadila, by which two traits does Allah raise believers in degrees?
optionsEn: Age and status
Wealth and lineage
Faith and knowledge
Strength and eloquence
explanationEn: Surah Al-Mujadila states that Allah raises in degrees those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mujadila, what etiquette is commanded when believers are told to make room in assemblies?
optionsEn: Make room so Allah will make room for you
Leave immediately after speaking
Sit strictly according to tribe
Stand in silence until addressed
explanationEn: Allah instructs believers that when told to make room in gatherings, they should make room, and Allah will make room for them in His mercy and Paradise.

questionEn: What does Surah Al-Mujadila declare regarding private consultations (najwa) of three or five people?
optionsEn: Allah is the fourth of three and the sixth of five
They are prohibited in every circumstance
Only prophets are aware of them
Angels record them only at night
explanationEn: Allah affirms His all-encompassing knowledge, stating there is no secret counsel of three except He is the fourth, nor of five except He is the sixth.

questionEn: Which group does Surah Al-Mujadila describe at its conclusion as 'the successful ones' (al-muflihun)?
optionsEn: Those who debate endlessly
Hizbullah (the Party of Allah)
The inhabitants of Madinah alone
Those who amass charity without prayer
explanationEn: The closing verse of Surah Al-Mujadila states that those loyal to Allah and His Messenger are the Party of Allah, and indeed the Party of Allah are the successful.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Hashr, why did Allah decree that fay' (booty gained without fighting) be distributed to specific needy categories?
optionsEn: So it would fund fortress construction
To reward poets of Madinah
So wealth does not circulate solely among the rich
To pay tribute to neighboring tribes
explanationEn: Allah explicitly states the economic wisdom of fay' distribution: 'so that it will not be a perpetual distribution among the rich from among you.'

questionEn: Which remarkable quality of the Ansar is praised in Surah Al-Hashr 59:9?
optionsEn: Preferring the Muhajirin over themselves despite their own need
Memorizing every scroll of earlier nations
Building the first naval fleet
Fasting every alternate day
explanationEn: Allah praises the Ansar for giving preference (ithar) to their brothers over themselves even when they themselves were in privation.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hashr, what parable illustrates the awe and weight of the Qur'an?
optionsEn: A seed sprouting seven hundred ears
A mountain humbling itself and splitting apart out of fear of Allah
A lightning bolt illuminating the horizon
An ocean parting before a staff
explanationEn: Allah states that had He sent this Qur'an down upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and splitting asunder out of fear of Allah.

questionEn: Which three Names of Allah appear together in Surah Al-Hashr 59:24 describing His creative perfection?
optionsEn: Al-Ghafur, Ar-Rahim, Al-Wadud
Al-Khaliq, Al-Bari', Al-Musawwir
Al-Awwal, Al-Akhir, Az-Zahir
As-Sami', Al-Basir, Al-Khabir
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hashr 59:24 concludes the majestic passage of Divine Names with Al-Khaliq (the Creator), Al-Bari' (the Inventor), and Al-Musawwir (the Fashioner).

questionEn: What does Surah Al-Hashr warn believers against forgetting in verse 19, leading Allah to make them forget their own souls?
optionsEn: Allah Himself
The laws of trade
The lunar calendar
Their ancestral lineage
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hashr 59:19 warns: 'And be not like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.'

questionEn: What does Surah Al-Mumtahanah 60:8 permit and encourage regarding non-Muslims who neither fight believers over religion nor expel them from their homes?
optionsEn: Forbidding any conversation with them
Boycotting their markets
Requiring them to migrate elsewhere
Treating them kindly (birr) and justly (qist)
explanationEn: Allah clarifies that He does not forbid believers from showing kindness and dealing justly with those who do not fight them for religion or drive them from their homes.

questionEn: Why does the title 'Al-Mumtahanah' (She Who Is Tested) apply to Surah 60?
optionsEn: It recounts the trial of Prophet Ayyub
It refers to testing gold and silver in fire
It describes the testing of angels before Adam's creation
It commands examining the sincerity of believing women migrating to Madinah
explanationEn: Verse 10 instructs believers to examine (test) believing women who migrate from Makkah so they are not returned to disbelieving husbands if their faith is sincere.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mumtahanah, which aspect of Prophet Ibrahim's (AS) conduct are believers told NOT to imitate?
optionsEn: His seeking forgiveness for his polytheist father after it became clear he was an enemy to Allah
His patience in the fire
His rebuilding of the Ka'bah
His hospitality toward strangers
explanationEn: Surah Al-Mumtahanah 60:4 presents Ibrahim (AS) and those with him as an excellent example, except his saying to his father, 'I will surely ask forgiveness for you.'

questionEn: Which of the following is explicitly included in the pledge of allegiance of believing women in Surah Al-Mumtahanah 60:12?
optionsEn: Traveling to Jerusalem annually
Memorizing half the Qur'an
Not associating anything with Allah, not stealing, and not committing unlawful sexual intercourse
Leading armies in battle
explanationEn: Verse 12 details the pledge taken from believing women: not committing shirk, not stealing, not committing zina, not killing children, not fabricating slander, and not disobeying in what is right.

questionEn: What strong rebuke opens Surah As-Saff regarding speech and action?
optionsEn: Saying what you do not do
Speaking loudly in the mosque
Speaking in poetry
Debating without books
explanationEn: Allah asks believers why they say what they do not do, stating it is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah to say what one does not practice.

questionEn: How does Surah As-Saff 61:4 describe those whom Allah loves when they strive in His cause?
optionsEn: Like solitary peaks in the desert
Like rivers flowing separately to the sea
In ranks as though they were a firmly cemented structure
Like swift eagles in the sky
explanationEn: Surah As-Saff takes its name from this verse: Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row (saffan) as though they were a solid, cemented structure.

questionEn: In Surah As-Saff 61:6, by what name did Prophet Isa (AS) give glad tidings of the Messenger to come after him?
optionsEn: Al-Farooq
Dhun-Nun
Ahmad
Al-Amin
explanationEn: Isa (AS), son of Maryam, announced to the Children of Israel that he was confirming the Torah and bringing glad tidings of a Messenger to come after him whose name is Ahmad.

questionEn: What does Surah As-Saff 61:10–11 refer to as a 'profitable trade' that saves believers from a painful punishment?
optionsEn: Trading spices between Makkah and Syria
Giving half of every harvest to judges
Believing in Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause with wealth and lives
Building inns along caravan routes
explanationEn: Allah invites believers to a trade that delivers them from painful torment: faith in Allah and His Messenger and striving with wealth and souls in His path.

questionEn: To what does Surah Al-Jumu'ah 62:5 compare those entrusted with the Torah who failed to uphold its teachings?
optionsEn: A tree without roots
A bird with clipped wings
A donkey carrying heavy books
A lamp without oil
explanationEn: Those given the Torah who did not bear its responsibilities are likened to a donkey carrying volumes of books—possessing scripture physically without benefiting from its guidance.

questionEn: What are believers commanded to do immediately when the call is proclaimed for the Friday (Jumu'ah) prayer?
optionsEn: Remain silent for three hours
Fast for the remainder of the day
Perform twelve sunnah cycles before entering
Hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade
explanationEn: Surah Al-Jumu'ah 62:9 commands believers: when the call to prayer on Friday is made, hasten earnestly to the remembrance of Allah and leave off business.

questionEn: After the Jumu'ah prayer has concluded, what does Surah Al-Jumu'ah 62:10 encourage believers to do?
optionsEn: Refrain from speaking until sunset
Stay inside the mosque until Maghrib
Travel only on foot for the day
Disperse through the land, seek Allah's bounty, and remember Him much
explanationEn: Verse 10 balances worship with livelihood: once prayer ends, disperse in the land, seek of Allah's bounty, and remember Allah abundantly so you may succeed.

questionEn: What historical incident is rebuked in the final verse of Surah Al-Jumu'ah (62:11)?
optionsEn: Sleeping through Fajr during travel
Rushing out toward a trade caravan and diversion, leaving the Prophet ﷺ standing
Delaying the adhan intentionally
Arguing over inheritance during the sermon
explanationEn: When a trade caravan arrived with drums, many rushed out of the mosque to see it, leaving the Prophet ﷺ standing on the pulpit; the verse reminds them that what is with Allah is better than amusement and merchandise.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Munafiqun 63:4, to what striking physical image are the hypocrites compared when seen sitting in gatherings?
optionsEn: Empty vessels of clay
Propped-up pieces of timber
Withered desert reeds
Shadows on a wall
explanationEn: Despite their impressive outward appearance and smooth speech, Allah describes the hypocrites as 'propped-up timber'—hollow and lacking true spiritual life.

questionEn: What arrogant statement made by the leader of the hypocrites is refuted in Surah Al-Munafiqun 63:8?
optionsEn: 'No army can reach us behind these walls'
'Our wealth will buy our salvation'
'We need no rain from the sky'
'The more honorable will surely expel the meaner from Madinah'
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Ubayy boasted that upon returning to Madinah the honorable would expel the meaner; Allah replied that all honor belongs to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers.

questionEn: What does Surah Al-Munafiqun 63:9 warn believers must never distract them from the remembrance of Allah?
optionsEn: Travel and poetry
Their wealth and their children
Seasonal harvests
Dreams and astrology
explanationEn: Allah addresses believers directly: 'Let not your wealth and your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that—those are the losers.'

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Munafiqun 63:10, what will a person beg for when death approaches if they failed to spend in charity during life?
optionsEn: To be delayed for a brief term so they may give charity and be among the righteous
To see their ancestors one last time
To return for one year to fast
To bequeath their home to strangers
explanationEn: Allah urges spending before death comes to anyone and they plead, 'My Lord, if only You would delay me for a brief term so I would give charity and be among the righteous.'

questionEn: What does the name of Surah At-Taghabun refer to in verse 9?
optionsEn: The Night of Assembly
The Valley of Echoes
The Day of Mutual Loss and Gain (Deprivation)
The Gathering of Scrolls
explanationEn: Yawm at-Taghabun refers to the Day of Judgment when people's true gains and losses are exposed—the righteous gain eternal bliss while disbelievers suffer manifest loss.

questionEn: How does Surah At-Taghabun 64:14 advise believers to respond when some of their spouses or children act as opponents to obedience?
optionsEn: Cut all family ties permanently
Pardon, overlook, and forgive, for Allah is Forgiving and Merciful
Publicly denounce them
Forbid them from eating at home
explanationEn: After warning that among spouses and children are enemies who may hold believers back from good, Allah counsels mercy: pardon, overlook, and forgive.

questionEn: In Surah At-Taghabun 64:15, what are wealth and children described as?
optionsEn: Obstacles to prayer
Exemptions from reckoning
Guaranteed signs of Allah's pleasure
A trial / test (fitnah)
explanationEn: Allah states: 'Your wealth and your children are but a trial (fitnah), and Allah has with Him a great reward.'

questionEn: What does Surah At-Taghabun 64:16 teach about the level of God-consciousness (taqwa) required of a believer?
optionsEn: It is measured only by nightly vigils
Fear Allah as much as you are able
It is required only during Ramadan
It applies exclusively to scholars
explanationEn: Surah At-Taghabun 64:16 states the merciful principle: 'So fear Allah as much as you are able, and listen and obey and spend for the good of your own souls.'

questionEn: What two blessings does Allah promise in Surah At-Talaq 65:2–3 to the one who fears Him (has taqwa)?
optionsEn: A way out of difficulty and provision from unexpected sources
Leadership over cities and abundant herds
Long life and immunity from illness
Knowledge of hidden treasures
explanationEn: Allah promises: 'Whoever fears Allah—He will make for him a way out, and will provide for him from where he does not expect.'

questionEn: What assurance does Surah At-Talaq 65:3 give to the person who places full reliance (tawakkul) upon Allah?
optionsEn: Angels will fight all their battles
Allah is sufficient for him
All debts will be erased
They will never face grief
explanationEn: The verse states: 'And whoever relies upon Allah—then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose.'

questionEn: According to Surah At-Talaq 65:1, what should NOT happen to a divorced woman during her waiting period ('iddah) unless she commits clear indecency?
optionsEn: She should not be expelled from her home, nor should she leave it
She should not fast
She should not speak to her parents
She should not receive her dowry
explanationEn: Surah At-Talaq 65:1 prohibits turning divorced women out of their houses or their leaving during the waiting period, so reconciliation remains possible.

questionEn: What cosmic fact does the final verse of Surah At-Talaq (65:12) mention alongside the seven heavens?
optionsEn: Seven pillars of light
Seven winds of mercy
Seven oceans of fire
Of the earth, the like of them (seven earths)
explanationEn: Surah At-Talaq 65:12 states: 'It is Allah who has created seven heavens and of the earth, the like of them,' with His command descending among them.

questionEn: What duty toward one's own family is commanded in Surah At-Tahrim 66:6?
optionsEn: Distribute all inheritance during one's lifetime
Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones
Teach them calligraphy and poetry
Assign each child a separate house
explanationEn: Allah addresses believers: 'O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones.'

questionEn: Which two women are cited in Surah At-Tahrim 66:10 as examples showing that family ties to prophets cannot save disbelievers?
optionsEn: The daughters of Shu'ayb
The wives of Ibrahim and Ya'qub
The sisters of Musa and Harun
The wives of Nuh and Lut
explanationEn: Allah presents the wives of Nuh (AS) and Lut (AS) as examples for disbelievers: both were under two righteous servants of Allah yet betrayed them, and their husbands availed them nothing.

questionEn: What prayer did Pharaoh's wife (Asiyah) make as recorded in Surah At-Tahrim 66:11?
optionsEn: 'Destroy Pharaoh's palaces before dawn'
'My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds'
'Turn the Nile into sweet honey'
'Grant me sovereignty over Egypt'
explanationEn: Asiyah is honored as an example for believers because she chose Allah over Pharaoh's tyranny, praying for a home near Allah in Paradise.

questionEn: Which phrase describes the sincere repentance commanded to believers in Surah At-Tahrim 66:8?
optionsEn: Tawbatan nasuha (sincere repentance)
Tawbatan qalbiyyah (silent repentance)
Tawbatan da'imah (continuous repentance)
Tawbatan sirriyyah (hidden repentance)
explanationEn: Allah calls upon believers: 'Repent to Allah with sincere repentance (tawbatan nasuha),' promising expiation of misdeeds and Gardens beneath which rivers flow.

questionEn: How many verses (ayahs) are in Surah Al-Mulk (Surah 67)?
optionsEn: 40 verses
30 verses
36 verses
25 verses
explanationEn: Surah Al-Mulk contains 30 verses, a number famously mentioned in the Prophet's ﷺ Hadith about a surah of thirty verses that intercedes for its reciter.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Mulk 67:2, why did Allah create death and life?
optionsEn: To separate angels from jinn
To measure the passage of stars
To test which of you is best in deed
To populate the earth with cities
explanationEn: Allah declares He created death and life 'to test you as to which of you is best in deed (ahsanu 'amala)'—emphasizing quality and sincerity, not mere quantity.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mulk 67:3–4, what happens when a person looks repeatedly at the seven layered heavens seeking any flaw or rift?
optionsEn: They discover hidden constellations
Their vision returns to them humbled and fatigued
Clouds obscure the horizon
They hear the angels' glorification
explanationEn: Allah challenges observers to look again and again for any flaw in the creation of the heavens; their gaze returns to them exhausted and humbled, finding no imperfection.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Mulk 67:5, what two functions do the lamps (stars) adorning the lowest heaven serve?
optionsEn: Measuring rainfall and marking eclipses
Warming the oceans and guiding birds
Adornment of the lowest heaven and missiles against the devils
Cooling the winds and lighting the moon
explanationEn: Allah states He adorned the lowest heaven with lamps (stars) and made them missiles to drive away the devils.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mulk 67:10, what two faculties will the dwellers of the Blazing Fire (Sa'ir) admit they failed to use when warned?
optionsEn: Writing and calculation
Travel and consultation
Listening and reasoning ('Had we listened or reasoned...')
Fasting and charity
explanationEn: The inhabitants of Sa'ir confess with regret: 'If only we had been listening or reasoning, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze.'

questionEn: Which two qualities of Allah's knowledge are highlighted together in Surah Al-Mulk 67:14?
optionsEn: Al-Latif (the Subtle) and Al-Khabir (the All-Aware)
Al-Malik and Al-Quddus
Ar-Razzaq and Al-Fattah
Al-Qawi and Al-Matin
explanationEn: After asking rhetorically, 'Does He who created not know?' verse 14 concludes that He is Al-Latif (the Subtle/Kind) and Al-Khabir (the All-Aware).

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Mulk 67:15 describe the earth in relation to human travel and livelihood?
optionsEn: Rigid and impassable
Reserved only for shepherds
Made subservient/manageable (dhalulan), so walk upon its slopes and eat of His provision
Suspended over boiling springs
explanationEn: Allah reminds mankind that He made the earth manageable (dhalulan) for them, inviting them to walk through its paths and eat from His provision while remembering the Resurrection.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mulk 67:19, what sustains birds in the sky as they spread and fold their wings?
optionsEn: The rotation of the moon
Warm currents from desert sands
Nothing holds them up except the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman)
Their hollow bones alone
explanationEn: Verse 19 draws attention to birds overhead spreading and folding their wings: 'None holds them up except the Most Merciful. Indeed He is, of all things, Seeing.'

questionEn: What warning closes Surah Al-Mulk in verse 30?
optionsEn: What if no rain fell for seven years?
What if the sun failed to rise at dawn?
What if the mountains crumbled into dust?
What if your water were to sink deep into the earth—who could bring you flowing water?
explanationEn: Surah Al-Mulk closes with a sobering question: 'Say: Have you considered—if your water was to become sunken [into the earth], then who could bring you flowing water?'

questionEn: According to an authentic Hadith narrated by Abu Hurayrah (RA), what does Surah Al-Mulk do for the person who recites it?
optionsEn: It intercedes for a man until he is forgiven
It reveals unseen dreams
It doubles the reward of Hajj
It guarantees wealth within a year
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'A surah from the Qur'an of thirty verses interceded for a man until he was forgiven; it is Tabarakalladhi bi-yadihil-mulk.'

questionEn: Alongside which other surah did the Prophet ﷺ habitually recite Surah Al-Mulk before going to sleep, according to Jabir (RA)?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Waqi'ah
Surah As-Sajdah (Alif-Lam-Mim Tanzil)
Surah Yasin
Surah Al-Kahf
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ would not sleep until he had recited Alif-Lam-Mim Tanzil (As-Sajdah, 32) and Tabarakalladhi bi-yadihil-mulk (Al-Mulk, 67).

questionEn: What promise is made in Surah Al-Mulk 67:12 for those who fear their Lord unseen (bil-ghayb)?
optionsEn: Forgiveness and a great reward
Freedom from all worldly toil
A palace of silver in Makkah
Immediate victory over kings
explanationEn: Verse 12 contrasts the dwellers of Hell with believers who fear their Lord in private/unseen: for them is forgiveness and a great reward.

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Mulk 67:22 compare the person walking with their face prone (mukibban) versus the one walking upright on a straight path?
optionsEn: The one walking upright on a straight path is far better guided
Both arrive at the same destination eventually
The one prone moves faster in darkness
Neither can see the horizon
explanationEn: Allah uses a vivid physical parable: someone stumbling face-down cannot match someone walking upright along a clear, straight path.

questionEn: What three faculties does Allah remind mankind He granted them in Surah Al-Mulk 67:23, yet they give little thanks?
optionsEn: Speech, memory, and strength
Wealth, shelter, and family
Hands, feet, and breath
Hearing, sight, and hearts (intellect)
explanationEn: Verse 23 states: 'It is He who produced you and made for you hearing and vision and hearts (af'idah); little are you grateful.'

questionEn: When disbelievers challenge the Prophet ﷺ in Surah Al-Mulk 67:25 asking 'When is this promise [of the Hour]?', what is he instructed to answer?
optionsEn: 'Ask the scribes of earlier books'
'When the stars fall to earth'
'Within three generations'
'The knowledge is only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner'
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ is commanded to affirm that exact knowledge of the Hour belongs solely to Allah, while his own duty is clear warning.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mulk 67:8, what emotion is ascribed to Hellfire as a group is cast into it?
optionsEn: Silence and stillness
Shrinking into ashes
Almost bursting with rage (tamayyazu minal-ghayz)
Weeping over their loss
explanationEn: Surah Al-Mulk 67:8 vividly describes Hellfire as nearly bursting apart with fury each time a disbelieving group is thrown into it, while its keepers ask if no warner came to them.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Mulk 67:16–17, why should people never feel secure from Allah's decree while living on earth?
optionsEn: Because wild beasts outnumber towns
Because He who is above the heavens can cause the earth to swallow them or send a storm of stones
Because winter winds can freeze rivers overnight
Because oceans rise every century
explanationEn: Verses 16–17 warn against complacency, reminding humanity that Allah can cause the earth to cave in beneath them or send upon them a storm of stones (hasiban).

questionEn: By what two things does Allah swear at the very opening of Surah Al-Qalam (68:1)?
optionsEn: The Tablet and the mountain
The Pen (al-qalam) and what they inscribe
The Dawn and the stars
The Inkwell and the parchment
explanationEn: Surah Al-Qalam opens with the letter Nun followed by an oath: 'By the pen and what they inscribe,' honoring writing and revelation.

questionEn: What majestic testimony does Allah give regarding the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Surah Al-Qalam 68:4?
optionsEn: 'You have memorized every scroll'
'And indeed, you are of a great moral character (khuluqin azim)'
'You are the most eloquent of the Arabs'
'You are granted authority over every wind'
explanationEn: Defending the Prophet ﷺ against the slander of madness, Allah declares: 'And indeed, you are of a great moral character.'

questionEn: In the parable of the Companions of the Garden (Ashab al-Jannah) in Surah Al-Qalam, what caused Allah to destroy their orchard overnight?
optionsEn: They flooded their neighbor's land
They worshiped statues beside the trees
They swore to harvest it at dawn secretly to deprive the poor without saying 'If Allah wills'
They sold unripe fruit in the market
explanationEn: The owners conspired to harvest early before any poor person could ask for a share, without exception ('In sha'Allah'), so a calamity from Allah turned their garden black and barren overnight.

questionEn: By what title does Surah Al-Qalam 68:48 refer to Prophet Yunus (AS) when advising the Prophet ﷺ not to be hasty like him?
optionsEn: Sahib al-Kahf
Dhu al-Kifl
Sahib al-Hut (the Companion of the Fish)
Kalimullah
explanationEn: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ: 'Be patient for the decision of your Lord and do not be like the Companion of the Fish (Yunus) when he called out while he was distressed.'

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Haqqah describe the destructive wind sent upon the people of 'Ad?
optionsEn: A whirlwind rising from the sea
A gentle breeze lasting forty days
A hot sandstorm lasting one afternoon
A furious roaring wind (rih sarsar) unleashed for seven nights and eight days
explanationEn: Allah destroyed 'Ad with a violent, roaring cold wind that raged over them for seven nights and eight consecutive days, leaving them fallen like hollow palm trunks.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Haqqah 69:17, how many angels will bear the Throne of Allah above them on the Day of Resurrection?
optionsEn: Seventy angels
Four angels
Eight angels
Twelve angels
explanationEn: Verse 17 states that the angels will stand on the sides of heaven, and eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Haqqah 69:19, what joyful exclamation does the person given their record in their right hand make?
optionsEn: 'The angels have written my praise'
'Here, read my record!'
'Bring forth my family at once'
'I have surpassed every king'
explanationEn: Filled with joy and relief, the believer cries out to those around: 'Here, read my record! Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my account.'

questionEn: What two false claims about the Qur'an does Allah explicitly deny at the end of Surah Al-Haqqah (69:41–42)?
optionsEn: That it was written by angels or jinn
That it is the word of a poet or the word of a soothsayer (kahin)
That it is a book of astronomy or medicine
That it was copied from Persian tablets or Greek scrolls
explanationEn: Allah declares that the Qur'an is the speech of a noble Messenger—it is neither the word of a poet nor the word of a soothsayer, rather a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'arij 70:4, what is the length of the Day in which the angels and the Spirit (Ruh) ascend to Allah?
optionsEn: Ten thousand years
Seven hundred years
One thousand years
Fifty thousand years
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ma'arij states that the angels and the Spirit ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years.

questionEn: What specific psychological weakness of mankind is described in Surah Al-Ma'arij 70:19–21?
optionsEn: Preferring darkness over daylight
Being created anxious/impatient (halu'a)—fretful when touched by evil and withholding when touched by good
Being overly forgetful in travel
Seeking constant conflict with neighbors
explanationEn: Allah describes man as halu'a (anxious and impatient): complaining when hardship strikes and stingy when prosperity comes—except those steadfast in prayer and charity.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Ma'arij 70:24–25, who holds a 'recognized right' (haqq ma'lum) in the wealth of the righteous?
optionsEn: Merchants and tax collectors
Tribal elders and poets
Travelers carrying gold
The one who asks (as-sa'il) and the deprived who refrains from asking (al-mahrum)
explanationEn: Among the defining traits of those honored in Gardens of Paradise is that within their wealth is a known share for both the beggar and the destitute who does not beg.

questionEn: What kind of patience is the Prophet ﷺ instructed to practice in Surah Al-Ma'arij 70:5?
optionsEn: Silent endurance for forty days
Gracious patience (sabran jamilan)
Withdrawing from public preaching
Patience only until migration
explanationEn: Allah commands: 'So be patient with gracious patience (sabran jamilan)'—patience free of panic or complaint.

questionEn: According to Surah Nuh 71:10–12, what worldly blessings did Prophet Nuh (AS) tell his people Allah would grant if they sought His forgiveness?
optionsEn: Abundant rain from the sky, increase in wealth and children, gardens, and rivers
Victory over distant empires and marble palaces
Knowledge of hidden mines of gold
Immunity from aging and flying steeds
explanationEn: Nuh (AS) promised his people that seeking Allah's forgiveness brings plentiful rain, increased wealth and offspring, and lush gardens and flowing rivers.

questionEn: Which five idols did the leaders of Nuh's (AS) people urge each other never to abandon in Surah Nuh 71:23?
optionsEn: Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr
Ba'l, Dagon, Ashtoreth, Molech, and Chemosh
Al-Lat, Al-'Uzza, Manat, Hubal, and Isaf
Anu, Enlil, Shamash, Sin, and Marduk
explanationEn: The chieftains plotted and told their followers: 'Never leave your gods, and never leave Wadd or Suwa' or Yaghuth and Ya'uq and Nasr.'

questionEn: What two methods of preaching did Prophet Nuh (AS) describe using with his people in Surah Nuh 71:5–9?
optionsEn: Through dreams and written tablets
Night and day, both openly in public and privately in secret
Only on market days in the square
Through messengers sent from neighboring valleys
explanationEn: Nuh (AS) reported to Allah that he called his people night and day, aloud in public gatherings as well as privately in earnest counsel, yet they put their fingers in their ears.

questionEn: Whom did Prophet Nuh (AS) include in his closing supplication in Surah Nuh 71:28?
optionsEn: Only himself and his sons
The angels of the Flood alone
Himself, his parents, whoever enters his house as a believer, and all believing men and women
His tribe and its livestock
explanationEn: The final verse records Nuh's comprehensive du'a: 'My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house a believer and the believing men and believing women.'

questionEn: How did the group of jinn react upon hearing the Prophet ﷺ recite the Qur'an in Surah Al-Jinn 72:1–2?
optionsEn: They debated whether it was ancient poetry
They said, 'Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur'an that guides to the right course, so we have believed in it'
They demanded a visible miracle of fire
They fled back to the valleys in fear
explanationEn: Allah revealed to the Prophet ﷺ that a band of jinn listened attentively, marveled at the Qur'an's guidance to rectitude, and immediately affirmed Tawhid.

questionEn: What foundational rule of worship is declared in Surah Al-Jinn 72:18?
optionsEn: Build mosques only facing north
The places of worship (masajid) belong to Allah, so do not invoke anyone alongside Allah
Close mosques between sunset and dawn
Recite only silently inside mosques
explanationEn: Verse 18 states clearly: 'And that the masajid are for Allah, so do not invoke anyone along with Allah.'

questionEn: What did the jinn discover regarding listening in on the heavens after the Prophet's ﷺ mission began, as stated in Surah Al-Jinn 72:8–9?
optionsEn: Clouds blocked all sound from reaching space
Heaven was filled with severe guards and flaming projectiles preventing eavesdropping
The angels descended to live on earth
The stars had stopped moving
explanationEn: The jinn reported that when they sought to reach heaven to eavesdrop as before, they found it guarded by stern protectors and shooting flames awaiting anyone who listens.

questionEn: What does the title 'Al-Muzzammil' mean, addressing the Prophet ﷺ at the start of Surah 73?
optionsEn: The Enwrapped One (wrapped in garments)
The Patient Caller
The Warner of Nations
The One Who Journeys by Night
explanationEn: 'Al-Muzzammil' refers to the Prophet ﷺ wrapped up in his garment, whom Allah commands to arise for night prayer except a little.

questionEn: What manner of Qur'anic recitation is commanded in Surah Al-Muzzammil 73:4?
optionsEn: Rapid recitation to finish before dawn
Chanting in rhymed prose
Measured, distinct recitation (tartilan)
Whispering without moving the lips
explanationEn: Allah commands: 'And recite the Qur'an with measured, clear recitation (tartilan),' noting in the next verse that He is about to cast upon him a weighty word.

questionEn: Which three groups of people are mentioned in the final verse of Surah Al-Muzzammil (73:20) as reasons Allah lightened the length of night prayer?
optionsEn: New converts, students, and judges
Farmers, shepherds, and sailors
Those who are ill, those traveling in the land seeking Allah's bounty, and those fighting in the cause of Allah
Elders, orphans, and scribes
explanationEn: In verse 20, Allah out of mercy eased the strict night vigil, knowing some would be sick, others traveling for livelihood, and others striving in Allah's path, commanding instead to recite whatever is easy of the Qur'an.

questionEn: Which four directives immediately follow 'O you who covers himself' (Ya ayyuhal-muddaththir) in Surah Al-Muddaththir 74:2–5?
optionsEn: Write, memorize, teach, and judge
Fast, pray, give charity, and migrate
Travel, build a mosque, call to Friday prayer, and reconcile tribes
Arise and warn, magnify your Lord, purify your garments, and shun defilement/idols
explanationEn: When revelation resumed after a pause, Allah instructed the Prophet ﷺ: 'Arise and warn, and your Lord glorify, and your garments purify, and uncleanliness/idols avoid.'

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Muddaththir 74:30, how many angels are appointed as guardians over Saqar (Hellfire)?
optionsEn: Twelve angels
Forty angels
Nineteen angels
Seven angels
explanationEn: Verse 30 states: 'Over it are nineteen [angels],' appointed as keepers to test disbelievers and strengthen the certainty of the believers and People of the Book.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Muddaththir 74:42–46, when the Companions of the Right ask the criminals 'What put you into Saqar?', which four sins do they confess?
optionsEn: Not praying, not feeding the poor, indulging in vain talk with those who indulged, and denying the Day of Recompense
Theft, dishonesty, anger, and cowardice
Breaking treaties, building tall towers, sleeping late, and arguing
Forgetting fasting, neglecting travel, hoarding silver, and mocking poets
explanationEn: The condemned reply: 'We were not of those who prayed, nor did we used to feed the poor, and we used to enter into vain discourse with those who engaged in it, and we used to deny the Day of Recompense.'

questionEn: To what animals does Surah Al-Muddaththir 74:50–51 compare those who flee away from the Qur'anic reminder?
optionsEn: Startled wild donkeys fleeing from a lion
Sparrows scattering in thunder
Timid gazelles fleeing hawks
Lost camels wandering in fog
explanationEn: Allah vividly describes their stubborn flight from guidance: 'As if they were alarmed donkeys fleeing from a lion.'

questionEn: What type of soul does Allah swear by in the second verse of Surah Al-Qiyamah (75:2)?
optionsEn: The commanding soul (an-nafs al-ammarah)
The self-reproaching soul (an-nafs al-lawwamah)
The tranquil soul (an-nafs al-mutma'innah)
The forgetful soul (an-nafs al-ghafilah)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Qiyamah opens by swearing by the Day of Resurrection and by the self-reproaching soul (an-nafs al-lawwamah), which blames itself for shortcomings.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Qiyamah 75:4, what intricate detail of the human body does Allah mention as proof of His power to resurrect mankind?
optionsEn: Even the very fingertips (bananah)
Every drop of blood in the veins
Every strand of hair on the head
The chambers of the heart
explanationEn: Answering the skeptic who doubts Allah can reassemble decayed bones, Allah declares: 'Yes—Able [even] to proportion his fingertips.'

questionEn: Why was the Prophet ﷺ told in Surah Al-Qiyamah 75:16, 'Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it'?
optionsEn: He was speaking too loudly during prayer
He was translating verses into another dialect
He wanted to finish the sermon early
He moved his tongue rapidly while Jibril recited revelation out of eagerness not to forget a word
explanationEn: Out of intense concern to memorize revelation immediately, the Prophet ﷺ would move his lips hastily; Allah reassured him that collecting it in his heart and reciting it rests upon Allah.

questionEn: What supreme honor is granted to the radiant faces of the believers in Surah Al-Qiyamah 75:22–23?
optionsEn: Riding winged steeds across Paradise
Crowns of emerald
Looking at their Lord
Ruling over stars
explanationEn: Allah says: '[Some] faces, that Day, will be radiant, looking at their Lord'—the Beatific Vision, the highest blessing of Paradise.

questionEn: Which three vulnerable groups do the righteous (al-abrar) feed in Surah Al-Insan 76:8–9 solely for the countenance of Allah?
optionsEn: The neighbor, the teacher, and the pilgrim
The farmer, the shepherd, and the soldier
The needy (miskin), the orphan (yatim), and the captive (asir)
The elderly, the merchant, and the scribe
explanationEn: Despite their own love/need for the food, the righteous feed the needy, the orphan, and the captive, saying in their hearts: 'We feed you only for the Face of Allah; we desire from you neither reward nor thanks.'

questionEn: What are the names of the two aromatic/refreshing drinks or springs of Paradise mentioned in Surah Al-Insan (76:5 and 76:17–18)?
optionsEn: Kafur (camphor) and Zanjabil (ginger) / Salsabil
Tasnim and Kawthar
Zamzam and Furat
Honey and saffron
explanationEn: Surah Al-Insan mentions the righteous drinking from a cup flavored with Kafur (76:5) and another mixed with Zanjabil from a spring therein called Salsabil (76:17–18).

questionEn: According to Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, when did the Prophet ﷺ regularly recite Surah As-Sajdah and Surah Al-Insan?
optionsEn: During the Eid al-Adha prayer
During the two rak'ahs of Eclipse prayer
In the Witr prayer after Isha
In the Fajr prayer on Fridays
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah (RA) reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to recite Alif-Lam-Mim Tanzil (As-Sajdah) in the first rak'ah and Hal ata 'alal-insani (Al-Insan) in the second rak'ah of Fajr on Friday.

questionEn: What alternative name is commonly used in classical mushafs and tafsir for Surah Al-Insan (Surah 76)?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Abrar
Surah As-Salsabil
Surah Ad-Dahr (or Hal Ata)
Surah Al-Miskin
explanationEn: Surah 76 is known both as Al-Insan ('Man') and Ad-Dahr ('Time') from its opening words: 'Hal ata 'alal-insani hinun minad-dahr.'

questionEn: How many times does the refrain 'Woe, that Day, to the deniers!' (Waylun yawma'idhin lil-mukadhdhibin) repeat in Surah Al-Mursalat?
optionsEn: 5 times
14 times
10 times
7 times
explanationEn: Surah Al-Mursalat punctuates its warnings of judgment and signs of creation with the stark refrain 'Woe, that Day, to the deniers!' ten times.

questionEn: To what does Surah Al-Mursalat 77:32–33 compare the sparks thrown up by Hellfire?
optionsEn: Volcanic boulders and dark clouds
Flaming arrows and iron chains
Falling meteors and red embers
Huge castles (palaces) and yellow/tawny camels
explanationEn: Allah describes Hell throwing sparks as huge as castles/fortresses (qasr), looking like a string of yellow/tawny camels (jimalatun sufr).

questionEn: What inability of the criminals on the Day of Sorting (Yawm al-Fasl) is highlighted in Surah Al-Mursalat 77:35–36?
optionsEn: They cannot open their eyes
They cannot walk across the sand
They cannot recognize their names
They will not speak, nor will it be permitted for them to make excuses
explanationEn: Verses 35–36 declare: 'This is a Day they will not speak, nor will it be permitted for them to make excuses'—silenced before undeniable truth.

questionEn: What is the 'Great News' (An-Naba' al-Azim) about which the disbelievers were questioning and differing at the opening of Surah An-Naba'?
optionsEn: The Resurrection and Day of Judgment (and the Qur'anic message warning of it)
The migration to Abyssinia
The discovery of ancient scrolls
The construction of the Ka'bah
explanationEn: People disputed over the Great News—the Resurrection, Judgment, and the truth of the Qur'an proclaiming it—to which Allah replies: 'No! They are going to know.'

questionEn: In Surah An-Naba' 78:6–7, to what two comforting structures are the earth and the mountains compared?
optionsEn: A carpet and walls of marble
A canopy and pillars of iron
A resting bed (mihadan) and stabilizing pegs (awtadan)
A ship and anchors of stone
explanationEn: Allah reminds mankind of His design: 'Have We not made the earth a resting place (mihadan) and the mountains as pegs (awtadan)?'

questionEn: How does Surah An-Naba' 78:9–11 describe sleep, night, and day?
optionsEn: Sleep as forgetting, night as cold, and day as heat
Sleep as dreaming, night as silence, and day as trial
Sleep as death, night as fear, and day as work
Sleep as rest (subatan), night as a covering garment (libasan), and day for livelihood (ma'ashan)
explanationEn: Verses 9–11 pair human rhythms with creation: sleep for rest, night as a protective cover, and day for seeking livelihood.

questionEn: What despairing wish does the disbeliever utter in the final verse of Surah An-Naba' (78:40) upon seeing what his hands put forward?
optionsEn: 'Oh, I wish I had been a mountain!'
'Oh, I wish I had never been born in Makkah!'
'Oh, I wish the stars would hide me!'
'Oh, I wish that I were dust!'
explanationEn: After seeing the reckoning of animals settled and turned to dust, the disbeliever cries out in agony: 'Oh, I wish that I were dust!'

questionEn: What greeting and falsehood-free speech is highlighted in Paradise in Surah An-Naba' 78:35?
optionsEn: They hear only rhythmic chants
They converse solely with angels
They speak only in whispers
They will not hear therein any ill speech (laghw) or any falsehood (kidhdhab)
explanationEn: Among the pure joys of the righteous in Paradise is total peace of speech: neither vain, idle talk nor lying is ever heard there.

questionEn: To what do the opening oaths of Surah An-Nazi'at (79:1–5) refer according to the overwhelming consensus of classical tafsir?
optionsEn: Wild horses charging in battle
Desert winds blowing across dunes
Angels executing Allah's commands—extracting souls violently or gently, gliding swiftly, and regulating affairs
Shooting stars guarding the sky
explanationEn: Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, and classical commentators explain An-Nazi'at as angels tearing out the souls of the wicked forcefully, contrasting with An-Nashitat gently drawing out believers' souls.

questionEn: What arrogant claim of Pharaoh is quoted in Surah An-Nazi'at 79:24 after Musa (AS) showed him the great sign?
optionsEn: 'I am your lord, the most high (ana rabbukumul-a'la)'
'My magicians control the heavens'
'No prophet can cross my borders'
'The Nile obeys only my staff'
explanationEn: Gathering his people, Pharaoh proclaimed: 'I am your lord most high,' prompting Allah to seize him in an exemplary punishment in both the Hereafter and this world.

questionEn: According to Surah An-Nazi'at 79:40–41, what two qualities lead a person to Paradise as their refuge?
optionsEn: Fearing the standing before one's Lord and restraining the soul from vain desire (hawa)
Memorizing genealogies and fasting Mondays
Wealth and eloquent speech
Traveling widely and building monuments
explanationEn: Verses 40–41 state: 'But as for he who feared the position of his Lord and prevented the soul from [unlawful] inclination, then indeed, Paradise will be [his] refuge.'

questionEn: In Surah An-Nazi'at 79:30–33, after raising the sky and darkening its night, what did Allah do to the earth?
optionsEn: Split it into ten equal islands
Spread it out (dahaha), brought forth its water and pasture, and set the mountains firmly
Filled it with gold beneath every stone
Surrounded it with walls of ice
explanationEn: Allah points to His majestic creation of the cosmos as greater than resurrecting humans: spreading out the earth, bringing out its springs and vegetation, and anchoring the mountains as provision for us and our livestock.

questionEn: Which blind Companion came seeking spiritual purification when the Prophet ﷺ was occupied with Quraysh leaders, prompting the opening of Surah 'Abasa?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum
Bilal ibn Rabah
Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas
Khabbab ibn al-Aratt
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum (RA) interrupted the Prophet's ﷺ conversation with Quraysh notables asking to be taught; Allah gently corrected the Prophet ﷺ so no seeker of truth is overlooked.

questionEn: How does Surah 'Abasa 80:15–16 describe the angels who transcribe the Noble Scriptures?
optionsEn: Swift and silent
Stationed at the four corners
Noble and dutiful/righteous (kiramin bararah)
Crowned with light
explanationEn: Describing the honored, purified pages of revelation, verse 15–16 states they are in the hands of angelic scribes (safarah) who are noble and dutiful (kiramin bararah).

questionEn: In Surah 'Abasa 80:24–32, what everyday blessing is humanity told to reflect upon to appreciate Allah's providence?
optionsEn: The plumage of migratory birds
Their food—how rain is poured down, soil split, and grain, grapes, olives, dates, and orchards grown
The metals forged inside caves
The sails of ships at sea
explanationEn: Verse 24 commands: 'Then let mankind look at his food,' tracing rain from the sky through split earth into crops and fruits for humans and cattle.

questionEn: What startling scene of the Deafening Blast (As-Sakhkhah) is depicted in Surah 'Abasa 80:34–37?
optionsEn: A man fleeing from his brother, mother, father, wife, and children, each absorbed in his own affair
Kings bowing to their servants
Mountains melting into silver rivers
Cities sinking beneath the waves
explanationEn: On that Day, worldly attachments vanish: every person flees from their closest family members because each has a matter occupying them completely.

questionEn: What does the title 'At-Takwir' refer to in the first verse of Surah 81?
optionsEn: The splitting of the moon
The roaring of the oceans
The gathering of clouds
The sun being wrapped up / folded in darkness
explanationEn: 'Idhash-shamsu kuwwirat' means when the sun is rolled/wrapped up and loses its light as the Day of Resurrection unfolds.

questionEn: Which pre-Islamic atrocity is explicitly condemned in Surah At-Takwir 81:8–9?
optionsEn: Worshiping trees in valleys
Usury in marketplace loans
Burying newborn infant girls alive (al-maw'udah)
Destroying travelers' wells
explanationEn: Surah At-Takwir warns that on the Day of Judgment, the female infant buried alive (al-maw'udah) will be asked for what sin she was killed.

questionEn: To which three surahs did the Prophet ﷺ say one should turn if they wish to look at the Day of Resurrection as though seeing it with their own eyes?
optionsEn: Al-Mulk, Al-Qalam, and Al-Haqqah
Al-Fajr, Al-Balad, and Ash-Shams
At-Takwir, Al-Infitar, and Al-Inshiqaq
An-Naba', An-Nazi'at, and 'Abasa
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said whoever wishes to see the Day of Resurrection as if with his own eyes should recite 'Idhash-shamsu kuwwirat' (81), 'Idhas-sama'un-fatarat' (82), and 'Idhas-sama'un-shaqqat' (84).

questionEn: Who is the 'noble Messenger, possessed of power and high status with the Owner of the Throne, obeyed and trustworthy' described in Surah At-Takwir 81:19–23?
optionsEn: Prophet Ibrahim (AS)
Angel Jibril (AS)
Angel Israfil (AS)
Prophet Musa (AS)
explanationEn: These verses affirm the integrity of revelation: the Qur'an was brought by Jibril (AS), who is mighty, honored near the Throne, obeyed among the angels, and whom the Prophet ﷺ saw on the clear horizon.

questionEn: What does the closing verse of Surah At-Takwir (81:29) state about human will in relation to Allah's will?
optionsEn: Human will operates independently of creation
Only prophets possess free choice
And you do not will except that Allah wills—Lord of the worlds
Willingness requires no action
explanationEn: After affirming in 81:28 that the Qur'an is a reminder for whoever wills to take a straight path, verse 29 balances human choice with divine sovereignty: 'And you do not will except that Allah wills—Lord of the worlds.'

questionEn: What touching rhetorical question does Allah ask mankind in Surah Al-Infitar 82:6?
optionsEn: 'Why do you sleep through the night?'
'Where will your caravans travel tomorrow?'
'Who built the seven heavens above you?'
'O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous (Al-Karim)?'
explanationEn: Surah Al-Infitar 82:6 gently yet powerfully awakens the human conscience: 'O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous, who created you, proportioned you, and balanced you?'

questionEn: Who are the 'Kiraman Katibin' mentioned in Surah Al-Infitar 82:10–12?
optionsEn: The noble recording angels who know whatever humans do
The guardians of Paradise's gates
The stars guiding travelers at night
The prophets of Israel
explanationEn: Surah Al-Infitar warns that over every human are appointed watchers—noble recorders (Kiraman Katibin)—who know and record everything we do.

questionEn: According to the final verse of Surah Al-Infitar (82:19), what characterizes the Day of Recompense?
optionsEn: Kings will ransom their subjects with gold
Every soul will argue on behalf of its tribe
A Day when a soul will not possess for another soul [power to do] a thing, and the command that Day is with Allah
Angels will distribute crowns to the wealthy
explanationEn: Surah Al-Infitar closes with complete accountability: no soul can benefit or rescue another soul on that Day, for all authority belongs solely to Allah.

questionEn: Who are 'Al-Mutaffifin' (the defrauders) rebuked at the opening of Surah 83?
optionsEn: Those who take full measure when buying from others, yet give less when measuring or weighing for them
Those who refuse to lend horses
Those who break fasting before sunset
Those who speak loudly in markets
explanationEn: Surah Al-Mutaffifin opens with 'Woe to those who give less [than due]'—exposing double standards in trade and justice, reminding them they will be resurrected before the Lord of the worlds.

questionEn: What are the two contrasting names given in Surah Al-Mutaffifin to the registers of the wicked and the righteous?
optionsEn: Hawiyah and Kawthar
Sijjin (for the wicked) and 'Illiyyun (for the righteous)
Barzakh and Sidrah
Saqar and Firdaws
explanationEn: Surah Al-Mutaffifin states that the record of the wicked is in Sijjin (lowest depths/prison, 83:7) while the record of the righteous (al-abrar) is in 'Illiyyun (lofty heights, 83:18).

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mutaffifin 83:25–27, what is the seal of the 'sealed pure nectar' (Rahiq Makhtum) given to the righteous, and what is it mixed with?
optionsEn: Its seal is musk (misk), and its mixture is from Tasnim
Sealed with honey and mixed with rosewater
Sealed with pearl and mixed with snow
Sealed with amber and mixed with milk
explanationEn: The righteous are given sealed pure wine/nectar whose final scent/seal is musk, blended with water from Tasnim—a lofty spring from which those brought near to Allah drink.

questionEn: How are the tables turned between the criminals and the believers in the closing passage of Surah Al-Mutaffifin (83:29–36)?
optionsEn: The criminals are given a second chance on earth
Those who mocked and winked at believers in worldly life will be laughed at by the believers seated on adorned couches in Paradise
The believers forget the disbelievers completely
Both groups stand silently without looking
explanationEn: In the world, the wicked laughed and winked knowingly as believers passed by; on the Day of Judgment, the believers will recline on couches looking on and laughing at the disbelievers' recompense.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Inshiqaq 84:6, what universal truth is addressed directly to every human being?
optionsEn: 'Indeed, the stars were created for your leisure'
'Indeed, your wealth will outlast your children'
'Indeed, you will rule the earth for a season'
'Indeed, you are laboring toward your Lord with [great] exertion and will meet Him'
explanationEn: Verse 6 reminds every person that all of life is a strenuous journey leading inexorably to meeting Allah: 'O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with exertion and will meet Him.'

questionEn: What difference in receiving the book of deeds is described in Surah Al-Inshiqaq 84:7–12?
optionsEn: Records are read aloud only to scholars
One given his record in his right hand receives an easy reckoning (hisaban yasira), while one given it behind his back cries for destruction
Some receive two books and others receive none
Some receive a scroll of silver and others of clay
explanationEn: The believer given his record in his right hand gets an easy account and returns joyfully to his family in Paradise, whereas the one given his record behind his back calls out for destruction and enters the Blaze.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Inshiqaq 84:21, what criticism is leveled at disbelievers—followed by a verse of prostration (Sajdah at-Tilawah)?
optionsEn: They conceal ancient coins
They fast only in winter
When the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate
They refuse to build mosques
explanationEn: Verse 21 asks: 'And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate [to Allah]?'—marking one of the places of Sajdah at-Tilawah in Juz Amma.

questionEn: What does 'Al-Buruj' mean in the opening oath of Surah 85?
optionsEn: The sky containing great stars / constellations
Deep ocean trenches
Desert fortresses
Mountain passes
explanationEn: Surah Al-Buruj opens by swearing 'By the sky containing great constellations (dhatil-buruj),' referring to the majestic celestial stations of the stars.

questionEn: For what single reason did the tyrants of the Ditch (Ashab al-Ukhdud) burn the believers in Surah Al-Buruj 85:4–8?
optionsEn: They migrated without permission
They damaged the king's palace
Only because they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy
They refused to pay market taxes
explanationEn: Allah testifies to the believers' innocence: 'And they resented them not except because they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.'

questionEn: Where does the final verse of Surah Al-Buruj (85:22) declare the Glorious Qur'an is preserved?
optionsEn: On stone pillars of Sinai
In vaults beneath Makkah
In the memory of kings
In a Preserved Tablet (Lawh Mahfuz)
explanationEn: Concluding the surah, Allah affirms the Qur'an's absolute preservation and honor: 'But this is an honored Qur'an, [inscribed] in a Preserved Tablet (Lawh Mahfuz).'

questionEn: How does Surah At-Tariq 86:3 explain what 'At-Tariq' (the Nightcomer) is?
optionsEn: A nocturnal wind
The crescent moon of Ramadan
It is the piercing star (an-najm ath-thaqib)
A dream sent before dawn
explanationEn: After swearing by the sky and At-Tariq, Allah clarifies: 'And what can make you know what At-Tariq is? It is the piercing star'—whose light pierces the darkness.

questionEn: What spiritual reality follows the opening oath in Surah At-Tariq 86:4?
optionsEn: Every dream comes true at dawn
Every mountain remembers its creator
There is no soul but that it has over it a protector/watcher (hafiz)
Every star sets before sunrise
explanationEn: The oath leads directly to human accountability: 'There is no soul but that it has over it a protector'—angels guarding and recording every deed.

questionEn: How does Surah At-Tariq 86:13–14 describe the Qur'an?
optionsEn: As gentle poetry for travelers
As an ancient chronicle of kings
As hidden riddles for philosophers
Indeed, it is a decisive statement (qawlun fasl), and it is not amusement (hazl)
explanationEn: Allah affirms the seriousness and clarity of revelation: 'Indeed, the Qur'an is a decisive statement separating truth from falsehood, and it is not amusement.'

questionEn: What reassuring promise did Allah make to the Prophet ﷺ regarding preserving the Qur'an in Surah Al-A'la 87:6–7?
optionsEn: 'Every angel will whisper it daily'
'You will never need to repeat a verse'
'Your scribes will carve it on silver'
'We will make you recite, and you will not forget, except what Allah should will'
explanationEn: Allah promised the Prophet ﷺ effortless, lasting preservation of revelation: 'We will make you recite, [O Muhammad], and you will not forget, except what Allah should will.'

questionEn: What three steps to success are outlined in Surah Al-A'la 87:14–15?
optionsEn: Speaking softly, reading scrolls, and resting
Purifying oneself (tazakka), remembering the Name of one's Lord, and praying
Fasting, traveling, and giving gifts
Gathering wealth, building homes, and teaching
explanationEn: Allah declares: 'He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, and mentions the name of his Lord and prays.'

questionEn: Which two prophets' earlier scriptures are explicitly named at the end of Surah Al-A'la (87:18–19)?
optionsEn: The Books of Yusuf and Isa
The Scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa
The Scrolls of Idris and Sulayman
The Scrolls of Nuh and Dawud
explanationEn: Surah Al-A'la concludes by reminding humanity that the supremacy of the Hereafter over worldly life is timeless truth found 'in the former scriptures—the scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa.'

questionEn: According to Sahih Muslim, in which two congregational prayers did the Prophet ﷺ regularly recite Surah Al-A'la and Surah Al-Ghashiyah?
optionsEn: Dhuhr and Asr prayers
Fajr and Isha prayers
The two Eid prayers and the Friday (Jumu'ah) prayer
Tarawih and Eclipse prayers
explanationEn: An-Nu'man ibn Bashir (RA) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite 'Sabbihisma rabbikal-a'la' and 'Hal ataka hadithul-ghashiyah' in the two Eid prayers and in Jumu'ah.

questionEn: Which four creations does Allah urge mankind to look at and reflect upon in Surah Al-Ghashiyah 88:17–20?
optionsEn: Palm trees, horses, moons, and clouds
Bees, ants, rivers, and stars
Oceans, forests, lightning, and snow
The camels—how they are created; the sky—how it is raised; the mountains—how they are erected; and the earth—how it is spread out
explanationEn: Addressing desert listeners and all humanity, Allah calls them to ponder four immediate wonders: camels, the raised heaven, anchored mountains, and the spread-out earth.

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Ghashiyah 88:21–22 define the Prophet's ﷺ role toward people's acceptance of faith?
optionsEn: He must debate until they weep
He is only a reminder (mudhakkir), not a controller/dictator (musaytir) over them
He must compel every tribe to submit
He should withhold reminders from stubborn elders
explanationEn: Allah comforts His Messenger ﷺ: 'So remind, [O Muhammad]; you are only a reminder. You are not over them a controller.'

questionEn: What bitter, thorny plant is mentioned as the food of the people of Hell in Surah Al-Ghashiyah 88:6–7?
optionsEn: Zaqqum
Ghislin
Hamim
Dari'—which neither nourishes nor avails against hunger
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ghashiyah states that the condemned will have no food except a bitter, foul thorny plant called dari', which neither fattens nor satisfies hunger.

questionEn: What are the 'Ten Nights' (wa layalin 'ashr) sworn by at the beginning of Surah Al-Fajr according to Ibn Abbas and the majority of commentators?
optionsEn: The middle ten nights of Sha'ban
The first ten days/nights of Dhul-Hijjah
The ten nights Prophet Musa spent at sea
The first ten nights of Muharram
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Kathir, and classical mufassirun identify 'layalin 'ashr' as the blessed first ten days/nights of Dhul-Hijjah, the best days of the year.

questionEn: Which three ancient rebellious peoples or rulers are cited as examples of Allah's swift reckoning in Surah Al-Fajr 89:6–14?
optionsEn: 'Ad (of Iram of the pillars), Thamud (who carved rocks in the valley), and Pharaoh (owner of stakes)
Midian, Saba', and Ashab al-Kahf
Babylon, Nineveh, and People of the Elephant
Qarun, Haman, and Jalut
