explanationEn: Allah reminds mankind of how He dealt with mighty tyrants: 'Ad of lofty Iram, Thamud who hewed homes into valley cliffs, and Pharaoh of the stakes—for indeed 'your Lord is in observation (bil-mirsad).'

questionEn: What social failures of worldly-minded people are exposed in Surah Al-Fajr 89:17–20?
optionsEn: Hoarding books and arguing in markets
Neglecting pilgrimages and speaking hastily
Building tall ships and traveling in winter
Not honoring the orphan, not encouraging feeding the poor, devouring inheritance greedily, and loving wealth excessively
explanationEn: Allah refutes those who measure His favor by wealth alone, pointing out four moral failings: dishonoring orphans, failing to urge feeding the needy, consuming others' inheritance, and loving wealth with immense greed.

questionEn: How does Allah tenderly address the believer's soul at the conclusion of Surah Al-Fajr (89:27–30)?
optionsEn: 'O striving soul, rise above the stars'
'O victorious soul, wear the crown of light'
'O reassured/tranquil soul (an-nafs al-mutma'innah), return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]'
'O patient soul, rest beside the rivers'
explanationEn: In one of the Qur'an's most moving endings, Allah welcomes the serene, faithful soul back to Himself—well-pleased and pleasing—to enter among His righteous servants and enter His Paradise.

questionEn: Which city is meant by 'this city' (hadhal-balad) in the opening oath of Surah Al-Balad 90:1?
optionsEn: Jerusalem
Ta'if
Makkah
Madinah
explanationEn: Allah swears by Makkah ('this city'), honoring it further with 'while you, [O Muhammad], are free [to dwell] in this city.'

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Balad 90:4, in what state did Allah create human life in this world?
optionsEn: In complete isolation
In perpetual ease
In unbroken silence
In toil, struggle, and hardship (fi kabad)
explanationEn: Verse 4 states: 'We have certainly created man into hardship/toil (kabad)'—struggling through life's physical and spiritual tests.

questionEn: What deeds make up 'breaking through the steep, difficult path' (al-'aqabah) in Surah Al-Balad 90:11–16?
optionsEn: Freeing a slave, or feeding in a day of severe hunger an orphan of near relationship or a needy person in dust
Building stone bridges and digging wells
Memorizing poetry and gifting horses
Fasting three months and climbing Mount Safa
explanationEn: Allah defines the steep upward climb toward salvation as sacrificial compassion: emancipating captives/slaves and feeding hungry orphans (especially relatives) and destitute people during famine.

questionEn: What distinction does Surah Ash-Shams hold in the Qur'an regarding its opening?
optionsEn: It is the shortest surah beginning with an oath
It has no rhymes at the end of verses
It mentions every prophet by name
It contains the longest consecutive series of oaths in the Qur'an (swearing by 7 pairs/entities: sun, brightness, moon, day, night, heaven, earth, and the soul)
explanationEn: Surah Ash-Shams opens with a dramatic chain of consecutive oaths (sun, brightness, moon, day, night, sky and its building, earth and its spreading, and the soul and its proportioning) leading to the fate of the soul.

questionEn: What is the central conclusion following the oaths in Surah Ash-Shams 91:9–10?
optionsEn: 'He has succeeded who conquers empires'
'He has succeeded who travels at dawn'
'He has succeeded who purifies it [the soul], and he has failed who instills it [with corruption]'
'He has succeeded who stores grain for famine'
explanationEn: After inspiring the soul with awareness of wickedness and righteousness, Allah declares true success lies in purifying the soul (tazkiyah), while ruin lies in burying it in sin.

questionEn: Which prophet's people and specific crime are recounted as a warning at the end of Surah Ash-Shams (91:11–15)?
optionsEn: Thamud, who rejected Prophet Salih and hamstrung the she-camel of Allah
The people of Nuh who mocked the Ark
The people of Lut who assaulted travelers
The people of Shu'ayb who cheated in scales
explanationEn: Thamud in their transgression sent forth their most wretched man to hamstring the miraculous she-camel of Allah despite Salih's warning, so Allah leveled them completely.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Layl 92:5–7, which three qualities cause Allah to facilitate for a person 'the path of ease' (al-yusra)?
optionsEn: Sleeping early, waking late, and speaking little
Traveling, debating, and fasting
Building palaces, reading stars, and memorizing names
Giving in charity, fearing Allah (taqwa), and believing in the best reward (al-husna)
explanationEn: Allah promises: 'As for he who gives and fears Allah and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease (al-yusra).'

questionEn: What three opposite traits lead a person toward 'the path of hardship' (al-'usra) in Surah Al-Layl 92:8–10?
optionsEn: Being stingy, considering oneself free of need [of Allah], and denying the best reward
Traveling too far, working late, and resting little
Poverty, shyness, and quietness
Asking questions, writing notes, and weeping
explanationEn: By contrast, whoever withholds stingily, arrogantly imagines himself self-sufficient without Allah, and denies the truth will be facilitated toward difficulty and ruin.

questionEn: Whom do classical commentators such as Ibn Kathir identify as the prime example of 'al-atqa' (the most righteous one) who gives wealth to purify himself seeking only Allah's Face in Surah Al-Layl 92:17–21?
optionsEn: Khalid ibn al-Walid
Zayd ibn Harithah
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (RA), especially when freeing enslaved Muslims like Bilal
Salman al-Farisi
explanationEn: Commentators note that while the verse applies generally to every sincere giver, it was revealed regarding Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (RA), who spent his wealth freeing persecuted slaves solely seeking the countenance of Allah.

questionEn: Why was Surah Ad-Duha revealed to console the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: After a temporary pause in revelation (fatrat al-wahy) led mockers to claim his Lord had forsaken him
After the Battle of Uhud
When his camel went missing in the desert
Before entering Cave Thawr during Hijrah
explanationEn: When revelation paused briefly, some disbelievers taunted that Muhammad's Lord had abandoned him; Allah revealed Surah Ad-Duha assuring him: 'Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you].'

questionEn: Which three past favors does Allah remind the Prophet ﷺ of in Surah Ad-Duha 93:6–8?
optionsEn: Granting him horses, orchards, and scribes
Teaching him languages, medicine, and astronomy
Finding him an orphan and sheltering him, finding him unaware [of revelation] and guiding him, and finding him poor and enriching him
Giving him victory at Badr, Uhud, and Hunayn
explanationEn: Allah comforts the Prophet ﷺ with concrete evidence of past care: sheltering him as an orphan, guiding him when seeking truth, and enriching/contenting him when poor.

questionEn: What three ethical commands conclude Surah Ad-Duha (93:9–11) in gratitude for Allah's blessings?
optionsEn: Build stone gates, weave garments, and store dates
Do not oppress the orphan, do not repel the one who asks, and proclaim the favor of your Lord
Keep silent in gatherings, memorize genealogies, and stay indoors
Fast Mondays, pray at night, and travel widely
explanationEn: Matching the three blessings just recalled, Allah instructs: treat the orphan gently without oppression, never harshly turn away a seeker/beggar, and gratefully speak of Allah's favors.

questionEn: What comforting promise about the Prophet's ﷺ future is given in Surah Ad-Duha 93:4–5?
optionsEn: The Hereafter is better for him than the first [life], and his Lord will give him until he is well satisfied
He would rule Damascus in one year
All mountains around Makkah would turn to silver
He would never experience hunger again
explanationEn: Allah promises: 'And the Hereafter is better for you than the first [life], and your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied.'

questionEn: Which three special favors to the Prophet ﷺ open Surah Ash-Sharh (94:1–4)?
optionsEn: Giving him two gardens, three springs, and ten helpers
Expanding his chest, removing his burden, and raising high his mention (dhikr)
Granting him a sword, a banner, and a pulpit
Splitting the sea, parting clouds, and healing blindness
explanationEn: Allah asks tenderly: 'Did We not expand for you your breast, and remove from you your burden which had weighed upon your back, and raise high for you your renown?'

questionEn: What famous comforting principle is repeated twice in Surah Ash-Sharh 94:5–6?
optionsEn: 'Patience brings victory after seventy days'
'Prayer is the pillar of faith'
'For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease'
'Knowledge precedes action'
explanationEn: Surah Ash-Sharh states twice for emphasis: 'For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease. Indeed, with hardship [will be] ease'—where the same definite hardship ('al-'usr') is accompanied by two distinct forms of ease ('yusran').

questionEn: How does Surah Ash-Sharh 94:7–8 advise a believer to spend time once finished with immediate tasks or duties?
optionsEn: Indulge in idle entertainment
Boast of completed deeds
Wander aimlessly in markets
Stand up in earnest worship/striving (fansab) and turn your longing to your Lord
explanationEn: The closing verses instill continuous spiritual momentum: 'So when you have finished [your duties], then stand up [for worship], and to your Lord direct [your] longing.'

questionEn: Which four sacred symbols or places form the opening oaths of Surah At-Tin (95:1–3)?
optionsEn: The river, the sea, Mount Arafat, and Mina
The date palm, the pomegranate, Mount Uhud, and Madinah
The cedar, the vine, Cave Hira, and Jerusalem
The fig, the olive, Mount Sinai (Tur Sinin), and this secure city (Makkah)
explanationEn: Surah At-Tin swears by the fig and olive (symbolizing blessed lands of revelation in Syria/Palestine), Mount Sinai (where Musa spoke with Allah), and Makkah (the secure city of Muhammad ﷺ).

questionEn: In what form did Allah create mankind according to Surah At-Tin 95:4?
optionsEn: In eternal physical strength
In the best of stature / finest form (fi ahsani taqwim)
In a fragile shadow
In complete forgetfulness
explanationEn: Allah declares: 'We have certainly created man in the best of stature (fi ahsani taqwim)'—both physically upright and spiritually endowed with intellect and purpose.

questionEn: Who are spared from being returned to 'the lowest of the low' (asfala safilin) in Surah At-Tin 95:5–6?
optionsEn: Those who live past ninety years
Those born in sacred cities
Those who amass great libraries
Those who believe and do righteous deeds—for them is an uninterrupted reward
explanationEn: Only those who combine genuine faith with righteous deeds escape spiritual degradation and receive a reward that never ends (ajrun ghayru mamnun).

questionEn: According to Surah Al-'Alaq 96:6–7, what causes human beings to transgress beyond all bounds?
optionsEn: Traveling across oceans
Seeing themselves as self-sufficient / independent of Allah (an ra'ahustaghna)
Suffering hunger for three days
Living near high mountains
explanationEn: After reminding man of his humble origin and divine gift of knowledge, verse 6–7 diagnoses arrogance: 'No! Indeed, man transgresses because he sees himself self-sufficient.'

questionEn: With what direct command does the final verse of Surah Al-'Alaq (96:19) end, which is also a place of prostration (Sajdah at-Tilawah)?
optionsEn: 'Fast for seven consecutive days'
'Flee from the city at night'
'Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near [to Allah]'
'Write these words on parchment'
explanationEn: Responding to Abu Jahl's attempt to stop the Prophet ﷺ from praying at the Ka'bah, Allah commands: 'No! Do not obey him. But prostrate and draw near [to Allah].'

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Qadr 97:3 quantify the spiritual worth of Laylatul-Qadr (the Night of Decree)?
optionsEn: Better than ten pilgrimages
Better than one hundred nights
Equal to seventy years precisely
Better than a thousand months
explanationEn: Surah Al-Qadr announces: 'The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months'—worship in that single night surpasses more than 83 years of worship.

questionEn: Who is 'ar-Ruh' (the Spirit) who descends alongside the angels during Laylatul-Qadr in Surah Al-Qadr 97:4?
optionsEn: A cool desert breeze
The spirit of Prophet Ibrahim
The souls of martyrs
Angel Jibril (AS)
explanationEn: Classical commentators explain 'ar-Ruh' here refers specifically to Angel Jibril (AS), singled out by honor as he descends with the angels by Allah's permission for every matter.

questionEn: Until what exact time does the peace (salam) of Laylatul-Qadr last according to Surah Al-Qadr 97:5?
optionsEn: Until the third watch of night
Until midnight
Until noon the next day
Until the emergence of dawn (matla'il-fajr)
explanationEn: The closing verse describes the entire night as steeped in tranquility and safety: 'Peace it is until the emergence of dawn.'

questionEn: According to Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, to which Companion did the Prophet ﷺ say, 'Allah has commanded me to recite to you' Surah Al-Bayyinah?
optionsEn: Zayd ibn Thabit
Mu'adh ibn Jabal
Abdullah ibn Mas'ud
Ubayy ibn Ka'b
explanationEn: Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to recite 'Lam yakunilladhina kafaru' (Surah Al-Bayyinah) directly to Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA), who wept with joy upon hearing that Allah had mentioned him by name.

questionEn: What core duties constitute 'the religion of uprightness' (din al-qayyimah) summarized in Surah Al-Bayyinah 98:5?
optionsEn: Isolating oneself in caves and wearing wool
Building shrines and reciting genealogy
Fasting continuously and refusing marriage
Worshiping Allah with sincere devotion as upright monotheists (hunafa'), establishing prayer, and giving zakah
explanationEn: Verse 5 distills the perennial message of all prophets: 'And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth, and to establish prayer and give zakah. And that is the correct religion.'

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Bayyinah 98:7 describe those who believe and do righteous deeds?
optionsEn: As the silent dwellers of Eden
As the heirs of ancient kings
As the best of creatures / creation (khayr al-bariyyah)
As the guardians of the earth
explanationEn: In stark contrast to stubborn deniers called 'sharr al-bariyyah' (worst of creatures), believers who do good are honored as 'khayr al-bariyyah' (the best of creation), rewarded with Gardens of perpetual residence.

questionEn: In Surah Az-Zalzalah 99:4–5, why will the earth recount all its news (akhbaraha) on the Day of Resurrection?
optionsEn: Because your Lord will inspire/command it to do so
Because the sun will shine from the west
Because prophets will ask the mountains to speak
Because the oceans will dry up
explanationEn: When the earth shakes violently and casts out its burdens, it will testify to every deed done upon its surface 'because your Lord has inspired (awha) it.'

questionEn: How did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ describe the concluding verses of Surah Az-Zalzalah (99:7–8: 'So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it...') when asked about lesser deeds?
optionsEn: As the hidden verse of recompense
As the third pillar of charity
As 'the comprehensive, unique verse' (al-ayah al-jami'ah al-fadhdhah)
As the verse of travelers
explanationEn: When asked whether horses and donkeys are included in charity/accountability, the Prophet ﷺ replied that nothing was revealed to him specifically about them except 'this comprehensive, unique verse'—Az-Zalzalah 99:7–8.

questionEn: In what manner will people emerge from their graves on the Day described in Surah Az-Zalzalah 99:6?
optionsEn: In silent single file
Grouped by their wealth
Riding mounts of light
In scattered groups (ashtatan) to be shown their deeds
explanationEn: Verse 6 states that mankind will depart/emerge in separate groups (ashtatan) according to their faith and deeds so that they may see the exact record of what they did.

questionEn: What imagery opens Surah Al-'Adiyat (100:1–5) before addressing human ingratitude?
optionsEn: Sailboats gliding across dark seas
Charging war horses panting, striking sparks with their hooves, and raiding at dawn
Camels crossing sunlit dunes
Eagles circling above mountain peaks
explanationEn: Allah swears by galloping steeds panting breathlessly, striking sparks from stones, charging at dawn, kicking up dust, and penetrating into the midst of the enemy—highlighting loyalty even in animals compared to human ingratitude.

questionEn: What does the word 'kanud' mean in Surah Al-'Adiyat 100:6 ('Indeed mankind, to his Lord, is kanud')?
optionsEn: Eager for travel
Generous and patient
Forgetful of names
Ungrateful / stubbornly unthankful (counting hardships while forgetting blessings)
explanationEn: Al-Hasan al-Basri and classical scholars explain 'kanud' as one who remembers calamities and complains while overlooking countless favors from his Lord.

questionEn: According to the final verses of Surah Al-'Adiyat (100:9–10), what two hidden things will be brought to light on the Day of Judgment?
optionsEn: Hidden stars and deep springs
Unspoken dreams and distant travels
What is in the graves will be scattered forth, and what is in the breasts (hearts) will be made known
Buried silver and ancient manuscripts
explanationEn: Surah Al-'Adiyat warns that true accountability reaches both body and intention: graves will give up the dead, and the innermost secrets of hearts will be exposed.

questionEn: To what two vivid images does Surah Al-Qari'ah 101:4–5 compare people and mountains on the Day of the Striking Calamity?
optionsEn: People like rushing ants and mountains like dark clouds
People like falling leaves and mountains like melting wax
People like drifting sand and mountains like broken glass
People like scattered moths (al-farash al-mabthuth) and mountains like carded/fluffed wool (al-'ihn al-manfush)
explanationEn: In bewilderment, humanity scatters like disoriented moths around a flame, while mighty mountains disintegrate into weightless, fluffed wool.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Qari'ah 101:6–9, what determines whether a person enters 'a pleasant life' ('ishatin radiyah) or 'Hawiyah'?
optionsEn: Whether their scales of good deeds are heavy or light
The number of cities they visited
Whether they wept during sermons
Their lineage and homeland
explanationEn: Allah makes the criterion crystal clear: whoever's scales (mawazin) of righteous deeds are heavy enjoys a pleasing life, while whoever's scales are light has Hawiyah as his abode.

questionEn: How does the final verse of Surah Al-Qari'ah (101:11) define 'Hawiyah'?
optionsEn: A desert of endless wind
A freezing abyss of darkness
A silent prison beneath the sea
A blazing, intensely hot Fire (Narun hamiyah)
explanationEn: After asking rhetorically, 'And what can make you know what that is?', the final verse answers starkly: 'It is a Fire, intensely hot (Narun hamiyah).'

questionEn: What spiritual trap does the opening of Surah At-Takathur (102:1–2) expose?
optionsEn: Competition in worldly increase (wealth, numbers, status) distracting people until they visit the graves
Excessive fasting without rest
Spending too long writing poetry
Arguing over travel routes
explanationEn: Allah warns that rivalry in amassing worldly possessions and boasting of numbers keeps people heedless of the Hereafter until death overtakes them and they enter the graves.

questionEn: Which two degrees of certainty are explicitly named in Surah At-Takathur (102:5 and 102:7)?
optionsEn: Nur al-yaqin and sirr al-yaqin
Qawl al-yaqin and 'amal al-yaqin
Knowledge of certainty ('ilm al-yaqin) and vision/eye of certainty ('ayn al-yaqin)
Zann al-yaqin and haqq al-qalb
explanationEn: Surah At-Takathur tells humanity that if they only knew with certain knowledge ('ilm al-yaqin), they would take heed now—before inevitably seeing Hellfire with the eye of certainty ('ayn al-yaqin).

questionEn: What final accountability does the closing verse of Surah At-Takathur (102:8) announce?
optionsEn: Then you will surely be asked that Day about the blessings/pleasures (an-na'im)
You will be questioned about every dream you saw
You will be questioned only about debts of silver
You will be asked which city you preferred
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ explained that even simple blessings—cool water, shade, food, health, and security—are part of 'an-na'im' about which Allah will question us on the Day of Judgment.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-'Asr 103:1–3, which four qualities together save a person from being in utter loss?
optionsEn: Prayer, silence, trade, and courage
Faith (iman), righteous deeds ('amal salih), mutually advising to truth (haqq), and mutually advising to patience (sabr)
Wealth, lineage, eloquence, and strength
Knowledge, travel, fasting, and solitude
explanationEn: Surah Al-'Asr swears by time that all humanity is in loss except those who unite personal righteousness (faith and good deeds) with communal responsibility (enjoining truth and patience).

questionEn: Which great classical scholar famously said of Surah Al-'Asr, 'If Allah had sent down no other proof to His creation besides this surah, it would have sufficed them'?
optionsEn: Imam Al-Bukhari
Imam Abu Hanifah
Imam Ash-Shafi'i
Imam Malik ibn Anas
explanationEn: Imam Ash-Shafi'i (rahimahullah) remarked that if people reflected deeply upon Surah Al-'Asr alone, its four criteria for salvation would suffice as a complete blueprint for life.
reference: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Introduction to Surah Al-'Asr 103

questionEn: Why does Surah Al-'Asr swear by 'time' (al-'asr) immediately before declaring 'Indeed, mankind is in loss'?
optionsEn: Because winter nights are shorter than summer nights
Because time is human life's capital—spending it in heedlessness guarantees loss unless invested in faith, good deeds, truth, and patience
Because prayers are offered only at sunset
Because lunar months determine inheritance
explanationEn: Scholars note that time is the very vessel of human existence; every passing moment shrinks our remaining lifespan, putting everyone at a loss except those who fill their time with the four saving qualities.

questionEn: Which two sins of speech and attitude open the warning of Surah Al-Humazah 104:1?
optionsEn: Swearing false oaths in court and gossiping about kings
Boasting of ancestry and interrupting elders
Speaking hastily during prayer and raising one's voice
Every scorner/slanderer by gesture or word (humazah) and mocker/backbiter (lumazah)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Humazah pronounces woe upon 'humazah' (one who mocks/defames by actions, winks, or gestures) and 'lumazah' (one who backbites and wounds others with the tongue), alongside hoarding wealth.

questionEn: What delusion does the hoarder of wealth harbor in Surah Al-Humazah 104:3?
optionsEn: That his wealth will make him immortal (akhladah)
That his wealth will buy him prophethood
That his coins will protect him from rain
That angels will carry his gold to Paradise
explanationEn: Obsessed with accumulating and counting riches, the miser acts as though his wealth grants him permanence and immunity from death and accountability.

questionEn: What is unique about the fire of 'Al-Hutamah' (the Crusher) described in Surah Al-Humazah 104:6–7?
optionsEn: It burns only once every thousand years
It surrounds only the feet
It is Allah's kindled Fire that mounts/penetrates directly to the hearts (al-af'idah)
It freezes bones before burning them
explanationEn: Al-Hutamah crushes whatever enters it and reaches right into the hearts—the very seat of arrogance, greed, and contempt for others—enclosed over them in towering columns.

questionEn: Whose failed campaign to demolish the Ka'bah is commemorated in Surah Al-Fil?
optionsEn: Nimrod of Babylon
Abrahah, the Abyssinian viceroy of Yemen, and his army with the elephant
Heraclius of Byzantium
Kisra of Persia
explanationEn: In the Year of the Elephant (570 CE, the year of the Prophet's ﷺ birth), Abrahah marched with an elephant to destroy the Ka'bah, and Allah annihilated his army.

questionEn: What instruments did Allah send to destroy the Companions of the Elephant in Surah Al-Fil 105:3–4?
optionsEn: Birds in flocks (tayran ababil) pelting them with stones of baked clay (sijjil)
A sudden earthquake and flood
A blazing whirlwind from the Red Sea
Locusts and hailstones
explanationEn: Allah sent waves of birds carrying small stones of baked clay (sijjil), striking the invading army and turning them into the likeness of 'eaten straw' ('asfin ma'kul).

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Fil 105:5 describe the final state of Abrahah's mighty army?
optionsEn: Like chewed/eaten-up straw ('asfin ma'kul)
Like ashes scattered by dawn wind
Like statues frozen in sand
Like sunken ships in deep water
explanationEn: Verse 5 concludes that Allah reduced the proud military force to 'asfin ma'kul—straw/chaff chewed and trampled by livestock.

questionEn: Which two seasonal trade journeys of Quraysh are mentioned as favors of security in Surah Quraysh 106:2?
optionsEn: Spring to Madinah and summer to Oman
Winter to Abyssinia and summer to Iraq
The winter journey (to Yemen) and the summer journey (to Ash-Sham/Syria)
Spring to Persia and autumn to Egypt
explanationEn: Because of their status as custodians of the Sacred House (reinforced after the Elephant event), Quraysh traveled safely in winter to Yemen and in summer to Ash-Sham.

questionEn: In gratitude for their safe trade caravans, whom does Surah Quraysh 106:3 command Quraysh to worship?
optionsEn: The Lord of this House (the Ka'bah)
The angels of the desert
The ancestral guardians of Makkah
The stars guiding caravans
explanationEn: Allah calls Quraysh back to pure monotheism: 'Let them worship the Lord of this House'—rather than the idols they placed around it.

questionEn: Which two essential blessings did the Lord of the Ka'bah bestow upon Quraysh according to the final verse of Surah Quraysh (106:4)?
optionsEn: Immense armies and stone walls
Feeding them against hunger and securing them against fear
Ships and fertile rivers
Rain and gold mines
explanationEn: In an arid, turbulent region, Allah protected Makkah's people from famine and constant tribal raids—providing both sustenance ('at'amahum min ju'') and safety ('amanahum min khawf').

questionEn: In the opening verses of Surah Al-Ma'un (107:1–3), which two behaviors characterize 'the one who denies the Recompense' (ad-din)?
optionsEn: Harshly repelling/pushing away the orphan and not encouraging the feeding of the needy
Sleeping late and forgetting travel prayers
Refusing to lend horses and arguing over poetry
Wearing coarse wool and staying silent
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ma'un links disbelief in final accountability directly to social cruelty: mistreating the vulnerable orphan and showing apathy toward feeding the poor.

questionEn: For which three faults does Surah Al-Ma'un 107:4–7 pronounce 'Woe to those who pray'?
optionsEn: Being heedless/neglectful of their prayers (sahun), doing deeds to be seen by people (yura'un), and withholding small kindnesses (al-ma'un)
Praying softly, praying slowly, and praying alone
Praying while seated, traveling, or fasting
Reciting short surahs, standing briefly, and leaving early
explanationEn: The warning targets hypocritical worship: delaying or being careless about prayer ('an salatihim sahun—note 'an, not fi), showing off before people (riya'), and refusing everyday neighborly help (al-ma'un).

questionEn: What does 'al-ma'un' signify in the closing verse of Surah Al-Ma'un (107:7)?
optionsEn: Annual tributes paid to rulers
Small, everyday acts of kindness and useful items lent to neighbors (such as a bucket, pot, salt, or water)
Gold coins stored for travel
Hidden treasures beneath homes
explanationEn: Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, and classical scholars explain 'al-ma'un' as ordinary household necessities or small favors people borrow from neighbors (e.g., a cooking pot, axe, bucket, or water) as well as obligatory charity.

questionEn: What distinction does Surah Al-Kawthar (Surah 108) hold regarding its length in the Qur'an?
optionsEn: It has the longest single verse in Juz Amma
It is the shortest surah revealed in Madinah
It contains only one sentence of three words
It is the shortest surah in the entire Qur'an, consisting of 3 verses
explanationEn: Surah Al-Kawthar is the shortest surah in the Qur'an with only three brief yet profoundly rich verses, promising the Prophet ﷺ abundant good.

questionEn: In authentic Hadith recorded in Sahih Muslim, how did the Prophet ﷺ explain 'Al-Kawthar' to his Companions?
optionsEn: As the city of Madinah
As the wealth of Persia
As a river in Paradise given to him by his Lord, abundant in goodness, where his Ummah will gather
As the Black Stone of the Ka'bah
explanationEn: Anas ibn Malik (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ woke smiling and said Surah Al-Kawthar had just been revealed, explaining Al-Kawthar as a river in Paradise promised to him by Allah, brimming with goodness (and scholars note it also encompasses all abundant good).

questionEn: What two acts of devotion is the Prophet ﷺ commanded to perform in gratitude in Surah Al-Kawthar 108:2?
optionsEn: Pray to your Lord and sacrifice (fasalli li-rabbika wanhar)
Weep and remain silent
Travel and teach
Fast and migrate
explanationEn: Surah Al-Kawthar instructs exclusive devotion to Allah in both prayer and ritual sacrifice, refuting idolaters who mocked the Prophet ﷺ as 'cut off' (abtar) after his sons passed away.

questionEn: What occasion led to the revelation of Surah Al-Kafirun?
optionsEn: The Battle of Badr
A debate with monks in Najran
Quraysh leaders proposed a compromise where the Prophet ﷺ would worship their idols for a year if they worshiped Allah for a year
The treaty of Hudaybiyyah
explanationEn: Polytheist leaders offered a syncretic bargain—alternating worship between idols and Allah; Allah revealed Surah Al-Kafirun to establish absolute, uncompromising disavowal of shirk.

questionEn: What does the closing declaration 'Lakum dinukum wa liya din' ('For you is your religion, and for me is my religion') in Surah Al-Kafirun 109:6 establish?
optionsEn: Clear separation between monotheism and polytheism—refusing compromise in worship while maintaining no forced conversion
That believers should leave Makkah immediately
That prophets worship differently each year
That all religions teach the same worship
explanationEn: The verse affirms absolute rejection of polytheism and religious syncretism while clearly defining distinct accountability: disbelievers bear their path, and the Prophet ﷺ adheres exclusively to Islam.

questionEn: In which two daily Sunnah prayers did the Prophet ﷺ regularly pair Surah Al-Kafirun (in the first rak'ah) with Surah Al-Ikhlas (in the second rak'ah)?
optionsEn: The two Sunnah rak'ahs before Fajr and the two Sunnah rak'ahs after Maghrib (as well as after Tawaf)
Witr and Duha
Before Dhuhr and after Asr
Tarawih and Tahajjud
explanationEn: Authentic narrations in Sahih Muslim and Tirmidhi report that the Prophet ﷺ recited Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun and Qul huwallahu ahad in the two rak'ahs of Fajr Sunnah, Maghrib Sunnah, and behind Maqam Ibrahim after Tawaf.

questionEn: In narrations recorded by At-Tirmidhi, what fraction of the Qur'an is Surah Al-Kafirun compared to in reward?
optionsEn: One-half of the Qur'an
One-tenth of the Qur'an
One-seventh of the Qur'an
One-fourth (a quarter) of the Qur'an
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas and Anas (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said 'Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun' is equivalent to a fourth of the Qur'an, and recommended reciting it before sleep as a declaration of freedom from shirk.

questionEn: When Allah's help and victory arrive and people enter Islam in crowds in Surah An-Nasr 110:3, what three actions is the Prophet ﷺ instructed to perform?
optionsEn: Build fortresses, collect taxes, and celebrate with feasts
Travel to Yemen, write letters, and fast a month
Divide spoils, appoint governors, and rest
Exalt his Lord with praise (tasbih & hamd) and seek His forgiveness (istighfar)
explanationEn: Rather than triumphalism at victory, Surah An-Nasr teaches humility and gratitude: 'Then exalt [Him] with praise of your Lord and ask forgiveness of Him. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.'

questionEn: Which young Companion correctly explained to Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) and the veterans of Badr that Surah An-Nasr signaled the approaching passing of the Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: Usamah ibn Zayd
Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA)
Al-Hasan ibn Ali
Zayd ibn Thabit
explanationEn: While senior Companions saw only the command to praise Allah upon victory, Ibn Abbas (RA) recognized it as an announcement of the Prophet's ﷺ completed mission and near departure—which Umar (RA) confirmed.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Baqarah, what did Allah teach Adam (AS) that demonstrated his superiority over the angels regarding stewardship on earth?
optionsEn: The secret of writing with iron
The names of all things
The languages of the stars
The laws of the seven oceans
explanationEn: Allah taught Adam (AS) the names of all things, then presented them to the angels, who admitted they had no knowledge except what He had taught them.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah, which reason did Iblis give for refusing to prostrate to Adam (AS) when commanded by Allah?
optionsEn: He argued that angels were forbidden from bowing to mortals
He was arrogant and considered himself better, created from fire whereas Adam was from clay
He claimed Adam had not yet repented for eating from the tree
He claimed he was created from light while Adam was from water
explanationEn: In Surah Al-A'raf and Al-Baqarah, Iblis refused out of arrogance; in Surah Al-A'raf 7:12 he explicitly stated, 'I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay.'

questionEn: According to Surah Taha, what did Allah warn Adam (AS) and his wife would happen if they were driven out of Paradise due to Iblis?
optionsEn: They would lose their ability to speak
They would suffer toil and misery on earth
They would be turned into angels of lesser rank
They would never be allowed to return to worship
explanationEn: Allah warned Adam that Iblis was an enemy to him and his wife, saying, 'So let him not drive you out of Paradise so that you would suffer.'

questionEn: How did Shaytan deceive Adam (AS) and his wife into eating from the forbidden tree according to Surah Taha?
optionsEn: He told them the tree would give them command over the wind
He claimed the tree's fruit was needed to feed the birds of Paradise
He disguised himself as an angel bringing a new revelation
He promised them the tree would grant eternal life and a kingdom that never decays
explanationEn: Shaytan whispered to Adam, 'O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that will not deteriorate?'

questionEn: In Surah Al-A'raf, what words of repentance did Adam (AS) and his wife say after eating from the forbidden tree?
optionsEn: My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom unlike any after me
Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers
Glory be to You, we were among the heedless
There is no deity except You, exalted are You; indeed we have been wrongdoers
explanationEn: Adam and Hawwa' supplicated: 'Rabbana zalamna anfusana wa in lam taghfir lana wa tarhamna lanakunanna minal-khasirin.'

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Baqarah, what enabled Adam (AS) to turn back to Allah in repentance and be forgiven?
optionsEn: He wept until the angels interceded for him
He fasted for forty consecutive days in Makkah
He built an altar of stone and offered a sacrifice
He received specific words from his Lord, and Allah accepted his repentance
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah states: 'Then Adam received from his Lord [some] words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah's account of the two sons of Adam, why did the righteous son refuse to raise his hand to kill his brother?
optionsEn: He feared Allah, the Lord of the worlds
Their father Adam forbade him from touching weapons
He was physically weaker than his brother
He had taken a vow of silence that day
explanationEn: The righteous brother said, 'If you should raise your hand against me to kill me, I shall not raise my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.'

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Ma'idah, which creature did Allah send to show the murderous son of Adam how to bury his brother's corpse?
optionsEn: An ant digging a burrow
A hoopoe bird
A crow scratching in the ground
A desert fox
explanationEn: Allah sent a crow (ghurab) scratching in the ground to show him how to hide the dead body of his brother.

questionEn: What moral principle does Allah immediately establish in Surah Al-Ma'idah right after recounting the story of Adam's two sons?
optionsEn: Whoever saves one life, it is as if he had saved all of mankind
No prophet is ever sent without a scripture
Charity extinguishes anger just as water extinguishes fire
Every soul must taste water before returning to clay
explanationEn: Because of that, Allah decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely; and whoever saves one, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely.

questionEn: In Surah Al-A'raf, while addressing the Children of Adam about clothing, what does the Qur'an declare to be the best garment?
optionsEn: Silk from Paradise
Woven wool of sheep
White linen
The garment of righteousness (libas al-taqwa)
explanationEn: Allah says: 'O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts and as adornment. But the clothing of righteousness (libas al-taqwa) — that is best.'

questionEn: According to Surah Al-A'raf, what testimony did Allah take from the descendants of Adam when He brought them forth from their loins?
optionsEn: To testify 'Am I not your Lord?' to which they replied, 'Yes, we have testified'
To testify that Jibril is the foremost of angels
To memorize the names of all twenty-five prophets
To pledge to make pilgrimage to Makkah every year
explanationEn: Allah took from the children of Adam from their loins their descendants and made them testify of themselves, asking, 'Am I not your Lord?' They said, 'Yes, we have testified.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hijr, what specific type of clay does the Qur'an mention Allah used to create the human being (Adam)?
optionsEn: Pebbles gathered from Mount Sinai
Pure white limestone
Red desert sandstone
Sounding clay of altered black mud (salsalin min hama'in masnun)
explanationEn: Allah says in Surah Al-Hijr: 'And We did certainly create man out of clay from an altered black mud (salsalin min hama'in masnun).'

questionEn: How is Prophet Idris (AS) described in Surah Maryam regarding his status and character?
optionsEn: A king who ruled over Egypt for seventy years
A man of truth and a prophet whom Allah raised to a high station
A builder of ships who crossed the Red Sea
A prophet whose rod turned into a flowing stream
explanationEn: Surah Maryam states: 'And mention in the Book, Idris. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet. And We raised him to a high station.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anbiya, alongside which two prophets is Dhul-Kifl (AS) praised as being among the steadfast and patient (as-sabirin)?
optionsEn: Isma'il and Idris
Musa and Harun
Dawud and Sulayman
Zakariyya and Yahya
explanationEn: Allah says: 'And [mention] Isma'il and Idris and Dhul-Kifl; all were of the patient. And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were of the righteous.'

questionEn: In Surah Sad, which three prophets are grouped together and described as 'all among the best/chosen' (min al-akhyar)?
optionsEn: Nuh, Hud, and Salih
Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Ya'qub
Yusuf, Ayyub, and Yunus
Isma'il, Al-Yasa', and Dhul-Kifl
explanationEn: Surah Sad 38:48 reads: 'And remember Isma'il, Al-Yasa' (Elisha), and Dhul-Kifl, and all are among the outstanding/chosen (min al-akhyar).'

questionEn: In Surah Al-An'am, Prophet Al-Yasa' (AS) is listed among the prophets favored above the worlds alongside which group?
optionsEn: Isma'il, Yunus, and Lut
Zayd, Bilal, and Abu Bakr
Talut, Qarun, and Luqman
Habil, Qabil, and Khidr
explanationEn: Surah Al-An'am 6:86 names 'Isma'il and Al-Yasa' and Yunus and Lut — and all [of them] We preferred over the worlds.'

questionEn: What specific spiritual reward does Surah Al-Anbiya affirm Allah granted to Idris, Isma'il, and Dhul-Kifl (AS) for their patience?
optionsEn: He sent down a table spread from heaven for them
He admitted them into His mercy because they were of the righteous
He made fire cool and safe for all three
He granted them dominion over the jinn
explanationEn: Immediately after naming Isma'il, Idris, and Dhul-Kifl as being of the patient, Allah states: 'And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were of the righteous.'

questionEn: Which Surah contains the Qur'anic mention of Idris (AS) immediately preceding the mention of the prophets blessed from the descendants of Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, and Isra'il?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Qasas
Surah Al-Mu'minun
Surah Ash-Shu'ara
Surah Maryam
explanationEn: In Surah Maryam 19:56-58, after mentioning Idris (AS), Allah summarizes that those were the prophets upon whom He bestowed favor from the descendants of Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, and Isra'il.

questionEn: Immediately after naming Idris, Ibrahim, Isma'il, Musa, Harun, and other prophets in Surah Maryam, how does the Qur'an describe their response when the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them?
optionsEn: They fell down in prostration and weeping (kharru sujjadan wa bukiyya)
They stood in silent meditation until dawn
They recited them aloud in the marketplace
They wrote them upon tablets of silver
explanationEn: Surah Maryam 19:58 states of those prophets upon whom Allah bestowed favor: 'When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell in prostration and weeping.'

questionEn: Which five idols are explicitly named in Surah Nuh as deities that Nuh's people refused to abandon?
optionsEn: Al-Lat, Al-'Uzza, Manat, Hubal, and Ba'l
Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr
Sawa', Isaf, Na'ilah, Dagon, and Moloch
Suwa', Manat, Wadd, Ba'l, and Shams
explanationEn: The leaders of Nuh's people said: 'Never leave your gods and never leave Wadd or Suwa' or Yaghuth and Ya'uq and Nasr.'

questionEn: In Surah Hud, what was the mocking insult used by the elite disbelievers of Nuh's people against those who followed him?
optionsEn: They mocked them for building stone temples in the desert
They accused his followers of being sorcerers from Babylon
They said his followers were wealthy merchants from Egypt
They claimed his followers were only the lowest/meanest of them with hasty judgment
explanationEn: The chiefs said: 'We do not see you but as a man like ourselves, and we do not see you followed except by those who are the lowest of us [and] at first glance.'

questionEn: According to Surah Hud, what sign marked the beginning of the Flood when Allah commanded Nuh (AS) to load the Ark?
optionsEn: Three days of continuous thunder shook the valleys
The stars disappeared from the night sky
A comet fell into the Euphrates
The oven (at-tannur) gushed forth with water
explanationEn: Allah told Nuh: 'Until when Our command comes and the oven (at-tannur) overflows, load upon the ship of each [creature] two mates and your family...'

questionEn: In Surah Hud, when Nuh (AS) called his disbelieving son to board the Ark, how did the son respond?
optionsEn: He said he would take refuge on a mountain that would protect him from the water
He claimed the rain had already stopped
He asked for a smaller boat of his own
He mocked the Ark for having no sails
explanationEn: Nuh's son replied, 'I will take refuge on a mountain to protect me from the water.' Nuh answered, 'There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for whom He gives mercy.'

questionEn: When Nuh (AS) pleaded with Allah about his drowned son in Surah Hud, why did Allah say his son was not of his family?
optionsEn: Because he was older than Nuh's other sons
Because he had left the city before Nuh built the Ark
Because his conduct was unrighteous (innahu 'amalun ghayru salih)
Because he was adopted from another tribe
explanationEn: Allah said: 'O Nuh, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is [one whose] work was other than righteous, so ask Me not for that about which you have no knowledge.'

questionEn: Upon which mountain does Surah Hud explicitly state that the Ark of Nuh (AS) came to rest?
optionsEn: Mount Tur (Sinai)
Mount Uhud
Mount Arafat
Mount Judi
explanationEn: Surah Hud states: 'And it was said, "O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold [your rain]." And the water subsided, and the matter was accomplished, and the ship came to rest on the [mountain of] Judi.'

questionEn: In Surah Nuh, how did Nuh (AS) describe his people's physical reaction whenever he called them to Allah so He might forgive them?
optionsEn: They thrust their fingers into their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and grew intensely arrogant
They fled across the sea in wooden boats
They threw stones at his house
They burned his written scrolls
explanationEn: Nuh complained to Allah: 'Indeed, every time I invited them that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and were arrogant with [great] arrogance.'

questionEn: In Surah At-Tahrim, how is the wife of Prophet Nuh (AS) presented alongside the wife of Prophet Lut (AS)?
optionsEn: As an example for those who disbelieve, because both betrayed their righteous husbands and were not availed against Allah
As mothers of future prophets
As righteous martyrs who perished in the flood
As women who repented at the last moment
explanationEn: Allah sets forth an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Nuh and the wife of Lut; they were under two of Our righteous servants but betrayed them, so those prophets did not avail them anything against Allah.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mu'minun, what supplication did Allah instruct Nuh (AS) to say upon settling aboard the Ark?
optionsEn: Our Lord, pour upon us patience and let us die as Muslims
My Lord, grant me entry into a blessed landing, for You are the best of those who bring to land
Glory be to Him who subjected this to us
All praise is due to Allah who has saved us from the wrongdoing people
explanationEn: Allah commanded Nuh: 'And when you have boarded the ship, you and those with you, then say, "Praise to Allah who has saved us from the wrongdoing people."' And also say, 'My Lord, let me land at a blessed landing place, and You are the best to accommodate [us].'

questionEn: What comprehensive prayer for forgiveness did Nuh (AS) make at the very end of Surah Nuh?
optionsEn: Forgive me, my parents, whoever enters my house as a believer, and all believing men and believing women
Forgive all the people of the earth after the waters subside
Forgive only my sons who boarded the ship with me
Grant me a righteous son to inherit my prophethood
explanationEn: Nuh prayed: 'My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house a believer and the believing men and believing women.'

questionEn: To which people was Prophet Hud (AS) sent as their brother and messenger according to the Qur'an?
optionsEn: The people of 'Ad
Thamud
The people of Madyan
The Companions of Ar-Rass
explanationEn: Allah states in Surah Hud and Surah Al-A'raf: 'And to 'Ad [We sent] their brother Hud.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ahqaf, what geographical region is named as the place where Hud (AS) warned his people?
optionsEn: The Plains of Madyan
Al-Hijr
The Valley of Bakkah
Al-Ahqaf (the curved sand-hills)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ahqaf 46:21 states: 'And mention, [O Muhammad], the brother of 'Ad, when he warned his people in the [region of] Al-Ahqaf...'

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Fajr uniquely describe the city of Iram associated with the people of 'Ad?
optionsEn: Iram of the sunken gardens
Iram of the seven iron gates
Iram of the golden domes
Iram of the lofty pillars, the like of which had never been created in the lands
explanationEn: Allah asks: 'Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Ad — [with] Iram — who had lofty pillars, the likes of whom had never been created in the land?'

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shu'ara, what architectural vanity did Hud (AS) rebuke the people of 'Ad for practicing?
optionsEn: Constructing a towering monument/landmark on every high place just for amusement, and taking fortresses hoping to live forever
Carving palaces out of coral reefs
Damming rivers to starve neighboring tribes
Building idols of solid silver inside caves
explanationEn: Hud asked them: 'Do you construct on every elevation a sign [i.e., monument] amusing yourselves, and take for yourselves palaces and fortresses that you might abide eternally?'

questionEn: In Surah Fussilat, what arrogant boast did the people of 'Ad make that provoked Allah's punishment?
optionsEn: 'Our gods will silence the wind'
'We possess the keys to the heavens'
'Who is mightier than us in strength?'
'No flood can reach our stone pillars'
explanationEn: The people of 'Ad grew arrogant upon the earth without right and said, 'Who is greater than us in strength?' Did they not see that Allah who created them was greater than them in strength?

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Haqqah, for how long did the furious, roaring wind blow continuously against the people of 'Ad?
optionsEn: Three days and three nights
Seven nights and eight days in succession
Forty days and forty nights
Twelve nights and thirteen days
explanationEn: Allah destroyed 'Ad by a screaming, violent wind which He imposed upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, leaving them fallen like hollow trunks of palm trees.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ahqaf, what did the people of 'Ad mistakenly think when they first saw the punishment approaching their valleys?
optionsEn: They thought it was a rain cloud bringing them welcome rain
They thought it was smoke from distant caravan fires
They thought it was an army of angels coming to serve them
They thought it was a passing sandstorm from Thamud
explanationEn: When they saw it as a dense cloud approaching their valleys, they said, 'This is a cloud bringing us rain!' Rather, it was that for which they were impatient: a wind within which was a painful punishment.

questionEn: In Surah Hud, what insult did the chiefs of 'Ad hurl at Hud (AS) to explain why he rejected their gods?
optionsEn: They said he was too young to speak in council
They claimed he had stolen gold from their temple
They accused him of spying for Egypt
They claimed one of their gods had struck him with evil/madness
explanationEn: They said, 'We only say that some of our gods have possessed you with evil [madness].' Hud replied, 'Indeed, I call Allah to witness, and witness [yourselves] that I am free from whatever you associate with Him.'

questionEn: What striking comparison does Surah Al-Qamar use to describe the uprooted bodies of 'Ad during the furious wind?
optionsEn: Like moths caught in a flame
As if they were trunks of palm trees uprooted
Like withered leaves in autumn
Like scattered pebbles on a riverbank
explanationEn: Surah Al-Qamar states that the furious wind plucked away the people 'as if they were trunks of palm trees uprooted.'

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shu'ara, besides calling them to worship Allah, what did Hud (AS) remind the people of 'Ad that Allah had blessed them with?
optionsEn: Manna from the sky and twelve rivers
Ships of cedar, pearls, and tin mines
Livestock, children, gardens, and springs
Iron armor and horses of war
explanationEn: Hud reminded them: 'And fear He who provided you with that which you know: He provided you with grazing livestock and children and gardens and springs.'

questionEn: How were the people of Thamud instructed to share the water supply with Salih's she-camel according to Surah Al-Qamar?
optionsEn: The camel drank only at midnight
They could drink simultaneously from opposite banks
Only the poor could drink on the camel's day
Every drink of water was divided between them in turns — one day for the camel, the next for them
explanationEn: Allah told Salih: 'And inform them that the water is shared between them, each [day of] drink attended [by turn].'

questionEn: According to Surah Ash-Shu'ara and Surah Al-A'raf, what remarkable skill were the people of Thamud known for in their architecture?
optionsEn: Skillfully carving homes out of mountains
Building floating palaces on rivers
Constructing pyramids of baked mud
Hanging bridges between mountain peaks
explanationEn: Salih reminded them: 'And you carve out of the mountains, homes, with great skill.'

questionEn: In Surah An-Naml, how many corrupt leaders (raht) in the city of Thamud plotted a secret night attack against Salih (AS) and his family?
optionsEn: Three
Seven
Nine
Twelve
explanationEn: Surah An-Naml states: 'And there were in the city nine family heads (tis'atu rahtin) who caused corruption in the land and did not reform.' They swore by Allah to attack Salih and his family by night.

questionEn: After the people of Thamud hamstrung the she-camel, how many days did Salih (AS) tell them to enjoy themselves in their homes before the punishment struck?
optionsEn: Ten days
Seven days
One day
Three days
explanationEn: After they hamstrung her, Salih said: 'Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise not to be denied.'

questionEn: What name does Surah Al-Hijr give to the dwelling place/valley of the people of Thamud?
optionsEn: Bakkah
Al-Ahqaf
Al-Hijr
Tihamah
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hijr 15:80-82 recounts: 'And certainly did the companions of Al-Hijr (Ashab al-Hijr) deny the messengers... And they used to carve from the mountains, houses, feeling secure.'

questionEn: According to Surah Hud and Surah Al-A'raf, what seized the wrongdoers of Thamud at sunrise on the fourth day?
optionsEn: A swarm of locusts and hail
A burning wind for eight consecutive days
The mighty blast / shriek (as-sayhah) and earthquake, leaving them fallen face-down in their homes
A flood of boiling tar
explanationEn: Surah Hud 11:67 says 'the shriek (as-sayhah) seized those who had wronged, and they became within their homes [corpses] fallen prone'; Surah Al-A'raf 7:78 mentions the earthquake (ar-rajfah).

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shams, how did the people of Thamud react when the most wretched man among them stepped forward to kill the she-camel?
optionsEn: They offered Salih a hundred camels in exchange
They all shared in the rejection and crime, so Allah leveled their doom upon them equally
They tried to stop him but failed
Only the nine leaders approved while the rest wept
explanationEn: Surah Ash-Shams states: 'Thamud denied [their prophet] by reason of their transgression, when the most wretched of them was sent forth... But they denied him and hamstrung her, so their Lord brought down upon them destruction for their sin and made it equal [upon all of them].'

questionEn: In Surah Hud, what emotional remark did the people of Thamud make to Salih (AS) when he forbade them from worshipping their fathers' idols?
optionsEn: 'You are nothing but a stranger from a distant land'
'Ask your Lord to turn our mountains into gold'
'O Salih, you were among us a figure of hope before this!'
'Leave our valley and take the camel with you'
explanationEn: They said: 'O Salih, you were among us a man of promise/hope before this. Do you forbid us to worship what our fathers worshipped?'

questionEn: In Surah Al-A'raf, what did Salih (AS) say to his destroyed people as he turned away from them after the punishment?
optionsEn: 'May your mountain homes stand as temples forever'
'O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you, but you do not like advisors'
'I wish I had built an ark for you'
'I will pray for rain to wash away your ruins'
explanationEn: Salih turned away from them and said: 'O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you, but you do not like advisors.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-An'am, what three celestial phenomena did Ibrahim (AS) successively examine before declaring 'I do not love those that set'?
optionsEn: A comet, an eclipse, and a rainbow
Mars, Venus, and the full moon
Lightning, clouds, and the North Star
A star, the moon, and the sun
explanationEn: When night covered him, Ibrahim saw a star, then the moon rising, then the sun rising; when each set, he declared his disassociation from shirk and turned his face exclusively to the Creator of the heavens and the earth.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Anbiya, when Ibrahim (AS) broke his people's idols into pieces, which idol did he leave intact?
optionsEn: An idol shaped like an eagle
The smallest idol near the door
A golden idol belonging to the king
The largest one among them (kabiran lahum), so they might question it
explanationEn: Surah Al-Anbiya states: 'So he made them into fragments, except a large one among them, that they might return to it [and question].'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah, how did Ibrahim (AS) silence the arrogant king who claimed 'I give life and cause death'?
optionsEn: By asking him to raise a dead bird before the court
By challenging him to turn a dry staff into a serpent
By predicting the exact hour of his death
By challenging him: 'Indeed, Allah brings up the sun from the east, so bring it up from the west'
explanationEn: When the ruler claimed he controlled life and death, Ibrahim said, 'Indeed, Allah brings up the sun from the east, so bring it up from the west.' So the disbeliever was overwhelmed/confounded.

questionEn: When Ibrahim (AS) asked Allah in Surah Al-Baqarah to show him how He gives life to the dead so his heart might be reassured, what did Allah instruct him to do?
optionsEn: Throw dust into the river and watch fish appear
Gather bones from an ancient battlefield and blow upon them
Plant four seeds in barren sand and watch them sprout
Take four birds, incline/cut them to himself, place a part on each hill, then call them
explanationEn: Allah told him: 'Take four birds and incline them to yourself [cutting them into parts]; then put on each hill a portion of them; then call them — they will come [flying] to you in haste.'

questionEn: According to Surah Ibrahim, why did Ibrahim (AS) pray that Allah make the hearts of people incline toward his family left in the uncultivated valley of Makkah?
optionsEn: So they could build a massive military fortress
So they could establish regular prayer (salah) and be grateful for the fruits provided
So they could search for gold mines in the Hijaz
So they could escape the heat of Syria
explanationEn: Ibrahim prayed: 'Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits that they might be grateful.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah, what supplication did Ibrahim (AS) and Isma'il (AS) recite together as they raised the foundations of the Ka'bah?
optionsEn: 'Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing'
'Our Lord, grant us a kingdom greater than Babylon'
'Our Lord, make its stones shine like stars'
'Our Lord, surround this house with walls of iron'
explanationEn: As Ibrahim and Isma'il raised the foundations of the House, they prayed: 'Rabbana taqabbal minna innaka Antas-Sami'ul-'Alim.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah, what did Ibrahim (AS) pray Allah would raise up from among his descendants in Makkah?
optionsEn: Angels to guard the Ka'bah visibly
Twelve tribal kings to rule from Jerusalem to Yemen
A messenger from among them who would recite Allah's verses, teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them
A spring of honey beneath the Black Stone
explanationEn: Ibrahim and Isma'il prayed: 'Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them.'

questionEn: In Surah As-Saffat, how did Ibrahim's son respond when Ibrahim (AS) told him of the dream in which he saw himself sacrificing him?
optionsEn: He fled toward the mountains of Arafat
He said: 'O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast'
He asked for three days to bid farewell to his mother
He asked his father to wait until he grew older
explanationEn: The son replied immediately with submission: 'O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast (as-sabirin).'

questionEn: According to Surah As-Saffat, with what did Allah ransom Ibrahim's son after both had submitted and he had laid him upon his forehead?
optionsEn: Forty camels from Makkah
A great sacrifice ('dhibhin 'azim')
A golden ram descending on a cloud
A white bull from Syria
explanationEn: Allah called out to Ibrahim that he had fulfilled the vision, and stated: 'And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice (bi-dhibhin 'azim).'

questionEn: According to Surah Hud, why did Ibrahim's wife Sarah laugh and express amazement when the angels gave glad tidings of Ishaq and Ya'qub?
optionsEn: She thought the guests were joking about the food
She had already been told she would have only daughters
She believed they were still living in Ur
She was barren and old, and her husband was an old man
explanationEn: She struck her face/forehead (in 51:29) and said (in 11:72): 'Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this, my husband, is an old man? Indeed, this is an amazing thing!'

questionEn: In Surah An-Nisa, by what affectionate title does Allah specifically designate Prophet Ibrahim (AS)?
optionsEn: Sayyid al-Mursalin
Khalil (Intimate Friend of Allah)
Kalimullah (One to whom Allah spoke)
Ruhullah (Spirit from Allah)
explanationEn: Allah declares in Surah An-Nisa: 'And Allah took Ibrahim as an intimate friend (khalilan).'

questionEn: In Surah An-Nahl, what collective term does Allah apply to Prophet Ibrahim (AS) alone because of his comprehensive devotion and obedience?
optionsEn: An Ummah (a comprehensive leader/nation unto himself), devoutly obedient to Allah, inclining toward truth (hanif)
A king over all the prophets
The scribe of the preserved tablet
The pillar of the Ka'bah
explanationEn: Surah An-Nahl states: 'Indeed, Ibrahim was a [comprehensive] leader (ummah), devoutly obedient to Allah, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah.'

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Mumtahanah, what was the single exception in Ibrahim's exemplary pattern (uswah hasanah) that believers are told NOT to imitate?
optionsEn: His breaking of the idols
His migration from Iraq to Syria
His hospitality to strangers
His promise to ask forgiveness for his idol-worshipping father, once it became clear he was an enemy to Allah
explanationEn: Surah Al-Mumtahanah 60:4 praises the excellent pattern in Ibrahim and those with him, 'except for the saying of Ibrahim to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you, though I have not [power to do] for you anything against Allah."' Surah At-Tawbah 9:114 clarifies he disassociated from him once it became clear he was an enemy of Allah.

questionEn: In Surah Hud, why did Ibrahim (AS) dispute/plead with Allah's angels once fear left him after learning they were sent to the people of Lut?
optionsEn: He feared the destruction might touch his own flocks
He wanted to travel to Sodom to debate their chiefs
He asked that the punishment be delayed by ten years
He was forbearing, tender-hearted, and turning to Allah, hoping Lut's people might be spared
explanationEn: Surah Hud explains: 'And when the fright had left Ibrahim and the good tidings had reached him, he began to argue with Us concerning the people of Lut. Indeed, Ibrahim was forbearing, grieving/tender-hearted, and returning [to Allah].'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah, when Ibrahim (AS) was tested by his Lord with certain commands and fulfilled them, what did Allah make him?
optionsEn: The guardian of Mount Sinai
The angel of the Ka'bah
The ruler of Babylon
An Imam (spiritual leader) for mankind
explanationEn: Allah told him: 'Indeed, I will make you a leader (imaman) for the people.' Ibrahim asked, 'And of my descendants?' Allah replied, 'My covenant does not include the wrongdoers.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hajj, which prophet is explicitly credited with naming the believers 'Muslims' (Al-Muslimin) previously, as reaffirmed in the Qur'an?
optionsEn: Ibrahim (AS)
Dawud (AS)
Musa (AS)
Nuh (AS)
explanationEn: Allah says in Surah Al-Hajj: '[It is] the religion of your father, Ibrahim. He named you "Muslims" before and in this [revelation]...'

questionEn: In Surah Hud, why was Prophet Lut (AS) deeply distressed and anguished when the angelic messengers arrived at his house in human form?
optionsEn: He thought they were spies sent by Pharaoh
He recognized them as angels of death coming for him
He feared the wicked men of his city would assault his guests and he felt powerless to defend them
He had no food to offer them
explanationEn: When Our messengers came to Lut, he was anguished for them and felt for them great discomfort, saying, 'This is a distressing day,' and wished he had strength against his people or could take refuge in a strong support.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-A'raf and Ash-Shu'ara, what was the unprecedented transgression for which Allah condemned the people of Lut (AS)?
optionsEn: Highway robbery only
Worshipping the sun during eclipses
Approaching men with desire instead of women, committing immorality no one in the worlds had preceded them in
Refusing to pay zakah on silver
explanationEn: Lut rebuked them: 'Do you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds? Indeed, you approach men with desire, instead of women. Rather, you are a transgressing people.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-A'raf, what was the sole excuse the people of Lut (AS) gave for demanding that Lut and his family be expelled from their town?
optionsEn: 'They refuse to pay taxes to the city'
'They are foreigners from Egypt'
'They destroyed our marketplaces'
'They are people who keep themselves pure!'
explanationEn: Their only answer was: 'Evict them from your city! Indeed, they are men who keep themselves pure (yatatahharun)!'

questionEn: In Surah Hud, when the angels revealed their true mission to Lut (AS), what instruction did they give him for escaping the city?
optionsEn: Hide inside a cave for seven days
Cross the sea before midday
Set out with your family during a portion of the night, and let none of you look back — except your wife
Climb to the rooftop of your house and wait for clouds
explanationEn: The angels said: 'O Lut, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; [therefore], they will never reach you. So set out with your family during a portion of the night and let not any among you look back — except your wife; indeed, she will be struck by that which strikes them.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hijr, what happened to the eyes of the men of Lut's city when they demanded his guests?
optionsEn: They were turned to stone
They fell asleep until noon
Allah obliterated/blinded their eyes (tamasna a'yunahum), as also mentioned in Surah Al-Qamar
They were struck by lightning
explanationEn: Surah Al-Qamar 54:37 explicitly records: 'And they had demanded from him his guests, but We obliterated their eyes, [saying], "Taste My punishment and warning."'

questionEn: How does Surah Hud describe the destruction of the cities of Lut's people?
optionsEn: Swallowed by a desert sinkhole without any stones
Flooded by a tidal wave
Turned upside down (ja'alna 'aliyaha safilaha) and rained upon with stones of baked clay (sijjil), marked by Allah
Burned by a solar eclipse
explanationEn: Surah Hud states: 'So when Our command came, We made the highest part [of the city] its lowest and rained upon them stones of layered hard clay, marked from your Lord.'

questionEn: According to Surah Adh-Dhariyat, how many believing households did the angels find in the town of Lut (AS) before its destruction?
optionsEn: Twelve households
Seven households
Forty believers
Only one household (that of Lut)
explanationEn: Allah states: 'So We brought out whoever was in the cities of the believers. And We found not within them other than a [single] house of Muslims.'

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shu'ara, why does Lut (AS) tell his people 'I am to you a trustworthy messenger' while asking for no reward?
optionsEn: Because he wanted to become their judge
To remind them that his reward is only from the Lord of the worlds
To collect charity for the travelers
Because he was appointed by the governor of Damascus
explanationEn: Like Nuh, Hud, and Salih, Lut declared: 'Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear Allah and obey me. And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.'

questionEn: In Surah Maryam, what two spiritual qualities are specifically highlighted about Prophet Isma'il (AS)?
optionsEn: He wrote the Zabur and commanded the winds
He spoke in the cradle and healed lepers
He interpreted dreams and controlled grain storehouses
He was true to his promise (sadiq al-wa'd) and used to enjoin prayer and zakah upon his family
explanationEn: Surah Maryam states: 'And mention in the Book, Isma'il. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet. And he used to enjoin on his people prayer and zakah and was to his Lord pleasing.'

questionEn: In Surah As-Saffat, what title does Allah give to the son promised to Ibrahim (AS) right before the narrative of the sacrifice?
optionsEn: A boy endowed with forbearance (ghulamin halim)
A boy of vast wealth
A boy of iron strength
A boy who would rule Egypt
explanationEn: After Ibrahim prayed for a righteous son, Allah gave him good tidings of 'a forbearing boy (bi-ghulamin halim),' and in the next verses Ibrahim's son showed remarkable forbearance in the sacrifice test.

questionEn: In Surah Sad, what honorific description is shared by Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Ya'qub (AS) together?
optionsEn: Men of strength/might and vision (ulil-aydi wal-absar)
Builders of the temple of Jerusalem
Keepers of the ark and tablets
Lords of the western seas
explanationEn: Surah Sad 38:45 says: 'And remember Our servants, Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Ya'qub — those of strength and [religious] vision.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah, when Prophet Ya'qub (AS) was on his deathbed, what question did he ask his sons to verify their faith?
optionsEn: 'Who will inherit my flocks after me?'
'What will you worship after me?'
'Where will you bury my remains?'
'Which of you will travel back to Egypt?'
explanationEn: Ya'qub asked his sons when death approached him: 'What will you worship after me?' They answered: 'We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim and Isma'il and Ishaq — one God. And we are Muslims [in submission] to Him.'

questionEn: According to Surah Yusuf, what precaution did Ya'qub (AS) advise his sons to take when entering Egypt together?
optionsEn: To travel only at night
To enter through one main gate with weapons drawn
Not to enter by a single gate, but to enter by different gates
To disguise themselves as Egyptian merchants
explanationEn: Ya'qub advised them: 'O my sons, do not enter from one gate but enter from different gates; and I cannot avail you against [the decree of] Allah at all. The decision is only for Allah.'

questionEn: In Surah Yusuf, what phrase did Ya'qub (AS) repeat both when his sons brought Yusuf's blood-stained shirt and when Binyamin was detained in Egypt?
optionsEn: 'Patience is most fitting (fa-sabrun jamil)'
'I will never eat until they return'
'Let us send a messenger to Pharaoh'
'Woe to me for what I lost'
explanationEn: On both occasions, Ya'qub responded with 'fa-sabrun jamil' — 'so patience is most fitting' — expressing complete trust in Allah.

questionEn: According to Surah Yusuf, what physical affliction befell Ya'qub (AS) from his prolonged grief over Yusuf (AS)?
optionsEn: His hair fell out completely
He lost his voice for seven years
He lost his ability to walk
His eyes turned white from grief, and he was suppressing sorrow
explanationEn: Surah Yusuf states: 'And he turned away from them and said, "Oh, my sorrow over Yusuf," and his eyes became white from grief, for he was [of that] a suppressor.'

questionEn: In Surah Yusuf, what did Ya'qub (AS) say when he sent his sons back to Egypt to search for Yusuf and his brother, encouraging hope in Allah?
optionsEn: 'Perhaps the king of Egypt will forgive your debt'
'And despair not of relief/mercy from Allah (la tay'asu min rawhillah). Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people'
'Do not return until the famine ends'
'Take double the silver this time'
explanationEn: Ya'qub instructed his sons: 'O my sons, go and find out about Yusuf and his brother and despair not of relief from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people.'

questionEn: How was Prophet Ya'qub's eyesight miraculously restored according to Surah Yusuf?
optionsEn: When Yusuf embraced him at the palace gate
By applying olive oil sent by Yusuf
By washing his face with water from Zamzam
When Yusuf's shirt was cast over his face, he became seeing again
explanationEn: Yusuf sent his shirt with his brothers, saying, 'Take this, my shirt, and cast it over the face of my father; he will become seeing.' When the bearer of good tidings cast it over his face, his sight returned.

questionEn: In Surah Yusuf, what did Ya'qub (AS) affirm to his family even before his sons returned with Yusuf's shirt?
optionsEn: 'Indeed, I perceive the scent of Yusuf [even] if you were not to think me weakened in mind'
'The stars have aligned in his favor'
'I saw Yusuf in a dream wearing a crown'
'A caravan from Gaza told me he is alive'
explanationEn: As the caravan departed Egypt, Ya'qub told those around him: 'Indeed, I find the smell of Yusuf [and would say that he was alive] if you did not think me weakened in mind.'

questionEn: In Surah Yusuf, what did Ya'qub (AS) say to his sons after they confessed their wrongdoing and asked him to pray for their forgiveness?
optionsEn: 'Your brother alone can forgive you'
'You must first fast for sixty days'
'I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful'
'Go back to the well and pray there'
explanationEn: Ya'qub replied gently: 'I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anbiya, how does Allah describe the gift of Ishaq (AS) and Ya'qub (AS) to Ibrahim (AS)?
optionsEn: Gifts granted after Ibrahim rebuilt Jerusalem
Ishaq as a son and Ya'qub as an added gift (nafilatan), and all of them He made righteous leaders guiding by His command
Only Ishaq as a prophet while Ya'qub remained a shepherd
Twins born on the same night in Makkah
explanationEn: Surah Al-Anbiya states: 'And We gave him Ishaq and Ya'qub in addition (nafilatan), and all [of them] We made righteous. And We made them leaders guiding by Our command.'

questionEn: In Surah Yusuf, what did young Yusuf (AS) see prostrating to him in his dream?
optionsEn: Twelve mountains and a river
Eleven stars, the sun, and the moon
Seven ears of wheat and seven doves
A crown of gold and two lions
explanationEn: Yusuf told his father: 'O my father, indeed I have seen [in a dream] eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me.'

questionEn: Why did Ya'qub (AS) warn young Yusuf (AS) not to relate his dream to his brothers?
optionsEn: Because dreams should never be spoken aloud before noon
Because the king of Egypt forbade dream interpretation
Because they might plot a scheme against him out of jealousy, as Shaytan is a clear enemy to man
Because his brothers would mock him for sleeping late
explanationEn: Ya'qub said: 'O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers or they will contrive against you a plan. Indeed Shaytan, to man, is a manifest enemy.'

questionEn: In Surah Yusuf, which suggestion prevented Yusuf's brothers from killing him outright?
optionsEn: One of them proposed casting him into the bottom of a deep well (ghayabat al-jubb) so a caravan might pick him up
They feared their mother's anger
They decided to sell him directly to their uncle
A wolf frightened them away before they could strike
explanationEn: One speaker among them said: 'Do not kill Yusuf but throw him into the bottom of the well; some travelers will pick him up — if you would do [something].'

questionEn: According to Surah Yusuf, for what price did the travelers sell Yusuf (AS) in Egypt?
optionsEn: Forty measures of wheat
A hundred gold dinars
Seven silver rings
A low price — a few counted dirhams (darahima ma'dudah)
explanationEn: Surah Yusuf states: 'And they sold him for a reduced price — a few dirhams — and they were, concerning him, of those content with little.'

questionEn: In Surah Yusuf, how did a witness from the household of the Aziz determine whether Yusuf (AS) or the Aziz's wife was telling the truth?
optionsEn: By checking whether Yusuf's shirt was torn from the front or from the back
By testing both with an oath before an idol
By examining footprints in the courtyard
By asking the palace guards what they heard
explanationEn: The witness reasoned: if his shirt is torn from the front, she told the truth; if torn from the back, she lied and he is truthful. When the Aziz saw it torn from the back, he knew it was her plot.

questionEn: When the Aziz's wife invited the women of the city to a banquet in Surah Yusuf, what happened when Yusuf (AS) walked out before them?
optionsEn: They immediately asked the Aziz to free him
They were so stunned by his beauty that they cut their own hands with their knives and exclaimed, 'This is not a man; this is none but a noble angel!'
They recognized him as a prophet from Canaan
They dropped their cups in silence
explanationEn: The women were astounded, cut their hands, and cried: 'Perfect is Allah! This is not a man; this is none but a noble angel!'

questionEn: In Surah Yusuf, what preference did Yusuf (AS) express in his supplication when pressured by the women's schemes?
optionsEn: 'My Lord, return me to my father's house tonight'
'My Lord, grant me wings to fly away'
'My Lord, strike them with blindness'
'My Lord, prison is more beloved to me than that to which they invite me'
explanationEn: Yusuf prayed: 'My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me. And if You do not avert from me their plan, I might incline toward them and [thus] be of the ignorant.'

questionEn: In Surah Yusuf, what were the dreams of the two young men imprisoned with Yusuf (AS)?
optionsEn: One saw himself pressing wine, and the other saw himself carrying bread on his head from which birds were eating
One saw a silver cup, and the other saw a golden key
One saw seven cows, and the other saw a broken ship
One saw himself climbing a palm tree, and the other saw a fountain of oil
