explanationEn: One prisoner dreamt he was pressing wine (interpreted as returning to serve his master wine), and the other dreamt he was carrying bread on his head with birds eating from it (interpreted as being crucified).

questionEn: Before interpreting his fellow prisoners' dreams in Surah Yusuf, what core message did Yusuf (AS) preach to them?
optionsEn: Tawhid — questioning whether separate lords are better or Allah, the One, the Prevailing
The agricultural cycles of the Nile
The history of the Egyptian pyramids
The laws of inheritance in Canaan
explanationEn: Yusuf taught them pure monotheism first, asking: 'Are separate lords better or Allah, the One, the Prevailing?' and affirming that legislation belongs only to Allah.

questionEn: According to Surah Yusuf, why did Yusuf (AS) remain in prison for 'several years' after interpreting the cupbearer's dream?
optionsEn: The king traveled away to war for ten years
Yusuf chose to stay until his brothers arrived
The prison warden refused to unlock the iron gate
Shaytan made the cupbearer forget to mention Yusuf to his master (the king)
explanationEn: Yusuf asked the one to be saved to mention him to his master, 'but Shaytan made him forget the mention [to] his master, and he remained in prison several years.'

questionEn: What dream of the King of Egypt finally prompted the cupbearer to remember Yusuf (AS) in Surah Yusuf?
optionsEn: A golden chariot sinking into the Nile
Seven rivers drying up beneath seven mountains
Seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of grain and seven dry ones
Eleven stars falling into a granary
explanationEn: The king dreamt: 'Indeed, I have seen [in a dream] seven fat cows being eaten by seven [that were] lean, and seven green spikes [of grain] and others [that were] dry.'

questionEn: In Surah Yusuf, why did Yusuf (AS) refuse to leave prison immediately when the king sent for him?
optionsEn: He demanded a golden robe first
He wanted to finish teaching the other prisoners
He was waiting for news of his mother
He wanted the king to investigate the case of the women who cut their hands so his innocence would be publicly vindicated
explanationEn: Yusuf told the messenger: 'Return to your master and ask him what is the case of the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plan.'

questionEn: When the King of Egypt offered Yusuf (AS) a high position of trust, which specific office did Yusuf request in Surah Yusuf?
optionsEn: Commander of the royal chariot army
Governor of Alexandria
Chief priest of the royal court
Keeper of the storehouses of the land (khaza'in al-ard)
explanationEn: Yusuf said: 'Appoint me over the storehouses of the land. Indeed, I will be a knowing guardian (hafizun 'alim).'

questionEn: In Surah Yusuf, what item did Yusuf (AS) secretly have placed into his younger brother Binyamin's saddlebag to lawfully detain him?
optionsEn: The king's drinking cup (siqayah / suwa' al-malik)
A scroll of grain accounts
A royal signet ring
A bundle of silver coins
explanationEn: Surah Yusuf states: 'He placed the [king's] drinking cup (as-siqayah) into the bag of his brother,' and the crier later called it 'the king's measuring goblet (suwa' al-malik)' so the penalty under the brothers' own judgment could detain him.

questionEn: When Yusuf (AS) finally revealed his identity to his stunned brothers in Surah Yusuf, what words of pardon did he speak to them?
optionsEn: 'No blame will there be upon you today (la tathriba 'alaykumul-yawm). May Allah forgive you; and He is the most merciful of the merciful'
'Repay me twice the silver you received for me'
'Leave Egypt and never return'
'I forgive only Binyamin among you'
explanationEn: Yusuf comforted them: 'No blame will there be upon you today. May Allah forgive you; and He is the most merciful of the merciful.'

questionEn: In Surah Yusuf, after raising his parents to the throne and seeing his family prostrate before him in respect, what did Yusuf (AS) declare?
optionsEn: 'O my father, this is the explanation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it reality'
'Now all of Egypt shall bow to our clan'
'Never again will anyone enter a well'
'Let us build a monument to the seven lean years'
explanationEn: Yusuf said: 'O my father, this is the explanation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it reality. And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you [here] from Bedouin life...'

questionEn: What moving final supplication of Prophet Yusuf (AS) is recorded at the conclusion of his story in Surah Yusuf?
optionsEn: 'Protect my storehouses from drought forever'
'Creator of the heavens and earth, You are my protector in this world and in the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous'
'Make my brothers prophets after me'
'Grant me eternal kingship over Egypt and Syria'
explanationEn: Yusuf prayed: 'Fatir as-samawati wal-ard, Anta waliyyi fid-dunya wal-akhirah, tawaffani musliman wa alhiqni bis-salihin.'

questionEn: In Surah Ghafir, which Egyptian believer from Pharaoh's family reminded his people of Prophet Yusuf's earlier message to Egypt?
optionsEn: Haman, the chief builder
Qarun, the wealthy kinsman
The magician who cast the first rope
The believing man from the family of Pharaoh (Mu'min Al Fir'awn)
explanationEn: In Surah Ghafir 40:34, the believing man from Pharaoh's family reminded them: 'And Yusuf had already come to you before with clear proofs, but you remained in doubt concerning that which he brought to you...'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anbiya, what humble supplication did Prophet Ayyub (AS) make to Allah during his severe trial?
optionsEn: 'Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful'
'My Lord, remove this illness before sunset'
'Why have my wealth and children been taken?'
'Grant me patience for seven more years'
explanationEn: Ayyub called to his Lord: 'Anni massaniyad-durru wa Anta Arhamur-rahimin' ('Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful').

questionEn: According to Surah Sad, what physical action did Allah instruct Ayyub (AS) to perform to bring forth a miraculous healing spring?
optionsEn: Strike the ground with his foot ('Urkud bi-rijlika')
Tap a mountain rock with a wooden staff
Dig beneath an olive tree with his hands
Pour water from a well over three stones
explanationEn: Allah commanded Ayyub: 'Strike [the ground] with your foot; this is a [spring for] a cool bath and drink.'

questionEn: For what two purposes does Surah Sad state Ayyub (AS) used the spring that gushed forth when he struck the ground?
optionsEn: As a cool bath and a drink (mughtasalun baridun wa sharab)
To irrigate crops and water camels
To wash silver vessels and make bricks
To cleanse a mosque and fill a cistern
explanationEn: Surah Sad 38:42 explicitly specifies: 'This is a cool [spring for] bathing and a drink.'

questionEn: In Surah Sad, how did Allah enable Ayyub (AS) to fulfill an earlier oath without breaking it or causing undue harm?
optionsEn: He absolved him from all oaths by feeding ten needy people
He told him to take a bundle of thin grass/twigs (dighthan) and strike with it once, so he would not break his oath
He commanded him to fast for three days instead
He instructed him to donate his finest camel
explanationEn: Allah told Ayyub: 'And take in your hand a bunch [of grass] and strike with it and do not break your oath.' Allah then praised him: 'Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant!'

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Anbiya and Surah Sad, how did Allah restore Ayyub's family after answering his prayer?
optionsEn: He moved his surviving relatives to Egypt
He granted him seventy palaces in Damascus
He gave him one son who became a king
He returned his family to him and the like thereof along with them (doubled them) as a mercy and a reminder
explanationEn: Surah Al-Anbiya 21:84 and Surah Sad 38:43 both affirm: 'We granted him his family and a like [number] with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers / those of understanding.'

questionEn: What specific praise does Allah bestow upon Prophet Ayyub (AS) in Surah Sad right after describing the resolution of his oath?
optionsEn: 'Indeed, he spoke to the birds and winds'
'Indeed, he was the wisest judge of his era'
'Indeed, he was the first to write with ink'
'Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one repeatedly turning [to Allah] (awwab)'
explanationEn: Surah Sad 38:44 concludes Ayyub's story with: 'Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one repeatedly turning [to Allah].'

questionEn: To which community was Prophet Shu'ayb (AS) sent, as named in Surah Hud and Surah Al-A'raf?
optionsEn: The people of Madyan
The people of Al-Hijr
The people of Ninawa
The people of Saba'
explanationEn: The Qur'an repeatedly states: 'And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb.'

questionEn: Besides idol worship, what major economic corruption did Shu'ayb (AS) repeatedly forbid the people of Madyan from committing?
optionsEn: Cheating in measure and weight and depriving people of their due goods
Charging interest on gold loans
Hoarding grain during winter
Refusing to mint silver coins
explanationEn: Shu'ayb admonished them: 'Give full measure and do not be of those who cause loss. And weigh with an even balance. And do not deprive people of their due and do not commit abuse on earth, spreading corruption.'

questionEn: In Surah Hud, how did the people of Madyan sarcastically connect Shu'ayb's worship to his demand for honest trade?
optionsEn: 'Only merchants may lead prayers in Madyan'
'O Shu'ayb, does your prayer (salatuk) command you that we should leave what our fathers worshipped or not do with our wealth what we will?'
'Why do you pray facing the desert instead of our market?'
'Pray for rain first, then we will balance our scales'
explanationEn: They mocked him saying: 'O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we should leave what our fathers worship or not do with our wealth what we please? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the discerning!'

questionEn: What noble statement of sincerity and reliance on Allah did Shu'ayb (AS) make in Surah Hud when declaring his goal to his people?
optionsEn: 'I have come to overturn your markets by force'
'I only intend reform as much as I am able. And my success is not but through Allah. Upon Him I have relied, and to Him I return'
'I will remain silent if you pay me a tenth of your profits'
'My brothers will defend me with swords if you reject me'
explanationEn: Shu'ayb replied: 'I only intend reform as much as I am able. And my success is not but through Allah (wa ma tawfiqi illa billah). Upon Him I have relied, and to Him I return.'

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shu'ara, by what additional title are the people to whom Shu'ayb (AS) was sent also identified?
optionsEn: Companions of the Wood / Thicket (Ashab al-Aykah)
Companions of the Cave (Ashab al-Kahf)
Companions of the Elephant (Ashab al-Fil)
Companions of the Trench (Ashab al-Ukhdud)
explanationEn: Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:176-177 reads: 'The Companions of the Wood (Ashab al-Aykah) denied the messengers, when Shu'ayb said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"'

questionEn: What specific form of punishment destroyed the Companions of the Wood who rejected Shu'ayb (AS) according to Surah Ash-Shu'ara?
optionsEn: The punishment of the Day of the Canopy/Shadow ('adhab yawm az-zullah)
A pillar of salt falling from the sky
A flood of boiling mud
Swarms of locusts for forty nights
explanationEn: They challenged him to drop a fragment of the sky upon them, and Allah states: 'So they denied him, and the punishment of the Day of the Canopy (yawm az-zullah) seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a terrible day.'

questionEn: In Surah Hud, why did the leaders of Madyan tell Shu'ayb (AS) they refrained from stoning him?
optionsEn: Because they feared the king of Egypt
Because he promised to leave at dawn
Out of regard for his family/tribe (rahtuka), though they held him in low esteem
Because he was weak and had no clan
explanationEn: They told him: 'O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say, and indeed, we consider you among us as weak. And if not for your family/clan, we would have stoned you.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-A'raf, what threat did the arrogant elites of Madyan issue against Shu'ayb (AS) and those who believed with him?
optionsEn: To seal all the wells in the valley
To drive them out of the town unless they returned to their religion
To double the taxes on their sheep
To confiscate their houses for seven years
explanationEn: The arrogant leaders said: 'We will surely evict you, O Shu'ayb, and those who have believed with you from our city, or you must return to our religion.'

questionEn: According to Surah Taha and Surah Al-Qasas, what did Allah inspire the mother of Musa (AS) to do when she feared Pharaoh's slaughter of infant boys?
optionsEn: Hide him in a mountain cave for a year
Nurse him, and when she feared for him, put him into a chest/basket (tabut) and cast it into the river (yamm)
Give him to the elders of Banu Isra'il
Send him with a merchant caravan to Madyan
explanationEn: Allah inspired Musa's mother: 'Suckle him; but when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and will make him [one] of the messengers.'

questionEn: How was infant Musa (AS) miraculously reunited with his own mother inside Pharaoh's household according to Surah Al-Qasas?
optionsEn: Pharaoh's soldiers recognized his mother at the palace gate
Asiyah sent word to all Israelite women to visit the palace
Allah forbade/prevented Musa from accepting the milk of any wet nurse beforehand, until his sister suggested his mother's household
Musa spoke in the cradle and named his mother
explanationEn: Allah had prevented all wet nurses from him beforehand, so his sister suggested a household that would rear him for them sincerely; thus Allah restored him to his mother so her eye might be comforted.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Qasas, how did Musa (AS) accidentally kill an Egyptian man before fleeing to Madyan?
optionsEn: He struck him with a wooden staff in self-defense
He threw a spear during a chariot race
He pushed him into a canal during a flood
He struck him with his fist (wakazahu) while defending an Israelite who called him for help
explanationEn: An Israelite sought Musa's help against an Egyptian enemy, so Musa struck the Egyptian with his fist (fa-wakazahu Musa), unintentionally killing him, and immediately sought Allah's forgiveness.

questionEn: When Musa (AS) arrived in Madyan in Surah Al-Qasas, why were two women holding back their flocks near the water?
optionsEn: They waited until the shepherds finished because their father was a very old man
The water was reserved for royal horses
They had no buckets to draw water
They were forbidden from approaching the well at noon
explanationEn: Musa saw two women holding back their flocks and asked what the matter was. They explained: 'We do not water until the shepherds dispatch [their flocks]; and our father is an old man.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Qasas, what two qualities did one of the two women of Madyan cite to her father when recommending that he hire Musa (AS)?
optionsEn: 'He is the wealthiest and most eloquent'
'He is a prince from Egypt who knows the Nile'
'He is skilled in carpentry and masonry'
'Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy (al-qawiyy al-amin)'
explanationEn: One of the women said: 'O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy.'

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Qasas, how many years of service did the righteous elder of Madyan ask Musa (AS) to complete as a marriage dowry for one of his daughters?
optionsEn: Forty months of tending olive groves
Three years, or five if Musa wished
Twelve years, with seven years of herding
Eight years, and if Musa completed ten, it would be from him
explanationEn: The elder proposed: 'Indeed, I wish to wed you one of these, my two daughters, on [the condition] that you serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it will be [as a favor] from you.'

questionEn: In Surah Taha, what drew Musa (AS) toward Mount Tur when he was traveling with his family at night?
optionsEn: A distant horn sounding
A fire he perceived on the side of the mount, hoping to bring back a burning brand or find guidance
An angel calling his name from the valley
A beam of moonlight shining on a well
explanationEn: Musa saw a fire and told his family: 'Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire; perhaps I can bring you a torch or find at the fire some guidance.'

questionEn: Which two physical miracles were immediately demonstrated to Musa (AS) at the sacred valley in Surah Taha?
optionsEn: His staff becoming a fast-moving serpent, and his hand emerging white without harm when placed under his arm/side
Commanding the wind and understanding bird speech
Walking on water and summoning hail
Splitting a rock into twelve springs and turning river water to red
explanationEn: Allah turned Musa's staff into a moving serpent when he threw it, and when he drew his hand from his side/pocket it came out white without disease as a second sign.

questionEn: In Surah Taha and Surah Al-Qasas, why did Musa (AS) specifically ask Allah to appoint his brother Harun (AS) as his helper (wazir)?
optionsEn: Because Harun knew how to read Egyptian hieroglyphs
Because Musa feared traveling alone across the desert
Because Harun was older and owned land in Egypt
Because Harun was more eloquent in speech (afsahu minni lisanan), to share his task and strengthen his back
explanationEn: Musa prayed in 20:29-32: 'And appoint for me a minister from my family — Harun, my brother. Increase through him my strength and let him share my task'; and in 28:34: 'My brother Harun is more fluent than me in tongue, so send him with me as support.'

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shu'ara, how did Pharaoh try to shame Musa (AS) when Musa first delivered Allah's message at the court?
optionsEn: He challenged Musa to race his royal chariots
He mocked Musa's shepherd garments from Madyan
He accused Musa of stealing from the treasury
He reminded Musa of raising him as a child in his palace and of the Egyptian whom Musa had killed
explanationEn: Pharaoh said: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you remained among us for years of your life? And you did your deed which you did, and you were of the ungrateful.'

questionEn: When Pharaoh asked 'And what is the Lord of the worlds?' in Surah Ash-Shu'ara, how did Musa (AS) respond?
optionsEn: 'The Creator of the Nile alone'
'Ask the magicians of Memphis'
'The Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you should be convinced'
'He who sits upon a throne in Jerusalem'
explanationEn: Musa answered: 'The Lord of the heavens and the earth and that between them, if you would be convinced,' and further identified Him as the Lord of Pharaoh and his forefathers, and Lord of the east and the west.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Isra, how many clear signs (ayat bayyinat) did Allah grant Musa (AS) for Pharaoh and his people?
optionsEn: Twelve signs
Five signs
Nine clear signs
Seven signs
explanationEn: Surah Al-Isra 17:101 states: 'And We had certainly given Musa nine clear signs, so ask the Children of Israel [about] when he came to them...'

questionEn: Which five plagues are listed together in a single verse of Surah Al-A'raf as signs sent upon Pharaoh's people?
optionsEn: Locusts, hornets, frost, blindness, and fever
Earthquakes, fire, thunder, drought, and wind
Darkness, hail, snakes, boils, and dust
The flood, locusts, lice, frogs, and blood (at-tufan, al-jarad, al-qummal, ad-dafadi', ad-dam)
explanationEn: Surah Al-A'raf 7:133 records: 'So We sent upon them the flood and locusts and lice and frogs and blood as distinct signs, but they were arrogant and were a criminal people.'

questionEn: In Surah Taha, what happened immediately after Musa's staff swallowed the ropes and staffs of Pharaoh's magicians?
optionsEn: The magicians fled the city in terror
The magicians fell down in prostration declaring faith in the Lord of Harun and Musa
Pharaoh immediately freed the Children of Israel
The palace courtyard collapsed
explanationEn: Witnessing truth overcome sorcery, the magicians fell in prostration and said: 'We have believed in the Lord of Harun and Musa.'

questionEn: How did Pharaoh's magicians bravely answer Pharaoh's threat to cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides and crucify them on palm trunks?
optionsEn: 'We will never prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and He who created us. So decree whatever you are to decree; you can only decree for this worldly life'
'Spare us and we will return to our sorcery'
'Ask Musa to release us from his spell'
'Give us until tomorrow morning to reconsider'
explanationEn: With unwavering faith, the magicians replied: 'Decree whatever you are to decree. You can only decree for this worldly life. Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins.'

questionEn: In Surah Ash-Shu'ara, when Musa's people panicked at the sea with Pharaoh's army behind them and cried 'We are overtaken!', what did Musa (AS) reply?
optionsEn: 'No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me (kalla inna ma'iya Rabbi sayahdin)'
'Turn back and surrender to Pharaoh'
'Prepare to fight on the shoreline'
'Swim across before the tide rises'
explanationEn: Musa declared with absolute certainty: 'No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.' Then Allah revealed to him to strike the sea with his staff, and it parted like towering mountains.

questionEn: According to Surah Yunus, what did Allah say when Pharaoh cried out in belief at the moment of drowning?
optionsEn: 'Your repentance is accepted because you spoke before sinking'
'Now? When you had disobeyed before and were of the corrupters? So today We will save you in body that you may be to those who succeed you a sign'
'Your army shall be spared along with you'
'Harun will pray for your soul'
explanationEn: Allah rejected his deathbed confession at the sight of punishment, declaring He would preserve Pharaoh's body (bi-badanika) as a sign for future generations.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah, how many springs gushed forth when Musa (AS) struck the stone with his staff for his thirsty people?
optionsEn: Seven springs
Twelve springs — one for every tribe
Forty springs
Three rivers
explanationEn: Allah instructed Musa: 'Strike with your staff the stone.' And there gushed forth from it twelve springs, and every people knew its watering place.

questionEn: In Surah Al-A'raf, what happened when Musa (AS) asked Allah: 'My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look at You'?
optionsEn: A mirror of water reflected light from heaven
Allah manifested His glory to the mountain, crushing it to dust, and Musa fell down unconscious
A blinding cloud covered Mount Sinai for seven days
Jibril appeared in his true angelic form
explanationEn: Allah told Musa he could not see Him, and when His Lord appeared to the mountain, He rendered it level/crumbled, and Musa fell unconscious; upon awakening he glorified Allah and repented.

questionEn: In Surah Taha, what excuse did Harun (AS) give Musa (AS) when Musa seized him by the beard and head over the golden calf incident?
optionsEn: 'I was asleep on the mountain when Samiri forged the calf'
'O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, "You caused division among the Children of Israel and did not observe my word"'
'Pharaoh's soldiers forced the people to worship it'
'I tried to melt the gold in a furnace but could not'
explanationEn: Harun explained gently that he feared causing division among the Children of Israel before Musa's return, and in Surah Al-A'raf 7:150 he added that the people oppressed him and were about to kill him.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah, why did Allah rebuke the Children of Israel after they demanded lentils, onions, cucumbers, garlic, and herbs instead of Manna and Salwa?
optionsEn: Because no farmland existed near Sinai
Because they refused to share them with Harun
Because those foods were forbidden in the Torah
Because they asked to exchange what is better for what is inferior
explanationEn: Musa asked them: 'Would you exchange what is better for what is less?' and told them to go down to any city where they would find what they asked for.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Baqarah, what did Allah grant Dawud (AS) after he killed Jalut (Goliath)?
optionsEn: Kingship and wisdom (al-mulk wal-hikmah), and taught him of that which He willed
The ability to heal the blind
Twelve springs in Jerusalem
Dominion over the jinn and winds
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah states: 'And Dawud killed Jalut, and Allah gave him the kingship and prophethood/wisdom and taught him from that which He willed.'

questionEn: Which two parts of creation does Surah Al-Anbiya and Surah Sad state Allah subjected to glorify Him alongside Prophet Dawud (AS)?
optionsEn: The sun and the stars
The desert winds and palm trees
The mountains and the birds (al-jibal wat-tayr)
The clouds and the oceans
explanationEn: Surah Al-Anbiya 21:79 states: 'And We subjected the mountains to exalt [Us], along with Dawud, and [also] the birds.' Surah Sad 38:18-19 echoes this in the evening and morning.

questionEn: What material did Allah make pliable for Dawud (AS) so he could craft protective coats of mail (armor) according to Surah Saba' and Surah Al-Anbiya?
optionsEn: Molten copper
Iron (al-hadid)
Hardened cedar wood
Mountain granite
explanationEn: Allah says in Surah Saba' 34:10-11: 'And We made pliable for him iron, [commanding], "Make full coats of mail and calculate [precisely] the links."'

questionEn: Which revealed scripture does the Qur'an explicitly state was given to Prophet Dawud (AS)?
optionsEn: The Injil
The Tawrah
The Zabur (Psalms)
The Suhuf (Scrolls)
explanationEn: Surah An-Nisa 4:163 and Surah Al-Isra 17:55 affirm: 'And to Dawud We gave the Zabur.'

questionEn: In Surah Sad, what dispute did two men who climbed over the wall into Dawud's prayer chamber bring before him?
optionsEn: A broken treaty between two tribes
A dispute over an inherited vineyard
One brother had ninety-nine ewes and the other had one ewe, yet the first demanded his single ewe too
A stolen camel from a caravan
explanationEn: One disputant said: 'Indeed this, my brother, has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe; so he said, "Entrust her to me," and he overpowered me in speech.' Dawud judged that he had wronged him, then realized Allah was testing him and fell in prostration seeking forgiveness.

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Anbiya, over what legal case did young Sulayman (AS) receive deeper understanding from Allah than his father Dawud (AS)?
optionsEn: A dispute over weights in the marketplace
A case involving sunken ships
An argument over water rights from a well
A case concerning people's sheep that had strayed at night and grazed in another's field/crops
explanationEn: Dawud and Sulayman both judged concerning a cultivated field in which people's sheep had pastured at night, and Allah gave Sulayman special understanding of the judgment while granting both judgment and knowledge.

questionEn: In Surah An-Naml, what did Sulayman (AS) declare he had been taught, describing it as a clear favor from Allah?
optionsEn: The language of the birds (mantiq at-tayr) and something of all things
The chemistry of molten silver
The hidden names of all stars
The art of building iron ships
explanationEn: Sulayman inherited Dawud and said: 'O people, we have been taught the language of birds, and we have been given from all things. Indeed, this is evident bounty.'

questionEn: When Sulayman's army of jinn, men, and birds marched through the Valley of the Ants in Surah An-Naml, how did Sulayman (AS) react upon hearing an ant warn its colony?
optionsEn: He smiled amused at her speech and prayed to Allah to inspire him to be grateful for His favors upon him and his parents
He spoke back to the ant in its own tongue
He ordered his army to change roads immediately
He stopped the march for three days
explanationEn: Hearing the ant warn her fellow ants to enter their dwellings lest Sulayman and his soldiers crush them unknowingly, Sulayman smiled, amused at her speech, and recited his famous dua of gratitude.

questionEn: According to Surah Saba', what was the remarkable travel capacity of the wind subjected to Prophet Sulayman (AS)?
optionsEn: It cooled his palaces during summer nights
Its morning course was a month's journey, and its afternoon course was a month's journey
It carried him across seven oceans in one hour
It blew only from the north toward Yemen
explanationEn: Surah Saba' 34:12 states: 'And to Sulayman [We subjected] the wind — its morning [journey was that of] a month and its afternoon [journey was that of] a month, and We made flow for him a spring of [liquid] copper.'

questionEn: What specific items does Surah Saba' mention the jinn crafted for Prophet Sulayman (AS) by Allah's permission?
optionsEn: Flying carpets and crystal domes
Swords, shields, and iron chariots
Elevated chambers/sanctuaries (maharib), statues/figures (tamathil), bowls as large as reservoirs, and stationary cooking pots
Pyramids, obelisks, and silver bridges
explanationEn: The jinn made for him whatever he willed of elevated chambers (maharib), figures/sculptures (tamathil), bowls like reservoirs, and heavy stationary kettles, while Allah reminded the family of Dawud: 'Work in gratitude!'

questionEn: In Surah An-Naml, which bird was absent when Sulayman (AS) inspected his avian ranks, only to return with certain news from the kingdom of Saba' (Sheba)?
optionsEn: The falcon
The hoopoe (al-hudhud)
The raven
The dove
explanationEn: Sulayman noticed the hoopoe (hudhud) was missing; it soon returned saying it had encompassed what Sulayman had not and brought sure news from Saba' of a woman ruling them who worshipped the sun.

questionEn: In Surah An-Naml, how did Sulayman (AS) begin the letter carried by the hoopoe to the Queen of Sheba?
optionsEn: 'I am the son of Dawud, king of the jinn'
'In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Be not haughty with me, but come to me in submission [as Muslims]'
'Prepare your armies or surrender your gold'
'Send me thirty camels of frankincense'
explanationEn: The Queen read the noble letter aloud: 'Indeed, it is from Sulayman, and indeed, it reads: "In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful, Be not haughty with me but come to me in submission."'

questionEn: In Surah Sad, why did Sulayman (AS) feel remorse when fine, swift horses (as-safinat al-jiyad) were paraded before him in the afternoon?
optionsEn: Because the jinn frightened the horses away
Because he had not paid the stables on time
Because they had distracted him from the remembrance of his Lord until the sun disappeared behind the veil
Because the horses had been injured in training
explanationEn: When the fine steeds were displayed before him in the evening, he realized: 'Indeed, I gave preference to the love of good [things] over the remembrance of my Lord until the sun disappeared into the curtain [of night].'

questionEn: What remarkable supplication of Sulayman (AS) in Surah Sad asks Allah for a kingdom unique to him?
optionsEn: 'My Lord, double the gold of Dawud'
'My Lord, give me eternal life upon my throne'
'My Lord, turn every mountain into copper'
'My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower'
explanationEn: After turning back to Allah in repentance, Sulayman prayed: 'My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower.'

questionEn: In Surah As-Saffat, which false deity did Prophet Ilyas (AS) rebuke his people for calling upon instead of the Best of Creators?
optionsEn: Wadd
Hubal
Al-Lat
Ba'l
explanationEn: Ilyas asked his people: 'Will you not fear Allah? Do you call upon Ba'l and leave the best of creators — Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers?'

questionEn: What honorific greeting does Allah record in Surah As-Saffat for Prophet Ilyas (AS) (also referred to there as Ilyasin)?
optionsEn: 'Peace be upon Ilyasin! Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good'
'He built the gates of Damascus'
'He ruled Syria for forty years'
'He was the keeper of the mountain fire'
explanationEn: Surah As-Saffat 37:130-131 proclaims: 'Peace be upon Ilyasin! Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good. Indeed, he was of Our believing servants.'

questionEn: By what descriptive title does the Qur'an refer to Prophet Yunus (AS) in Surah Al-Anbiya and Surah Al-Qalam?
optionsEn: Dhul-Qarnayn (The Two-Horned)
Khalilullah (Friend of Allah)
Dhun-Nun / Sahib al-Hut (Companion of the Fish)
Dhul-Kifl (Possessor of the Portion)
explanationEn: Yunus (AS) is referred to as Dhun-Nun in Surah Al-Anbiya 21:87 and Sahib al-Hut in Surah Al-Qalam 68:48, both referring to his trial inside the whale/great fish.

questionEn: In Surah As-Saffat, why did the sailors aboard the overloaded ship cast lots, resulting in Yunus (AS) being thrown into the sea?
optionsEn: Because Yunus asked to swim to shore
Because they suspected a fugitive/passenger had brought danger upon the heavily laden ship, and the lot fell on Yunus
Because a pirate ship approached them
Because they ran out of drinking water
explanationEn: Yunus fled to the laden ship; when they drew lots (fasahama), he was among the losers (al-mudhadin), and the great fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy.

questionEn: What exact supplication did Yunus (AS) cry out from within the darknesses of the fish's belly in Surah Al-Anbiya?
optionsEn: 'Our Lord, forgive me and my people who rejected me'
'There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers (La ilaha illa Anta Subhanaka inni kuntu minaz-zalimin)'
'O Allah, turn the night into morning'
'My Lord, command the sea to spit me onto dry land'
explanationEn: Inside the layers of darkness, Yunus cried out: 'La ilaha illa Anta, Subhanaka, inni kuntu minaz-zalimin.' Allah responded to him and saved him from distress, promising the same deliverance for believers.

questionEn: According to Surah As-Saffat, what would have happened to Yunus (AS) if he had NOT been among those who glorify Allah (al-musabbihin)?
optionsEn: He would have been cast onto a distant desert island
He would have remained inside the belly of the fish until the Day of Resurrection
He would have lost his prophethood permanently
He would have drowned immediately
explanationEn: Surah As-Saffat 37:143-144 states: 'And had he not been of those who exalt Allah, he would have remained inside its belly until the Day they are resurrected.'

questionEn: Approximately how many people does Surah As-Saffat state Yunus (AS) was sent to, who all believed when he returned?
optionsEn: Ten thousand
Twelve thousand
Fifty thousand
A hundred thousand or more (mi'ati alfin aw yazidun)
explanationEn: Surah As-Saffat 37:147-148 says: 'And We sent him to [his people of] a hundred thousand or more. And they believed, so We gave them enjoyment [of life] for a time.'

questionEn: What unique distinction does Surah Yunus give to the town/people of Yunus (AS) compared to every other warned city before destruction?
optionsEn: It was the only town whose belief when seeing the signs profited them, so Allah removed from them the punishment of disgrace
Its people built a golden mosque in one night
It was the largest city built of white marble
Its people fasted for a hundred days
explanationEn: Allah asks: 'Then has there not been a [single] city that believed so its faith benefited it except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in worldly life and gave them enjoyment for a time.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Qalam, why does Allah advise Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: 'Do not be like the Companion of the Fish'?
optionsEn: As an order never to leave Makkah
As a warning never to travel by ship
As a reminder to eat fish only on land
As an admonition to be patient for the judgment of his Lord and not act out of frustration before permission is given
explanationEn: Allah commands: 'Then be patient for the decision of your Lord, [O Muhammad], and be not like the companion of the fish when he called out while he was distressed.'

questionEn: In Surah Ali 'Imran, what miraculous sight in Maryam's sanctuary inspired Prophet Zakariyya (AS) to pray for a pure offspring despite his old age?
optionsEn: A dove bringing written scrolls to her
Whenever he entered her prayer chamber (mihrab), he found fresh provision (rizq) with her out of season
Angels visibly conversing with her at dawn
A spring of milk flowing inside the temple
explanationEn: Every time Zakariyya entered upon Maryam in the sanctuary, he found provision with her; when she told him 'It is from Allah,' Zakariyya right then prayed to his Lord for pure offspring.

questionEn: According to Surah Maryam, what two physical obstacles did Zakariyya (AS) mention in his quiet prayer when asking Allah for an heir?
optionsEn: His bones had weakened and his head shone with gray hair, and his wife was barren
His wealth was lost and his brothers opposed him
He was blind and lived in exile
He was mute and had no home
explanationEn: Zakariyya called upon his Lord privately: 'My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened, and my head has filled with white, and never have I been in my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy... and my wife has been barren.'

questionEn: What miraculous sign did Allah give Zakariyya (AS) in Surah Maryam and Surah Ali 'Imran to confirm the promise of Yahya's birth?
optionsEn: His staff blossomed with almonds overnight
His hair turned black again
He would not speak to people for three nights (or three days) except by gesture, though being completely sound/healthy
A star stood still above the sanctuary for three nights
explanationEn: Allah said his sign was that he would not speak to the people for three nights/days except by signals/gestures, while remembering his Lord abundantly and glorifying Him evening and morning.

questionEn: In Surah Maryam, what command was given to Prophet Yahya (AS) and at what stage of life was he granted wisdom/judgment (hukm)?
optionsEn: 'O Yahya, take the Scripture with determination!' And We gave him wisdom/judgment while yet a boy (sabiyya)
He was told to lead armies at age eighteen
He was commanded to build a new temple in Jericho
He received wisdom at age forty after fleeing to Sinai
explanationEn: Allah commanded: 'O Yahya, take the Scripture with determination.' And We gave him judgment [while yet] a boy, and affection/compassion from Us and purity, and he was fearing of Allah and dutiful to his parents.

questionEn: In Surah Ali 'Imran, how did Allah respond when Maryam (AS) asked how she could have a son when no man had touched her?
optionsEn: 'Wait until you travel to Egypt'
'An angel will adopt the child'
'Ask Zakariyya to explain the Torah'
'Even so; Allah creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is'
explanationEn: She was answered: 'Such is Allah; He creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.'

questionEn: According to Surah Ali 'Imran and Surah Maryam, what was the very first miracle performed by Isa (AS) while still an infant?
optionsEn: Speaking to people from the cradle (fil-mahd), declaring himself a servant and prophet of Allah
Turning water into milk
Healing a blind shepherd
Splitting a date-palm tree
explanationEn: When Maryam pointed to the baby in the cradle, infant Isa spoke clearly: 'Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.'

questionEn: Which miracles performed by Prophet Isa (AS) 'by Allah's permission (bi-idhnillah)' are listed together in Surah Ali 'Imran 3:49?
optionsEn: Causing mountains to walk and speaking to ants
Summoning rain from clear skies and multiplying silver coins
Parting the sea, softening iron, and calming storms
Shaping a bird from clay and breathing into it so it becomes a bird, healing the born-blind and the leper, raising the dead, and telling people what they eat and store in their homes
explanationEn: Surah Ali 'Imran 3:49 details all these signs performed strictly 'bi-idhnillah' (by Allah's permission), proving his prophethood to the Children of Israel.

questionEn: In Surah Ali 'Imran, what does Allah compare the miraculous fatherless creation of Isa (AS) to?
optionsEn: The creation of Adam (AS), whom Allah created from dust and then said 'Be' and he was
The creation of the moon from light
The birth of Yahya to elderly parents
The sprouting of rain-soaked grain
explanationEn: Surah Ali 'Imran states: 'Indeed, the example of Isa to Allah is like that of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him, "Be," and he was.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah, why did the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) ask Isa (AS) to pray for a Table Spread (ma'idah) to be sent down from heaven?
optionsEn: So they could eat from it, have their hearts reassured, know he had told them the truth, and be witnesses to it
Because they wanted golden plates for a royal banquet
To sell the heavenly bread in Jerusalem
Because they refused to fast during Ramadan
explanationEn: The disciples replied: 'We wish to eat from it and let our hearts be reassured and know that you have been truthful to us and be among its witnesses.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah, what severe warning did Allah attach when granting Isa's prayer to send down the Table Spread?
optionsEn: No woman or child could approach it
They could only eat from it once a year
The table would vanish if anyone touched it with iron
Whoever disbelieves among them afterward would receive a punishment unlike any He had ever inflicted upon anyone in the worlds
explanationEn: Allah said: 'Indeed, I will send it down to you, whoever disbelieves afterwards from among you — then indeed will I punish him with a punishment by which I have not punished anyone among the worlds.'

questionEn: What does Surah An-Nisa explicitly state regarding the claim that Isa (AS) was killed and crucified?
optionsEn: He died on the cross and was resurrected after two nights
They did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; rather, it was made to appear so to them (shubbiha lahum), and Allah raised him to Himself
His disciples hid him in a cave in Sinai
He was rescued by the Roman governor after three days
explanationEn: Surah An-Nisa 4:157-158 clearly states: 'And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but [another] was made to resemble him to them... Rather, Allah raised him to Himself.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah, how will Isa (AS) answer on the Day of Judgment when Allah asks him: 'Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah?"'
optionsEn: 'Yes, my followers misunderstood my parables'
'Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right... I said not to them except what You commanded me — to worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord'
'I only taught that to the priests of Rome'
'Ask the disciples who wrote after me'
explanationEn: Isa will completely disavow any claim to divinity, testifying that he only commanded them to worship Allah alone and was a witness over them only while among them.

questionEn: In Surah Maryam, what blessings did infant Isa (AS) declare Allah placed upon him wherever he might be?
optionsEn: He made him king of Judea and Syria
He promised him immunity from all hunger
He made him blessed wherever he is, enjoined upon him prayer (salah) and zakah as long as he lives, and made him dutiful to his mother
He exempted him from prayer and fasting
explanationEn: Infant Isa declared: 'And He has made me blessed wherever I am and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive, and [made me] dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a wretched tyrant.'

questionEn: In Surah Az-Zukhruf, how does the Qur'an describe Isa (AS) in relation to the Hour (Day of Judgment)?
optionsEn: 'He will write the final book before the Hour'
'Indeed, he [Isa] will be a sign/knowledge of the Hour ('ilmun lis-sa'ah), so be not in doubt of it'
'He will judge between angels and jinn'
'He will build a barrier like Dhul-Qarnayn'
explanationEn: Surah Az-Zukhruf 43:61 states regarding Isa: 'And indeed, he will be [a sign for] knowledge of the Hour, so be not in doubt of it, and follow Me. This is a straight path.'

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Anbiya, for what universal purpose did Allah send Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: Not except as a mercy to the worlds (rahmatan lil-'alamin)
Only to the residents of Makkah and Madinah
Solely to restore the kingdom of Sulayman
Only as a warner to the Quraysh tribe
explanationEn: Surah Al-Anbiya 21:107 declares: 'And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ahzab, what final prophetic title does Allah confer upon Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: Rasul Bani Isra'il
The First of the Messengers
The Judge of the Sacred Months
The Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets (Khatam an-Nabiyyin)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ahzab 33:40 affirms: 'Muhammad is not the father of [any] one of your men, but [he is] the Messenger of Allah and last/seal of the prophets (Khatam an-Nabiyyin).'

questionEn: How does Allah describe the moral character of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Surah Al-Qalam?
optionsEn: 'You are the richest merchant of Makkah'
'You are the bravest knight in Arabia'
'And indeed, you are of a great moral character (la-'ala khuluqin 'azim)'
'You are the most poetic speaker of Quraysh'
explanationEn: Surah Al-Qalam 68:4 testifies: 'And indeed, you are of a great moral character.'

questionEn: In Surah At-Tawbah, which episode from the Hijrah is recounted where the Prophet ﷺ comforted his companion by saying: 'Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us'?
optionsEn: During the Battle of Badr
When they were two in the Cave (of Thawr)
At the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
When they reached the outskirts of Quba
explanationEn: Surah At-Tawbah 9:40 describes when the disbelievers drove him out, 'the second of two, when they were in the cave and he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us."'

questionEn: Between which two sacred mosques did Allah take His servant Muhammad ﷺ by night in Surah Al-Isra?
optionsEn: From Al-Masjid al-Haram (Makkah) to Al-Masjid al-Aqsa (Jerusalem)
From Al-Masjid al-Haram to Masjid al-Nabawi
From Al-Masjid al-Aqsa to Damascus
From Masjid Quba to Mount Tur
explanationEn: Surah Al-Isra 17:1 begins: 'Exalted is He who took His Servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs.'

questionEn: In Surah An-Najm, near which heavenly landmark did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ see Jibril (AS) in his true form a second time during the Mi'raj?
optionsEn: Beneath the Mountain of Light
Above the Throne's right pillar
At the Gate of Al-Kawthar
Beside the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha)
explanationEn: Surah An-Najm 53:13-16 recounts: 'And he certainly saw him in another descent at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha) — near it is the Garden of Refuge.'

questionEn: According to Surah Ali 'Imran, how many angels did the Prophet ﷺ ask if it would suffice for Allah to reinforce the believers with at Badr (with an added promise if patient and God-fearing)?
optionsEn: Three thousand angels sent down, and up to five thousand marked angels if they remained patient and conscious of Allah
Ten thousand angels from the seventh heaven
Five hundred angels, then one thousand
Seven thousand angels on white horses
explanationEn: Surah Ali 'Imran 3:124-125 records the Prophet encouraging the believers with reinforcement of three thousand angels, and Allah promising five thousand marked angels if they remained patient and pious when the enemy rushed upon them.

questionEn: In Surah At-Tawbah, which battle is explicitly named as the occasion when the Muslims were initially amazed by their large numbers, only to flee before Allah sent down tranquility and unseen forces?
optionsEn: The Day of Hunayn
The Battle of Uhud
The Battle of Mu'tah
The Battle of Tabuk
explanationEn: Surah At-Tawbah 9:25 recalls: 'And on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth was confining for you with its vastness; then you turned back, fleeing.'

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Ahzab, what two unseen means did Allah send against the confederate armies besieging Madinah in the Battle of the Trench?
optionsEn: Darkness and thunderbolts
Floods and hailstorms
A wind (rihan) and forces/angels they did not see
Earthquakes and locusts
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ahzab 33:9 reminds believers of Allah's favor when armies came against them: 'and We sent upon them a wind and armies [of angels] you did not see.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Fath, where were the believers when they gave the Pledge of Allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ with which Allah declared Himself pleased?
optionsEn: Atop Mount Safa
Under the Tree (at Hudaybiyyah — Bay'at ar-Ridwan)
Beside the Well of Badr
Inside Masjid al-Nabawi
explanationEn: Surah Al-Fath 48:18 declares: 'Certainly was Allah pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you, [O Muhammad], under the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with an imminent conquest.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah, why did Allah turn the Qiblah of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ toward Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: Because the Jews of Madinah requested a change
In response to seeing the turning of his face toward the heaven, granting him a direction he would be pleased with
Because the companions disagreed about sunrise
Because Jerusalem was destroyed in an earthquake
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:144 states: 'We have certainly seen the turning of your face, [O Muhammad], toward the heaven, and We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram.'

questionEn: In Surah 'Abasa, over what gentle interaction did Allah admonish the Prophet ﷺ to teach the primacy of the sincere seeker regardless of social rank?
optionsEn: Frowning and turning away when a blind man ('Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum) came seeking purification while the Prophet was addressing Quraysh leaders
Allowing travelers to pray seated
Speaking softly to a hypocrite during Friday prayer
Delaying the distribution of charity after Badr
explanationEn: Surah 'Abasa 80:1-10 gently corrects the Prophet ﷺ for turning away from the blind seeker who came striving with fear of Allah while giving attention to the wealthy arrogant leaders.

questionEn: In Surah Ad-Duha, what three past favors does Allah remind Prophet Muhammad ﷺ of as reassurance that He had not forsaken him?
optionsEn: Making him king of Makkah, Ta'if, and Yemen
Teaching him Hebrew, Syriac, and Arabic
Giving him camels, horses, and olive groves
Finding him an orphan and sheltering him, finding him unaware/seeking guidance and guiding him, and finding him poor and enriching him
explanationEn: Surah Ad-Duha 93:6-8 asks: 'Did He not find you an orphan and give [you] refuge? And He found you lost [unaware of revelation] and guided [you], and He found you poor and made [you] self-sufficient.'

questionEn: In Surah Ali 'Imran, what vow did the mother of Maryam (AS) make while pregnant with her?
optionsEn: To travel to Makkah every year
To dedicate what was in her womb exclusively to the service of Allah's sanctuary (muharraran)
To donate all her jewelry to the poor
To name her child Zakariyya
explanationEn: The wife of 'Imran prayed: 'My Lord, indeed I have pledged to You what is in my womb, consecrated [for Your service], so accept this from me.'

questionEn: In Surah Maryam, when Maryam (AS) suffered labor pains beside the trunk of a date-palm tree, what miraculous sustenance was provided for her?
optionsEn: Warm milk from a mountain spring
A basket of figs brought by Zakariyya
A flowing rivulet beneath her and fresh ripe dates falling when she shook the palm trunk
Manna and quail descending from the clouds
explanationEn: She was comforted from below: 'Do not grieve; your Lord has provided beneath you a stream. And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Qasas, what words did Pharaoh's wife (Asiyah) speak to persuade Pharaoh not to kill infant Musa (AS) when they pulled him from the river?
optionsEn: '[He will be] a comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son'
'Kill him after he grows older'
'He is the son of an Egyptian noble'
'Send him back down the river tomorrow'
explanationEn: Pharaoh's wife said: 'A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Kill him not; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son.'

questionEn: What famous supplication of Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh, is held up as an example for all believers in Surah At-Tahrim?
optionsEn: 'My Lord, return Musa to his mother tonight'
'My Lord, strike Pharaoh's palace with fire'
'My Lord, hide my faith from the court guards'
'My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds and save me from the wrongdoing people'
explanationEn: Surah At-Tahrim 66:11 presents Pharaoh's wife as an example for those who believe when she prayed: 'Rabbi ibni li 'indaka baytan fil-jannah wa najjini min Fir'awna wa 'amalihi wa najjini minal-qawmiz-zalimin.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Kahf, what miraculous incident marked the exact place where Musa (AS) and his young attendant found the righteous servant (Khidr)?
optionsEn: A white dove landed on a rock
Three palm trees bowed toward the shore
A spring of honey bubbled out of the sand
Their salted fish miraculously took its way back into the sea (as if through a tunnel), which the boy forgot to mention at the rock
explanationEn: At the junction of the two seas, they forgot their fish, which made its way into the sea miraculously; realizing that was the very place they sought, they retraced their footsteps and found a servant of Allah endowed with mercy and knowledge from Him.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Kahf, why did the righteous servant (Khidr) bore a hole in the poor people's ship that had carried them free of charge?
optionsEn: To prevent Musa from returning to Egypt
To punish the sailors for refusing to pay zakah
Because the wood was rotten and needed replacing
Because behind them was a king seizing every sound/undamaged ship by force
explanationEn: Khidr explained: 'As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working at sea. So I intended to cause defect in it as there was after them a king who seized every [good] ship by force.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Kahf, why did the righteous servant (Khidr) rebuild a collapsing wall in a town whose people had refused them hospitality?
optionsEn: Because beneath the wall lay a buried treasure belonging to two orphan boys in the city whose father had been righteous
Because the wall protected the town's mosque
Because the town governor ordered him to repair it
To earn silver coins for food
explanationEn: Khidr explained: 'And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and there was beneath it a treasure for them, and their father had been righteous. So your Lord intended that they reach maturity and extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord.'

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Kahf, what materials did Dhul-Qarnayn use to build the massive barrier holding back Ya'juj and Ma'juj?
optionsEn: Granite blocks and tar
Baked clay bricks and sea salt
Sheets/blocks of iron (zubar al-hadid) until leveled between two cliffs, then heated with bellows and covered with molten copper (qitran)
Timber beams plated with silver
explanationEn: Dhul-Qarnayn requested blocks of iron until he filled the gap between the two mountain sides, blew upon it until it became like fire, and then poured molten copper over it.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Kahf, after completing the mighty barrier against Ya'juj and Ma'juj, to whom did Dhul-Qarnayn credit the achievement?
optionsEn: To the strength of the mountain tribe
To his own military engineering
To the skilled artisans of his empire
To the mercy of his Lord, adding that when His Lord's promise comes, He will make it level
explanationEn: Dhul-Qarnayn humbly declared: 'This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level, and ever is the promise of my Lord true.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Kahf, how did Dhul-Qarnayn say he would judge the people he found near the setting place of the sun?
optionsEn: Banish everyone beyond the mountains
Leave them without any laws or guidance
Enforce tribute on all inhabitants equally
Punish whoever does wrong before his Lord returns him to a terrible punishment, and speak gently and reward whoever believes and does righteousness
explanationEn: Given authority, Dhul-Qarnayn declared balanced justice: punishing the wrongdoer while showing kindness and ease to the righteous believer.

questionEn: In Surah Luqman, what unflattering comparison did Luqman use when advising his son to lower his voice?
optionsEn: 'Like thunder frightening sheep'
'Like crows fighting over grain'
'Indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys (lasawtul-hamir)'
'Like iron scraping stone'
explanationEn: Luqman advised: 'And be moderate in your pace and lower your voice; indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Kahf, what animal accompanied the Youths of the Cave (Ashab al-Kahf) at the cave's entrance?
optionsEn: A lion guarding the path
A white mare tied to an olive tree
Their dog stretching out its two forelegs at the threshold (basitun dhira'ayhi bil-wasid)
A falcon perched on a rock
explanationEn: Surah Al-Kahf 18:18 describes the sleeping youths being turned right and left while 'their dog stretching his forelegs at the entrance.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Kahf, why did the People of the Cave warn their companion sent to the city with silver coins to act gently and be careful?
optionsEn: Lest the coins turn to dust in sunlight
Lest the idolatrous townsfolk discover them and stone them or force them back into their religion
Lest he spend too long chatting in the market
Lest merchants cheat him out of the silver's value
explanationEn: They told him to bring the purest food politely and let no one know about them: 'Indeed, if they come to know of you, they will stone you or return you to their religion. And never would you succeed, then — ever.'

questionEn: Which two Prophets uttered the supplication 'Rabbana taqabbal minna innaka Antas-Sami'ul-'Alim' while raising the foundations of the Ka'bah?
optionsEn: Ibrahim and Ishaq
Dawud and Sulayman
Ibrahim and Isma'il
Musa and Harun
explanationEn: While raising the foundations of the Sacred House in Makkah, Ibrahim and his son Isma'il prayed for Allah to accept their deed, affirming that He is All-Hearing and All-Knowing.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah 2:128, after asking Allah to make them and their descendants a Muslim nation, what did Ibrahim and Isma'il specifically ask Allah to show them?
optionsEn: The exact hour of the Day of Judgment
The boundaries of Jerusalem
Their rites of worship and pilgrimage (manasik)
The treasures of the earth
explanationEn: They prayed: 'And show us our rites (wa arina manasikana) and accept our repentance,' establishing the spiritual and ritual foundations of pilgrimage.

questionEn: Which comprehensive Qur'anic supplication did Anas ibn Malik (RA) report was the most frequent du'a of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)?
optionsEn: Rabbana la tuzigh qulubana ba'da idh hadaytana
Rabbi zidni 'ilma
Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhaban-nar
Rabbana zalamna anfusana wa in lam taghfir lana
explanationEn: This supplication in Surah Al-Baqarah asks Allah for good in this world, good in the Hereafter, and protection from the punishment of the Fire.

questionEn: Who recited the supplication 'Rabbana afrigh 'alayna sabran wa thabbit aqdamana wansurna 'alal-qawmil-kafirin' when confronting an overwhelmingly larger army?
optionsEn: Talut's faithful soldiers facing Jalut (Goliath)
The companions of Kahf inside the cave
Musa and Bani Isra'il at the Red Sea
The people of Lut before leaving Sodom
explanationEn: When the steadfast believers under King Talut came into view of Jalut and his forces, they asked Allah to pour patience upon them, make their feet firm, and grant them victory.

questionEn: In the closing verse of Surah Al-Baqarah (2:286), what do believers ask Allah NOT to hold them accountable for?
optionsEn: Traveling during the sacred months
Speaking softly during night prayers
Forgetting or making an unintentional error (in nasina aw akhta'na)
Engaging in lawful commerce during pilgrimage
explanationEn: Believers pray: 'Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred,' and authentic Hadith confirms Allah responded 'I have done so.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-'Imran 3:8, who makes the supplication 'Rabbana la tuzigh qulubana ba'da idh hadaytana' ('Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us')?
optionsEn: The People of the Heights (Ashab al-A'raf)
Those firmly grounded in knowledge (ar-rasikhuna fil-'ilm)
The angels who bear the Throne
The disbelievers upon seeing the Fire
explanationEn: Those firmly grounded in knowledge acknowledge Allah's revealed Book completely and beseech Him to keep their hearts steadfast upon guidance and bestow mercy.

questionEn: Which group in Surah Al-'Imran 3:53 made the du'a 'Rabbana amanna bima anzalta wattaba'nar-rasula faktubna ma'ash-shahidin'?
optionsEn: The elders of Madyan
The Muhajirun of Makkah
The disciples (Al-Hawariyyun) of Prophet 'Isa
The magicians of Pharaoh
explanationEn: When 'Isa asked who would be his helpers for Allah, his disciples affirmed their faith and asked Allah to record them among the witnesses.

questionEn: Alongside forgiveness of sins, what specific fault did the godly companions (ribbiyyun) of earlier prophets ask forgiveness for in Surah Al-'Imran 3:147?
optionsEn: Excess or immoderation in their affairs (wa israfana fi amrina)
Delaying their departure for Hajj
Sleeping through the night
Eating from forbidden livestock
explanationEn: Even while fighting patiently in Allah's path, they humbly asked forgiveness for their sins and any excess in their conduct, asking for firm footing and victory.

questionEn: When told that hostile forces had gathered against them, what concise phrase of reliance did the believers say in Surah Al-'Imran 3:173 that increased them in faith?
optionsEn: Bismillahil-ladhi la yadurru ma'asmihi shay'
La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal-wakil
Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un
explanationEn: Saying 'Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs' increased their faith and resulted in them returning with Allah's favor and no harm touching them.

questionEn: What do the 'people of understanding' (Ulul-Albab) declare in their supplication after reflecting on the creation of the heavens and the earth in Surah Al-'Imran 3:191?
optionsEn: Our Lord, hasten for us the Day of Reckoning
Our Lord, reveal to us the unseen treasures
Our Lord, grant us dominion over the stars
Our Lord, You did not create this aimlessly (ma khalaqta hadha batila)
explanationEn: Remembering Allah standing, sitting, and lying on their sides, they reflect on creation and exclaim that Allah did not create it in vain, seeking refuge from Hellfire.

questionEn: In Surah Al-'Imran 3:193, what do the believers say they heard that moved them to believe and pray for forgiveness?
optionsEn: The trumpet of Israfil
The thunder of the clouds
A caller calling to faith (munadiyan yunadi lil-iman)
The voices of the angels descending at Badr
explanationEn: They pray: 'Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, [saying], Believe in your Lord, and we have believed.'

questionEn: Which two figures offered the repentant prayer 'Rabbana zalamna anfusana wa in lam taghfir lana wa tarhamna lanakunanna minal-khasirin'?
optionsEn: Nuh and his son
Dawud and Sulayman
Yunus and his people
Adam and his wife (Hawwa)
explanationEn: After eating from the forbidden tree, Adam and his wife immediately confessed their wrong against their own souls and begged Allah for forgiveness and mercy.

questionEn: Who utters the supplication 'Rabbana la taj'alna ma'al-qawmiz-zalimin' ('Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people') upon looking toward the inhabitants of Hellfire?
optionsEn: The companions of Al-A'raf (the Heights)
The angels guarding Paradise
The People of the Ditch
The followers of Shu'ayb
explanationEn: The people standing upon Al-A'raf (the elevated barrier between Paradise and Hell) say this prayer when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire.

questionEn: Which Prophet prayed 'Rabbana-ftah baynana wa bayna qawmina bil-haqqi wa Anta khayrul-fatihin' ('Decide between us and our people in truth')?
optionsEn: Prophet Salih
Prophet Shu'ayb
Prophet Hud
Prophet Ilyas
explanationEn: When the arrogant leaders of Madyan threatened to expel Shu'ayb and the believers unless they returned to their religion, Shu'ayb placed his trust in Allah and made this prayer.

questionEn: Who prayed 'Rabbana afrigh 'alayna sabran wa tawaffana muslimin' ('Pour upon us patience and let us die as Muslims') immediately after embracing faith despite threats of crucifixion?
optionsEn: The Believer of Ya-Sin
Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh
The Youths of the Cave
Pharaoh's magicians after witnessing Musa's miracle
explanationEn: When Pharaoh threatened to cut off their hands and feet and crucify them, the newly believing magicians turned to Allah in this steadfast prayer.

questionEn: After returning from Mount Tur and witnessing the worship of the Golden Calf, what did Prophet Musa pray for himself and his brother Harun in Surah Al-A'raf 7:151?
optionsEn: Destruction of Mount Sinai
A new scripture written on silver
Forgiveness for both of them and entry into Allah's mercy
Immediate removal of prophethood from Bani Isra'il
explanationEn: Once his anger subsided, Musa prayed: 'My Lord, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy, for You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.'

questionEn: In Surah Yunus 10:85-86, what did Musa's oppressed followers pray not to be made for the wrongdoing people?
optionsEn: Captives in Babylon
Builders of monuments
A trial/temptation (fitnatan lil-qawmiz-zalimin)
Tax collectors
explanationEn: Trusting in Allah under Pharaoh's tyranny, they prayed not to be made a trial for the wrongdoers—meaning they not be overpowered in a way that misleads oppressors—and asked for deliverance.

questionEn: What did Prophet Nuh pray in Surah Hud 11:47 immediately after Allah clarified that his drowned son was not of his righteous household?
optionsEn: To descend onto Mount Arafat
Refuge in Allah from asking about what he had no knowledge of
To bring his son back to life
To rebuild the Ark for another voyage
explanationEn: Nuh humbly repented and said: 'My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You that of which I have no knowledge. And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers.'

questionEn: In Surah Yusuf 12:33, facing relentless temptation in Egypt, what did Prophet Yusuf pray was dearer to him than what the women were inviting him to?
optionsEn: Imprisonment (As-sijnu ahabbu ilayya)
Exile to Madyan
Silence for forty years
Manual labor in the fields
explanationEn: Yusuf turned to Allah saying prison was dearer to him than sin, and asked Allah to divert their plot from him lest he incline toward them.

questionEn: After being granted authority in Egypt and reunited with his parents and brothers, what spiritual ending did Prophet Yusuf ask for in Surah Yusuf 12:101?
optionsEn: To be buried beneath the Nile
To conquer the land of Rome
To remain ruler of Egypt for a thousand years
To die as a Muslim and be joined with the righteous
explanationEn: Even at the pinnacle of worldly honor, Yusuf praised Allah and prayed: 'Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.'

questionEn: In Surah Ibrahim 14:35, while praying for the security of Makkah, what sin did Prophet Ibrahim ask Allah to keep him and his sons away from?
optionsEn: Eating from hunted animals
Worshipping idols (an na'budal-asnam)
Charging interest in trade
Forgetting the Hebrew language
explanationEn: Ibrahim prayed: 'My Lord, make this city [Makkah] secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols,' acknowledging how many people idols have led astray.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Ibrahim state in Surah Ibrahim 14:37 that he settled part of his offspring in 'an uncultivated valley' (bi-wadin ghayri dhi zar') near Allah's Sacred House?
optionsEn: To isolate them permanently from all visitors
So that they may establish prayer (li-yuqimus-salah)
To mine gold from the surrounding hills
To hide them from the army of Nimrod
explanationEn: Ibrahim explicitly prayed that they establish prayer there, that Allah make people's hearts incline toward them, and provide them with fruits so they might be grateful.

questionEn: Which two acts of worship/supplication did Prophet Ibrahim ask Allah to grant him and his offspring in Surah Ibrahim 14:40?
optionsEn: Nightly fasting and lifelong seclusion
Ruling kingdoms and commanding the wind
Memorizing the Psalms and building bridges
Being an establisher of prayer and having his supplication accepted
explanationEn: Ibrahim prayed: 'My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [many] from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.'

questionEn: Whom did Prophet Ibrahim include alongside himself and his parents in the prayer for forgiveness in Surah Ibrahim 14:41?
optionsEn: The kings of ancient Mesopotamia
All the believers on the Day the account is established
Only his direct sons
Only the residents of Makkah
explanationEn: He prayed: 'Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers the Day the account is established.'

questionEn: What reason is attached to the Qur'anic prayer for one's parents, 'Rabbirhamhuma...' in Surah Al-Isra 17:24?
optionsEn: As they raised me when I was small (kama rabbayani saghira)
Because they built a house for me
As they taught me calligraphy
Because they paid one's debts
explanationEn: Lowering the wing of humility out of mercy to parents, a believer asks Allah to have mercy upon them just as they nurtured and cared for them in childhood.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra 17:80, what did Allah instruct the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to ask for regarding his 'entry' and 'exit' (often linked by scholars to the Hijrah)?
optionsEn: Secret entry and rapid exit
An entry of truth and an exit of truth, plus a supporting authority
Wealthy entry and quiet exit
Entry into Rome and exit from Persia
explanationEn: He was commanded to pray: 'My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and to exit a sound exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.'

questionEn: Upon fleeing their polytheistic people and taking refuge in the cave, what did the Youths of the Cave (Ashab al-Kahf) pray for in Surah Al-Kahf 18:10?
optionsEn: Mercy from Allah and right guidance in their affair (rashada)
An army of angels to conquer the city
Immortality in this world
A spring of milk inside the mountain
explanationEn: They prayed: 'Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance.'

questionEn: In Surah Maryam 19:4-6, what physical signs of aging did Prophet Zakariyya mention when privately calling upon his Lord for a righteous heir?
optionsEn: His voice had grown hoarse from preaching
He could no longer walk up Mount Safa
His bones had weakened and his head glistened with gray hair
His eyesight had vanished and his hands trembled
explanationEn: Zakariyya humbly said: 'My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened, and my head has filled with white,' yet affirmed he had never been unblessed in calling upon Allah.

questionEn: When Allah commanded Prophet Musa to go to Pharaoh, what did Musa ask Allah to untie in Surah Ta-Ha 20:27?
optionsEn: The chains around his ankles
The knot from his tongue (wahlul 'uqdatan min lisani)
The waters of the Euphrates
The gates of Pharaoh's palace
explanationEn: Musa prayed: 'My Lord, expand for me my breast, ease for me my task, and untie the knot from my tongue that they may understand my speech.'

questionEn: In Surah Ta-Ha 20:114, what is the only thing Allah explicitly commanded the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to ask Him to increase?
optionsEn: His material wealth
The size of his cavalry
His years of life
Knowledge ('Rabbi zidni 'ilma')
explanationEn: Allah instructed His Messenger not to hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation was completed, and instead to pray: 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge.'

questionEn: From inside the layers of darkness (night, sea, and belly of the great fish), what three elements formed the du'a of Prophet Yunus (Dhun-Nun)?
optionsEn: Tawhid ('There is no deity except You'), glorification ('Exalted are You'), and confession ('Indeed I was of the wrongdoers')
Asking for dry land, asking for shade, and asking for fish
Praising his people, cursing the sailors, and requesting rain
Reciting the Torah, asking for a ship, and seeking wealth
explanationEn: Yunus called out: 'La ilaha illa Anta subhanaka inni kuntu minaz-zalimin,' combining pure monotheism, glorifying Allah above fault, and humble repentance.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anbiya 21:89, which beautiful attribute of Allah did Prophet Zakariyya invoke when asking not to be left childless ('fardan')?
optionsEn: Ash-Shadid (The Severe)
Al-Muntaqim (The Avenger)
Khayr al-Warithin (The Best of Inheritors)
Al-Jabbar (The Compeller)
explanationEn: Zakariyya prayed: 'My Lord, do not leave me alone [without an heir], while You are the best of inheritors,' and Allah answered by granting him Yahya.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:97-98, what specific harm from the devils (shayatin) is the believer taught to seek refuge from?
optionsEn: Their incitements/whisperings (hamazat) and their presence around one
Their physical shadows
Their speech in ancient languages
Their visible armies
explanationEn: The Qur'an teaches: 'Say, My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils, and I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they be present with me.'

questionEn: Which two attributes of Allah are paired in the concluding du'a of Surah Al-Mu'minun (23:118): 'Wa qul Rabbighfir warham wa Anta...'?
optionsEn: The Swift in Account
The Owner of Sovereignty
The Best of the Merciful (Khayrur-Rahimin)
The Creator of the Heavens
explanationEn: Surah Al-Mu'minun ends by instructing the Prophet and believers to pray: 'My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of the merciful.'

questionEn: In Surah Al-Furqan 25:65, why do the 'Servants of the Most Merciful' ('Ibad ar-Rahman) pray for Allah to avert the punishment of Hell from them?
optionsEn: Because its punishment is ever-adhering / inescapable torment (gharama)
Because they saw the angel Malik in a dream
Because they fear losing their earthly houses
Because they think no believer will enter Paradise
explanationEn: They pray: 'Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell. Indeed, its punishment is ever-adhering (inseparable and devastating); indeed it is evil as a settlement and residence.'

questionEn: What dual blessing regarding family and community do 'Ibad ar-Rahman ask for in Surah Al-Furqan 25:74?
optionsEn: Freedom from travel and exemption from charity
Long life until the end of time
Spouses and offspring who are the comfort of their eyes, and to be made leaders for the righteous
Large palaces and fertile orchards
explanationEn: They pray: 'Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us an example (imama) for the righteous.'

questionEn: In Prophet Ibrahim's extended supplication in Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:83-85, what does 'waj'al li lisana sidqin fil-akhirin' mean?
optionsEn: Make my tomb a marble monument
Grant me fluency in every foreign tongue
Grant me an honorable, truthful mention among later generations
Give me a written scroll from heaven
explanationEn: Ibrahim asked Allah to leave a good, truthful reputation and remembrance for him among all generations to come—fulfilled as Jews, Christians, and Muslims all honor him.

questionEn: In Surah An-Naml 27:19, immediately after smiling with amusement at the speech of the ant, what did Prophet Sulayman pray to Allah?
optionsEn: To inspire him to be grateful for His favors upon him and his parents, and do righteous deeds pleasing to Him
To enlarge his army of birds
To silence the insects of the valley
To build a marble dam over the valley
explanationEn: Rather than feeling pride at understanding animal speech, Sulayman immediately asked Allah to inspire him to gratitude and righteous action.

questionEn: What did Prophet Musa immediately pray in Surah Al-Qasas 28:16 after unintentionally killing an Egyptian man while defending an Israelite?
optionsEn: 'My Lord, punish the ruler of Egypt today'
'My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me'
'My Lord, hide my footprints in the sand'
'My Lord, make me invisible to the guards'
explanationEn: Musa recognized it as the work of Satan, immediately repented saying 'Rabbi inni zalamtu nafsi faghfir li,' and Allah forgave him.

questionEn: After helping two women water their flock in Madyan and retreating into the shade, what humble du'a did Prophet Musa make in Surah Al-Qasas 28:24?
optionsEn: 'My Lord, grant me a swift horse'
'My Lord, return me to the palace of Egypt'
'My Lord, send rain upon these desert wells'
'My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in dire need'
explanationEn: Hungry, exhausted, and a stranger in a foreign land, Musa said: 'Rabbi inni lima anzalta ilayya min khayrin faqir,' and Allah soon provided him shelter, work, and family.

questionEn: In Surah As-Saffat 37:100, what did Prophet Ibrahim pray when asking Allah for a child, and how did Allah describe the son promised in response?
optionsEn: He asked for one of the righteous ('minas-salihin'), and was given glad tidings of a forbearing boy ('ghulamin halim')
He asked for a warrior, and was promised a king
He asked for twin sons, and was promised triplets
He asked for a scribe, and was promised a poet
explanationEn: Ibrahim prayed 'Rabbi hab li minas-salihin,' and Allah gave him the glad tidings of a gentle, forbearing son (Isma'il), who later willingly submitted to Allah's command.

questionEn: What unique kingdom did Prophet Sulayman ask Allah for in Surah Sad 38:35 after seeking forgiveness?
optionsEn: A kingdom stretching only over Syria
A kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after him
A kingdom hidden beneath the sea
A kingdom lasting until the Day of Resurrection
explanationEn: Sulayman prayed: 'My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me,' whereupon Allah subjected the wind and jinn to him.
