explanationEn: Rejecting pagan blood-sprinkling rituals, the Qur'an reminds pilgrims that Allah wants no physical offering for Himself—what ascends to Him is sincere devotion and gratitude.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Qasas 28:57 and Surah Al-'Ankabut 29:67, what blessing unique to Makkah did Allah remind its people of to inspire gratitude and faith?
optionsEn: Navigable rivers flowing into the Red Sea
Gold mines beneath Arafat
Snow-capped peaks cooling the city all summer
Establishing Makkah as a safe, inviolable sanctuary (Haraman aminan) to which fruits of all kinds flow while people around them were snatched away
explanationEn: Surrounded by tribal raids and insecurity across Arabia, Makkah enjoyed divine protection and abundant imports precisely because of Allah's Sacred House.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Fath 48:25, during the year of Hudaybiyyah when Muslims were prevented from reaching the Sacred Mosque, why did Allah hold back fighting in the valley of Makkah?
optionsEn: Because the Muslims forgot their weapons in Madinah
Because Quraysh had already evacuated the city
To protect believing men and women living unrecognized in Makkah whom the Muslims might have unknowingly harmed
Because it was raining too heavily to march
explanationEn: Allah restrained both sides' hands out of mercy for hidden believers inside Makkah, turning the apparent setback of Hudaybiyyah into a 'Clear Victory.'

questionEn: What true vision of the Prophet (peace be upon him) did Allah confirm in Surah Al-Fath 48:27—fulfilled the following year during 'Umrat al-Qada?
optionsEn: That the Ka'bah would be moved to Madinah
That Roman ships would dock at Jeddah
That believers would surely enter Al-Masjid al-Haram safely, with heads shaved and hair shortened, without fear
That pilgrims would stop shaving their heads after Umrah
explanationEn: Though deferred by one year under the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, Allah fulfilled His Messenger's dream exactly as shown, teaching believers patience and trust in Allah's timing.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Fil (105:1-5), how did Allah defend the Sacred House when the Companions of the Elephant (Abraha's army) marched to destroy it?
optionsEn: By freezing their camels in a snowstorm
By flooding the Red Sea across the desert
By blinding them with dense fog for forty days
By sending flocks of birds (tayran ababil) pelting them with stones of baked clay (hijaratin min sijjil), leaving them like chewed straw
explanationEn: Even before the Prophet's mission began—in the very year of his birth—Allah miraculously protected the Ka'bah, showing Quraysh His sovereignty over the Sanctuary.

questionEn: In Surah Quraysh (106:1-4), what two seasonal trade journeys did Allah protect for Quraysh, and what obligation did He call them to in return?
optionsEn: Spring and autumn voyages to India; building watchtowers
Eastward and westward sea expeditions; paying annual tribute
The winter journey (to Yemen) and summer journey (to Sham); worshipping the Lord of this House who fed them from hunger and secured them from fear
Night caravans to Egypt; carving idols of marble
explanationEn: Enjoying safe passage across Arabia solely due to being custodians of the Sacred House, Quraysh were reminded to worship the Lord of the Ka'bah alone in gratitude.

questionEn: In Surah At-Tawbah 9:17-18, who alone is truly worthy to maintain and frequent the mosques of Allah (ya'muru masajidAllah)?
optionsEn: Tribal chiefs regardless of their beliefs
Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish prayer, give Zakah, and fear none except Allah
Those who decorate walls with gold leaf
Only wealthy stone masons
explanationEn: True stewardship of Allah's mosques—beginning with Al-Masjid al-Haram—belongs to sincere worshippers grounded in Tawhid, prayer, charity, and reverence for Allah alone.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Anfal 8:34-35, what did the Makkan polytheists substitute for genuine worship at the Sacred House before Islam?
optionsEn: Their 'prayer' at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping (muka'an wa tasdiyah), while barring true believers
Continuous silent study of the Psalms
Fasting every day of the sacred months
Daily distribution of all their wealth to orphans
explanationEn: Allah declared they were not the true guardians (awliya') of Al-Masjid al-Haram; its true guardians are only the God-conscious (al-muttaqun).

questionEn: In Surah Al-Hajj 22:30, what spiritual promise is attached to honoring Allah's sacred ordinances/sanctities (hurumatillah)?
optionsEn: Guaranteed leadership of Makkah
It is better for a person with their Lord (khayrun lahu 'inda Rabbih)
Double share in commercial caravans
Exemption from all daily prayers
explanationEn: Honoring Allah's sacred places, months, and boundaries reflects deep spiritual maturity that brings immense goodness before Allah.
